By revealing the latent dynamics of a research field and its response to interventions, research world models offer a new way to simulate and test research decisions before they are made.

papers.title: Fat base schemes and unexpected hypersurfaces of type $(d+k,d)$
papers.abstract: We study hypersurfaces of degree $d+k$ containing a prescribed zero-dimensional fat point scheme $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ and having multiplicity at least $d$ along a general codimension-two linear subspace. We associate with this interpolation problem a vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1$ whose splitting type determines the dimensions of all linear systems of type $(d+k,d)$. For a fat point of multiplicity $m$, we determine the exact number of conditions detected by this bundle and introduce the corresponding effective length. This leads to an excess formula separating the contributions of the splitting type, the part of the fat structure invisible to degree-$k$ fibrewise sections, and the Hilbert-function defect of the fixed scheme. We also prove a truncation theorem showing that multiplicities larger than $k$ contribute only a uniform twist of the bundle and, geometrically, fixed hyperplane components. Finally, we exhibit explicit planar and three-dimensional examples showing that genuinely unexpected phenomena persist for nonreduced fixed base schemes, including geometrically irreducible unexpected hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Inter-Agent Influence: Evaluating Persuasion, Deception, and Coercion in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: The deployment of AI agents in multi-agent settings enables inter-agent influence, whereby agents can strategically steer each other's behaviour towards an intended outcome. Such capabilities pose novel risks, as malicious agents could direct others towards harmful actions. In this work we investigate three such capabilities - persuasion, deception, and coercion - across five realistic evaluation environments and a variety of agents instantiated with frontier language models. We observed significant inter-agent influence capabilities; in oversight environments, all tested models shifted overseer decisions from rejection to approval through persuasion, deception, or coercion. We also observed successful influence in non-hierarchical 'peer-to-peer' settings through redirection of a peer's safety research trajectory. As multi-agent deployments become increasingly commonplace, these results point to a pressing need for work on mitigating the risks from inter-agent influence. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Cooperative-AI-Foundation/inter-agent-influence.

papers.title: CosmosAlpha: Multi-Relational Graph Search with Pareto-Guided Exploration for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining
papers.abstract: Discovering predictive alpha factors from noisy financial data is a fundamental yet challenging problem in quantitative finance. LLM-driven formulaic alpha mining offers an attractive paradigm by combining interpretable symbolic expressions with iterative generation and refinement guided by quantitative feedback. However, existing generation-centric and tree-based search strategies primarily organize factors through generation lineage, leaving structural and statistical relationships across search branches underutilized. Consequently, information remains localized along parent--child trajectories, which can confine exploration to redundant regions. Moreover, effective factor discovery must account for multiple distinct objectives that cannot be adequately captured by a single search criterion. We introduce CosmosAlpha, a graph-based LLM factor-mining framework that represents discovered factors as a multi-relational graph encoding generation lineage, expression-structure similarity, and cross-sectional exposure correlation. A Graph Flow mechanism propagates search utilities across the graph, allowing each factor to be assessed using relational evidence from nearby factors rather than in isolation. Pareto-guided selection jointly considers quality, fertility and diversity, explicitly modeling their trade-offs within a multi-objective search framework. Across CSI 300 and CSI 500, CosmosAlpha-Graph achieves the best mean rank over seven predictive and portfolio metrics and outperforms its controlled CosmosAlpha-MCTS counterpart on every reported metric, showing a consistent advantage for relational graph search in LLM-driven factor mining. The source code is available at https://github.com/wzhmtldswz/CosmosAlpha

papers.title: Wigner-Function Fingerprints of Collective Excitations in Mirror-Terminated Waveguide QED
papers.abstract: We investigate the emission profiles of singly excited collective states and propose a matched-mode witnessing protocol in a mirror-terminated waveguide quantum electrodynamics system. The amplitudes and relative phases of the initial collective excitation are encoded in the temporal mode of the emitted single-photon wavepacket, providing a route to state verification through the common waveguide output. We identify the emission mode associated with a chosen target state and employ an auxiliary virtual-cavity representation to evaluate the quantum state of this selected output mode. For a matched initial state, the selected mode contains the emitted single photon, whose Wigner function exhibits a pronounced non-classical negative dip, serving as a distinct fingerprint of the target many-body state. With the reference mode held fixed, different initial configurations yield different photon occupations and phase-space distributions, demonstrating the state selectivity of the protocol. These results connect collective-state verification with temporal-mode analysis of the emitted radiation, offering access to collective coherence with reduced reliance on qubit-resolved correlation measurements.

papers.title: Mutual-Coupling-Aware Joint Precoding and Antenna Positioning for Movable-Antenna MU-MIMO Systems
papers.abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) improve wireless communications by adapting antenna positions to the propagation environment. However, antenna movement also changes the mutual coupling (MC) among elements of the transmit and receive arrays, which affects the performance of MA-enabled systems. In this paper, we investigate MC-aware joint precoding and antenna positioning for a downlink multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system with MAs at both the base station and users. We establish an MC-aware system model by combining field-response propagation with a circuit-based representation of the transmit and receive arrays. Based on this model, we formulate a weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization problem that jointly optimizes multi-stream precoders and antenna positions. The problem is challenging because the precoders and positions are coupled through the propagation channels and position-dependent MC matrices. To address this challenge, we reformulate the problem in the antenna-current domain to to efficiently handle the MC matrices and develop a current-domain weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) framework for alternating optimization. Furthermore, we handle the nonconvex position updates within the framework by using majorization--minimization (MM) and solve the resulting convex subproblems with a dedicated conic alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design improves the WSR over both an MC-aware fixed array and a movable-array design that ignores MC during optimization.

papers.title: Strain-Glass Dynamics in the Superionic Conductor Na$_3$PS$_4$
papers.abstract: Ionic conduction in solid-state electrolytes is conventionally described by mobile cations migrating through a static host lattice. Yet the fastest conductors are often the most disordered, and how disorder enhances transport remains unresolved at the mesoscale, inaccessible to ensemble-averaged probes. We use Bragg X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy to measure nanoscale structural dynamics of a single ball-milled Na$_3$PS$_4$ particle. We find that the cubic phase behaves as a strain glass: a frustrated configuration of three degenerate tetragonal variants with short-range order. Its domain-wall motion is stress-driven, crossing over irreversibly to thermally activated dynamics on annealing as residual milling stress is depleted. Rearrangements follow scale-free avalanche statistics, matching ferroelastic martensites but without external driving. The tetragonal polymorph shows none of these features and relaxes fifty times more slowly. These dynamics occur on timescales comparable to estimated ionic diffusion across the particle, indicating the host structure cannot be assumed static on transport-relevant timescales.

papers.title: Are LLM Assistants Regulatory Ready? Answers from regenold's 2026 EU AI Act Q&A Challenge
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) assistants are increasingly proposed for regulatory affairs, yet their reliability in regulatory tasks remains unclear. We introduce the EU AI Act Q&A Benchmark, an expert-curated benchmark of 110 open-ended questions about the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). Each question comes with an exemplary answer, question-specific correctness criteria, and expected references. Evaluation measures answer correctness, reference quality, conciseness, tone, and latency, with a multi-turn ``hard mode'' testing responses to simulated user pushback. We also present the results of the 2026 EU AI Act Q&A Challenge, based on the benchmark, where three off-the-shelf baselines and five purpose-built assistants (from four commercial developers and one academic entrant) were tested. Only two of the five submitted assistants consistently outperformed the baselines; one achieved high scores across all evaluated metrics. These results show that specialist development alone does not guarantee better performance and highlight the critical importance of LLM assistant evaluation in regulatory affairs. The benchmark code is openly available at https://github.com/regenold-GmbH/eu-ai-act-benchmark-2026/.

papers.title: CANDO: Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization for Residual Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Pretrained generative policies provide strong behavior priors for robot control, but adapting them efficiently with online reinforcement learning remains difficult. A central challenge is how to improve a frozen generative policy without destroying the structure learned from offline demonstrations. Noise-space residual methods address this by modifying the policy's input noise, but existing noise-space methods typically regulate adaptation through fixed latent feasible regions, which may exclude valuable noise edits. In contrast, action-space residual methods are more sample-efficient, but their efficiency can still be further improved. We propose Conservative Noise Directional Optimization (CNDO), a noise-space residual RL method that improves a frozen generative policy by learning state- and noise-conditioned directions around Gaussian latent samples. CNDO removes predefined latent feasible regions and instead regulates noise-space adaptation through the soft conservative constraint, which consists of conservative value estimation and gated execution. We further introduce Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization (CANDO), which adds an action-space residual, combining structured latent-space improvement with local action correction. Experiments show that, once CNDO narrows the gap between noise-space and action-space residual learning, CANDO further improves over single-space optimization, achieving 76.1 NAUC and a 91.4% final success rate, surpassing the best single-space results by 6.6 NAUC and 4.1% success rate. More demos and info are available on https://cando-rl.github.io/.

papers.title: Decoy-state quantum key distribution with a leaky Mach-Zehnder receiver
papers.abstract: We prove the security of phase-encoded decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution for a Mach-Zehnder receiver with imbalanced beam splitters and two threshold detectors that leak fine-grained information about the detection patterns. For this, we derive a lower bound on Bob's single-photon contributions and combine it with the decoy-state method and a recent phase-error framework for leaky receivers. The leakage-induced correction to the phase-error rate is independent of channel loss, providing a loss-tolerant treatment of receiver leakage even in the presence of beam-splitter imbalance. Our results provide a practical route toward loss-tolerant security proofs for imperfect QKD receivers in the presence of receiver leakage.

papers.title: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
papers.abstract: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2π$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole contributions in atoms exhibiting only electric dipole transitions. This eliminates the need to simultaneously excite pure electric-dipole and magnetic-dipole responses with exactly matched radiation. We derive a two-mode model for this response and show that it accurately captures full coupled-dipole simulations near the optimal lattice spacings. Because of the wide applicability of coupled-dipole models, the relevance of our microscopic analysis extends beyond atomic physics to nanostructured metasurfaces. Moreover, the same platform also connects directly to established subradiance-protected single-photon storage protocols, suggesting a route toward combining wavefront engineering, storage, and retrieval in a simple atomic bilayer.

papers.title: BtsPruner: Role-Aware Visual Token Pruning for Large Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) often process hundreds or thousands of visual tokens, resulting in substantial computational and memory overhead during inference. Existing training-free pruning methods typically estimate token importance using language-model attention, visual attention, or feature similarity. However, these methods treat visual tokens with uniform criteria and overlook that tokens may serve different roles during visual encoding. In this work, we investigate the evolution of visual token roles in LVLMs and observe that tokens progressively transition from local detail carriers to globally referenced representatives as encoding proceeds. Based on this observation, we propose BtsPruner, a training-free role-aware visual token pruning framework that preserves complementary token roles under a fixed budget. Specifically, BtsPruner first identifies the token-role transition point based on the evolution of attention concentration. It then discovers globally referenced representatives from later encoding stages and recursively retrieves local detail tokens from earlier stages to recover complementary fine-grained evidence. Extensive experiments across LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen-VL, InternVL, and CogVLM demonstrate that BtsPruner achieves superior performance retention under aggressive token reduction. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, BtsPruner preserves 91.6% of the dense model's performance using only 32 of 576 visual tokens (5.6%). In the high-resolution LLaVA-NeXT-7B setting, it achieves up to a 5.95x CUDA-latency speedup.

papers.title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
papers.abstract: The superposition principle at the heart of optics states that electromagnetic fields do not interact in vacuum. This principle is not universal, instead electromagnetic fields couple weakly via quantum vacuum fluctuations. Striking consequences are light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence. Experimental results from colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers combined with dark-field detection and polarimetry for background suppression are reported. This approach yields the most stringent bound for light-by-light scattering in the low-energy regime achieved to date -- improving upon previous experimental limits by ten orders of magnitude -- and paves the way for precision measurements.

papers.title: Long-lived quantum memories with rare-earth ions doped in crystals
papers.abstract: Quantum memory is a core enabling device for large-scale quantum networks, serving as the fundamental building block for quantum repeaters and transportable quantum memories. Among various physical platforms, rare-earth-ion-doped crystals stand out as one of the most promising solid-state candidates for long-lived photonic quantum memories, owing to their exceptionally long spin coherence time and their compatibility with integration. In this review, we first introduce the physical mechanisms underlying long-lived spin coherence in rare-earth systems, with particular emphasis on the zero-first-order-Zeeman transition and dynamical decoupling techniques. We then review the experimental progress in this field, highlighting three distinct lifetimes--the spin coherence time, the light storage time, and the quantum storage time--and covering experiments that have achieved hour-scale spin coherence, minute- to hour-scale light storage, and minute-scale single-photon-level quantum storage. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges that hinder the realization of practical long-lived quantum memories, explore potential strategies to overcome these obstacles, and outline the prospects for their future applications in quantum networks.

papers.title: Late-time echoes from planar wave-packet scattering by an ultracompact star
papers.abstract: We simulate the propagation and scattering of an incident plane scalar wave in the spacetime of an ultracompact, horizonless constant-density star using a time-domain multipole mode-sum method. By reconstructing the coherently superposed time-domain waveforms, we compare the star's dynamical response with that of a Schwarzschild black hole. We find that the early-time response closely mimics a black-hole ringdown due to wave scattering near the exterior unstable photon sphere. Conversely, the late-time signal develops a sequence of delayed echoes originating from wave trapping near the interior stable light ring and subsequent leakage through the exterior potential barrier. While individual multipoles exhibit regular echoes, their coherent superposition induces interference, producing complex waveforms with irregular profiles that nonetheless retain an underlying temporal organization with alternating peak separations. Finally, as a proof of concept, we perform a signal-to-noise ratio analysis using an assumed strain normalization, demonstrating that these weak, late-time signatures can be resolved by third-generation gravitational-wave detectors.

papers.title: Estimating the generator of matrix exponential time-series
papers.abstract: The achievable precision in estimating the spectrum of a time-series signal that is promised to be sparse in Fourier space deteriorates rapidly as the spectral peaks get closer together, as soon as we introduce noise. Here, we study the related task of generator estimation: estimating the generator of a matrix exponential time-series and its eigenvalues. We obtain rigorous non-asymptotic precision guarantees on genESPRIT, a practical algorithm solving generator estimation, and show that this task can be solved with precision independent of the spectral spacing. The guarantees are complemented by a Cramér--Rao analysis of a relaxation of the problem. In particular, in the case of unitary data with bounded additive noise with effective entrywise variance $σ^2$, we show that genESPRIT estimates the associated propagator matrix in Frobenius norm with precision scaling as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(σNL^{-\frac12})$ in the length of the time-series $L$ and matrix dimension $N$, matching the corresponding spectrum-independent Cramér--Rao standard deviation scaling up to logarithmic factors. We prove that the matching distance error in the spectrum estimated by genESPRIT scales as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}} (σ^2 N^3 L^{-1} + σN^{\frac32} L^{-\frac32} )$, which we compare to the lower bound on the corresponding Cramér--Rao bound with the asymptotic standard deviation scaling $\mathcal{O}(σL^{-\frac32})$. These guarantees provide the first rigorous bounds on solving the generator estimation problem. As the matrix exponential time-series can be obtained from linearly independent vector time-series by concatenation, this work opens up a new direction in spectral estimation, which circumvents the problem of crowded spectra, under the additional assumption of linear independence.

papers.title: Learnings and Pitfalls from AI-Assisted A/B Experimentation at Scale
papers.abstract: A/B testing underpins product decisions by providing trustworthy, reproducible quantification of proposed changes' effects. Growing large language model (LLM) capabilities have motivated efforts to automate experimentation workflows. Yet LLMs are nondeterministic and prone to hallucination, properties that conflict with the trust experimentation systems must provide. Experiments are also operationally messy: diagnosing anomalies, debugging configurations, and conducting bespoke follow-up analyses require flexible reasoning and manual effort. These tasks let agents accelerate experimentation without replacing its deterministic statistical foundations. We report lessons from building and operating such an agent. Our central finding is that this tension is resolved not by making the model deterministic, but by bounding where its nondeterminism can reach; the model selects and sequences procedures, while deterministic code computes every quantity it reports. Three consequences surprised us: withholding information from the model improved its answers, demand concentrated on mundane retrieval rather than the autonomous decisions we anticipated, and the agent's eagerness to help threatened statistical validity.

papers.title: Motional Decoherence of the internal state of an atom by vacuum and thermal fluctuations of a quantum field: Necessity of a fully relativistic treatment
papers.abstract: We consider a massive object, such as a neutral atom or an Unruh-DeWitt detector, moving at constant speed in a quantum field and investigate how motion affects the quantum coherence of its internal degrees of freedom, manifesting as quantum dispersion in the absence of a quantum field, and decoherence in its presence. Our investigation aims to serve two purposes: One is to obtain the correct results for these effects, which are essential for the design of quantum information processing schemes where the quantum coherence of an atom's internal degrees of freedom is of major concern. The other is to expose the fallacies in commonplace approaches, which start with a non-relativistic calculation and then add on relativistic ``corrections". We first show a fully relativistic calculation of the internal dynamics based on covariance principles, and then one which ignores these principles, often justified by the atom's slow motion. By a direct comparison of results from these two approaches, we identify {significant discrepancies} in a non-relativistic treatment, even at low atomic speeds. The proper procedure, and a much safer one in terms of accuracy, is recommended here: first derive the dynamics and the necessary regularizations within a fully covariant relativistic framework. Only after the exact, internally consistent equations of motion are established should low-velocity limits be extracted from them. Only in this way can all the relativistic effects which matter: time dilation, aberration, non-inertial mass shifts, be systematically preserved, and accurate results obtained.

papers.title: Fast, Cheap, and Fair? Evaluating Decision Models
papers.abstract: Industries are increasingly adopting AI-driven systems to automate a wide range of tasks, including high-stakes decisions in human resources, such as candidate screening and recruitment. This makes evaluating their fairness essential, particularly when decisions directly affect individuals' opportunities. Accordingly, the EU AI Act classifies recruitment AI systems as high-risk, imposing strict requirements on their deployment. In this context, compact ``System~1'' decision models offer a fast and cost-efficient alternative to general-purpose LLMs, yet their fairness remains largely unexplored. This article presents the first systematic bias and fairness audit of \jev{}, a typed-decision model targeting recruitment applications. The study evaluates how explicit demographic attributes and implicit candidate cues influence screening scores, rankings, and shortlisting outcomes. These effects are compared against a noise floor derived from name substitutions and typographical variations. The evaluation also examines output validity, latency, and cost. Counterfactual CV datasets and evaluation code are released for reproducibility.

papers.title: Signals: Continuous Diagnostics of AI Agents
papers.abstract: AI agents can make incorrect decisions or waste resources even when their tools and infrastructure work normally. Their nondeterministic behavior makes these problems difficult to reproduce and diagnose. We developed Signals to identify such problems from agentic traces and suggest concrete remediations. We built the method around a taxonomy of 45 problem types across eight families, with definitions and evidence requirements for each type. The method distinguishes realized failures, risk exposures, and inefficiencies, groups related findings into engineering issues called Signals, and assesses their severity from the supporting evidence. Each Signal includes actions a developer can take and checks for evaluating the change. Further executions can add evidence to an existing Signal or reveal a new problem. We evaluated the method on public agent executions and achieved 91.43% F1 when matching Signals to reference issues, about 18 percentage points higher than a one-pass LLM control that used the same model and taxonomy.

papers.title: Regge bounds and eikonal scaling in a four-dimensional scalar EFT
papers.abstract: Positivity bounds rest on twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which assume that the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partialφ)^4/Λ^4$ and $g_6(\partialφ)^6/Λ^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. The same construction is applied in the forward limit required by the dispersion relation, and we use the one- and three-loop absorptive parts below the cutoff to constrain $g_4$ and $g_6$.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the Strassen CP Rank Gap and Symmetric Rank Gap of Third-Order Tensors
papers.abstract: For two third-order tensors over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, we define the Strassen CP rank gap as the sum of their CP ranks minus the CP rank of their direct sum. For arbitrary third-order tensors, we derive explicit upper bounds on this gap in terms of CP rank excess and dimension. For symmetric third-order tensors, we similarly define the Strassen symmetric rank gap using symmetric rank and establish explicit upper bounds in terms of symmetric rank excess, CP rank excess, and dimension. These bounds also yield sufficient conditions for the respective gaps to vanish, ensuring additivity of CP rank or symmetric rank under direct sums.

papers.title: Sample-Grained Approximate Unlearning with Provable Per-Sample Bounds
papers.abstract: Machine unlearning aims to erase the influence of a designated forget set from a trained model while preserving strong utility on the retain set. Approximate unlearning methods efficiently achieve this goal without full retraining, but their effectiveness is primarily assessed using dataset-level aggregate metrics. These aggregate metrics can mask deviations from retraining at the level of individual samples. In this work, we focus on per-sample unlearning effectiveness. We introduce SALA (Sample-grained Likelihoods ALignment), a plug-in optimization framework that enables approximate unlearning methods to operate at the level of individual samples by steering each example toward its correct target distribution. To quantitatively assess this behavior, we further propose the sample-grained distribution gap, a metric that captures per-sample discrepancies between approximate unlearning and exact retraining output distributions. We provide theoretical guarantees showing that SALA contracts this gap and yields a bounded per-sample discrepancy to retraining. To make this framework practical, we develop a low-cost estimation method for the member and non-member target distributions. Extensive experiments on classification and generation tasks demonstrate that SALA reduces the sample-grained distribution gap by up to $86.67\%$ when paired with existing approximate unlearning baselines, while also improving robustness to unlearning hyperparameters.

papers.title: Broken-Symmetry Reference States for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Near-DMRG Accuracy
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) accuracy remains limited for strongly correlated systems like iron-sulfur clusters. This accuracy heavily depends on the mean-field reference state, which determines the sampling ansatz and configuration-recovery target. We extend the qcsc-prefect workflow to support a broken-symmetry unrestricted Hartree-Fock (BS-UHF) starting point, derived from atom-localized antiferromagnetic initial guesses. For the $[Fe_4S_4(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$ cubane (54 electrons, 36 orbitals, 72 data qubits; 88 total qubits), this lowers the mean-field reference by $\approx 534$ mHa relative to the Restricted Hartree-Fock (RHF) solution (-327.0809 vs. -326.5474 Ha). Combined with deep multi-step configuration recovery on ROQUO GPU nodes at subspace dimension $d = 3 \times 10^{10}$, we reach $E = -327.235076$ Ha. This is 4.3 mHa above the finite-$D = 4000$ DMRG value (-327.2393952 Ha) and $\sim 512-517$ mHa below a previous same-active-space RHF-reference SQD calculation. Extrapolating to the $d \to \infty$ limit via a Gaussian-in-log $d$ fitting ansatz gives an asymptotic estimate $E_\infty = -327.244468$ Ha $\pm 1.05$ mHa, just 0.33 mHa above our discarded-weight-extrapolated DMRG estimate ($E_{D\to\infty} = -327.244797$ Ha $\pm 0.46$ mHa), well within their combined $1σ$ uncertainty. We characterize the determinant-subspace composition driving convergence, show matching validation on $[Fe_2S_2(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$, and report multi-HPC execution on Fugaku, Miyabi-G, and ROQUO. We conclude that reference-state preparation, rather than subspace size alone, is a key driver of SQD energy accuracy under strong electronic correlation.

papers.title: On the propagation of chaos for three-dimensional Coulomb Brownian particles
papers.abstract: While the mean field limit of the Brownian particles with 3D Coulomb interaction has been resolved starting from the Liouville equation, the justification directly from the random trajectories is not fully resolved. In our previous work (J. Math. Phys., 60, 111501, 2019), it has been shown that the time marginals of any limit point of the empirical measure form a weak solution to the mean field nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation. However, the identification to the strong solution is not established due to the lack of regularity. In this short note, we first make use of the variational formulation of the quadratic function to establish the desired space-time $L^2$ bound mentioned already in J. Math. Phys., 60, 111501, 2019. This fills gap and shows that the time marginals must be the must be the strong solution. Moreover, making use of the virial type estimates and the force dissipation, we also establish the propagation of chaos in path space directly from the random trajectories of the particle systems.

papers.title: Spatial Memory for AR Glasses: Hierarchical Visual Acquisition and Source-Linked Recall
papers.abstract: We present a spatial-memory system that enables optical see-through AR glasses to recall earlier physical encounters. The dual-camera prototype combines hierarchical visual acquisition with source-linked storage and staged retrieval. Quality screen-ing, global and regional appearance novelty, and temporal support select monochrome observations for detailed RGB cap-ture. Semantic observations retain links to their source images, allowing retrieval to answer indexed historical questions direct-ly or inspect visual details omitted from scene descriptions. The architecture separates capture acceptance, interpretation out-come, and support for a particular question. This distinction motivates two core control mechanisms: bounded reassessment of familiar views when earlier processing leaves an evidence gap, and retention guided by source dependencies. In a 131.35 s egocentric replay, the implemented acquisition policy selected six RGB views from 648 monitoring observations, while feature extraction ran on 97.7% of observations. These results demon-strate selective RGB acquisition and identify frequent local inference as a remaining cost. Exposure duration and cross-view timing further constrain the evidence preserved from se-lected encounters. The system provides a practical acquisition-to-recall architecture for persistent AR assistance, with explicit boundaries between captured evidence, indexed interpretations, and supported historical claims.

papers.title: Perseus: A Full-Stack System for Homomorphic Model Inference
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made it exceptionally convenient for users to send their private data to model providers, which process them in plaintext. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) promises to secure remote inference by computing directly on encrypted data, yet it has remained prohibitively slow. The effort to make it practical remains fragmented, with most existing frameworks being closed-source, which keeps progress from compounding. We present Perseus, a free and open Python software library that supports the full stack of encrypted model inference, from the cryptographic backend and data packing, to encrypted nonlinearities and end-to-end model execution. Perseus ships with built-in novel optimizations, one at each level of the stack: in-kernel regeneration of key-switching keys at the (i) backend level, a complex variant of Cachemir packing at the (ii) data level, and a state-of-the-art bootstrap placer that is both packing- and magnitude-aware at the (iii) model level. Perseus achieves state-of-the-art latency across multiple models and modalities, within $3\%$ of the plaintext models' accuracy and perplexity. Remarkably, it is $3.96\times$ faster at single-token decoding than any other implementation on Llama-3-8B. We initiate, for the first time, a public speedrun on encrypted GPT-2, so that progress can compound.

papers.title: Reconstruction-Based Diagnosis through Gödel-Regularized Virtual Observability
papers.abstract: Not every component in a technical system can be equipped with sensors. Hence, when a fault occurs, available sensors often detect it only after its effects have propagated. This makes the isolation of faults difficult. We approach this problem by introducing virtual sensors. For each combination of component and fault type, we let external knowledge describe the fault-sensitive variables. We introduce a novel neural observer that is only trained on normal data. For fault isolation, it uses available sensor measurements where it is possible and reconstructs missing variables as virtual sensors to predict normal behavior. It detects deviations between current values and nominal predictions and computes local symptoms, which are then compared by onset time. The result is a set of root causes describing the faulty behavior. We use Gödel logic to encode physical knowledge and guide training. We evaluate our approach on synthetic networks, the Tennessee Eastman Process, and datasets of two modular production plants.

papers.title: CogniLife: Continuous Cognitive Distillation for Deployed Multi-Expert Agent Marketplaces
papers.abstract: Multi-expert agent marketplaces -- where creators publish domain-specific AI experts for end users to consult -- are an emerging deployment pattern for language technology. A published expert can receive many requests yet little evidence about its creator, who remains active elsewhere: the cold-expert problem. We frame continuous cognitive distillation as converting attributed creator observations into revisable decision rules, communication patterns, and domain procedures. CogniLife proposes a cross-expert attribution design for this problem, with Creator Profiles for transferable creator patterns and Expert Journals for listing-specific knowledge; this design is not yet implemented or evaluated. A deployed platform partially realizes the surrounding lifecycle through creator-authorized authoring, capability-owned proposal filtering, and reversible consolidation of eligible owner-scoped memory. On ProfyBench-v1, an 85-task offline benchmark built from replay seeds and controlled internal tests, the Profy Full configuration as a whole achieves a mean overall score of 4.65/5 from the primary LLM judge, compared with 4.01 for Raw LLM and 4.28 for Expert Prompt, with the largest gains in completeness, specificity, and missing-information tasks. These configuration-level scores do not test cold-expert mitigation, cross-expert transfer, or longitudinal distillation.

papers.title: Structural axes of sources in the SUMSS survey and their alignments
papers.abstract: Coherent orientations of extragalactic radio sources have been reported on large angular scales, but their statistical significance and susceptibility to observational systematics remain debated. Searches based on very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) also leave the far southern sky comparatively sparsely sampled. We test for local alignments of kiloparsec-scale radio source structural axes in the Sydney University Molonglo Sky Survey (SUMSS), providing a complementary probe in the undersampled southern sky. We constructed a catalog of structural position angles for 4087 sources from 629 SUMSS mosaics. A convolutional neural network supplied initial angle estimates, which were corrected for image-to-sky coordinate distortion and visually vetted. We searched for local alignments using a coordinate-invariant parallel transport statistic on HEALPix tessellations, then refined candidate regions with a genetic algorithm. We calibrated the significance of the full search against mock skies that preserve the declination-dependent position angle distribution and undergo the same search procedure. Several regions show apparently strong local alignment, but none remains statistically significant after accounting for the look-elsewhere effect. The candidate signals are consistent with chance fluctuations in the full search. We find no statistically significant evidence for alignment of structural axes of radio sources in SUMSS images. The resulting southern sky position angle catalog provides a useful resource for future studies of radio source morphology and population properties.

papers.title: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness
papers.abstract: We propose goal-driven self-recursive optical research in which agents use physical evidence to revise the hardware, software, models, and protocols used to pursue a scientific goal. The framework can be instantiated with different stimulus systems and measurement devices. We formalize its updates and derive a relation between physical attainability, command access, and model approximation error. We demonstrate the concept in an optical see-through color-matching case study using an iPad, RayNeo X3 glasses, and a TOP 300 probe coupled to a CAS140D spectroradiometer, both from Instrument Systems. A revised glasses application adds USB-controlled RGB holds and frame acknowledgements, keeping model-generated colors displayed during spectral acquisition. The interface passes 12 live control checks. Spectral feedback reduces one target color difference from 19.756 to 1.211 ΔE_76^*; all five targets improve in a separate comparison. These measurements demonstrate the concept in one configuration. The resulting software and protocols remain available for subsequent investigations.

papers.title: A Parametric Linear Conic Projection for Structured Sparse Attention
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Cone Alignment Index (CAI), a scale-invariant sparsity measure associated with a Lorentz-cone geometry. We provide a probabilistic analysis of the distribution of the CAI score, including a general theorem and explicit corollaries for Gaussian and uniform distributions. As a consequence, we show that, in the high-sparsity regime, the probability that the samples lie within the convex cone tends to one. Building upon this formulation, we derive two complementary projections: the \emph{Parametric Linear Conic Projection} (PLCP), an efficient closed-form approximation, and the \emph{Parametric Euclidean Conic Projection} (PECP), the exact Euclidean projection onto the cone boundary. Our analysis establishes several fundamental theoretical properties. We prove that PLCP and PECP are collinear, differ only by a positive radial scaling factor, and induce exactly the same sparsity threshold, thereby preserving an identical active support. Furthermore, we derive a support-identification theorem showing that, for any prescribed sparsity level $l<n$, the number of coefficients discarded at each iteration is theoretically controlled. Building on this theoretical foundation, we develop a bilevel PLCP framework for structured matrix sparsification. The proposed method naturally generates hardware-friendly structured sparsity patterns, including row-wise, column-wise, and diagonal masks, making it particularly well suited for accelerating Transformer attention mechanisms.

papers.title: Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution
papers.abstract: Parton multiplicity entropy, proposed by Kharzeev and Levin as entanglement between the region probed in deep inelastic scattering and the proton's remainder, was compared with hadron multiplicity data. It is computed from parton densities, which do not fix the partons' quantum state. We show that a one-parton density matrix from Lipatov's wave functions determines two entropies for resolved modes with finite mean number and entropy. Its trace is the mean parton number, and normalization gives a sampled parton's entropy. A compatible thermal state, if it exists, maximizes entropy at fixed one-parton matrix. This maximum equals the actual entropy only for that thermal state and measures entanglement only for a specified subsystem of a pure state. The geometric multiplicity entropy follows if all emitted partons share one mode. An entropy computed from densities becomes such a maximum, an upper bound on the actual entropy, only for specified resolved modes. We also show that the state averaged over unrecorded emissions, assumed incoherent across scales, obeys probability-preserving Lindblad evolution on finitely many regulated modes with the resolution scale if emission and no-emission terms match. The occupations reproduce leading-order DGLAP, with virtual terms, at leading logarithmic accuracy as the cutoffs on momentum fractions are removed. The reduction holds for strongly ordered transverse momenta in light-cone gauge and dilute occupations, including those of newly resolved modes. Approximating momentum and helicity modes by independent thermal populations closes the occupation equation and gives this bound's evolution, with Bose and Pauli factors from the operator algebra. We propose testing this approximation at HERA or the LHC. The test compares the mode number inferred from normalized hadron factorial moments in a rapidity window with the window's transverse mode count.

papers.title: Soft-confinement approximation of no-flux McKean-Vlasov dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the approximation of the no-flux McKean-Vlasov equation on a bounded convex domain by a whole-space equation with quadratic confinement of strength $λ^{-1}$ outside the domain. For a smooth bounded interaction kernel and a common bounded initial density with square-integrable gradient, we establish an $O(λ^{1/4})$ approximation rate. The estimate controls the $L^2$ density error uniformly on every finite time interval and the gradient error in space-time $L^2$. Without interaction, a spectral gap independent of $λ$ yields the $O(λ^{1/4})$ rate uniformly in time for the density error and uniformly over all unit time intervals for the gradient error. With interaction, we construct a counterexample showing that even weak convergence can fail to be uniform in time.

papers.title: Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause: Anatomy of a Scientific Reasoning Failure
papers.abstract: Scientific agents can find interventions that work without understanding why they do. We study this failure mode in controlled synthetic regulatory systems, where agents must experimentally identify a hidden fault and rescue the resulting phenotype. Across seven LLMs, every model restores the healthy phenotypes more often than it identifies the fault. Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 rescue every organism while diagnosing only 55% and 35% of them. This failure is not simply due to insufficient exploration or unavailable evidence. In most cases, the cause is experimentally identifiable, and agents encounter evidence that distinguishes competing causes in 91% of relevant sessions, and still frequently misdiagnose the system. Targeted probes reveal where experimental reasoning breaks down. Models reliably interpret decisive evidence and revise hypotheses when the causal comparison is explicit, and can locate that evidence within a full experimental record. However, they struggle to predict the outcome of the experiment under each competing cause, a necessary step in using the observed result to distinguish between them. Agents can therefore gather the right evidence and still infer the wrong cause. As AI systems take on a growing role in synthesising scientific evidence, these findings highlight the need to evaluate how they use evidence to reach causal conclusions, alongside whether their interventions succeed.

papers.title: Algebraicity, Hodge Gradings, and the Geometry of Period Images
papers.abstract: We prove the algebraicity of period images in arithmetic quotients without using o-minimality. The proof uses infinitesimal neighborhoods and formal algebraization to recover the images and the maps from their algebraic sources. Hodge positivity and an algebraic ampleness criterion yield the Griffiths polarization and quasi-projectivity. For lifted images, we construct Stein neighborhoods and holomorphic matrix realizations of the Hodge filtration. On closed horizontal subspaces, we bound canonical Bergman density below by the Hodge volume form. We compare the Bergman and Griffiths--Schmid metrics near one-parameter boundaries with nontrivial unipotent monodromy and nondegenerate graded period maps, and in all directions near general one- and two-node quintic threefolds. A period surface arising from abelian threefolds shows that the upper metric comparison fails in general.

papers.title: Vertex-resummed kinetic theory of dipole-symmetric bosons from 2PI effective action
papers.abstract: The formalism of non-equilibrium dynamics for the dipole-symmetric $U(N)$ model involving $N$-component charged scalar fields is studied on the Schwinger-Keldysh contour by a systematic $1/N$ expansion of two-particle-irreducible (2PI) effective action to the next-to-leading order (NLO). The differential equations describing non-equilibrium evolution equations of two-point functions and field expectation values related to the symmetry breaking in the dynamics are derived, which encompass scatterings between modes essential in the late-time evolution and thermalization beyond the scope of the mean field. At the late-time regime of the evolution, the leading-order (LO) gradient expansion is performed to construct the vertex-resummed kinetic theory by encoding non-perturbative effects in the vertex through the resummation, which is distinct from the standard kinetic theory written by the weak-coupling expansion.

papers.title: From Watching to Steering: Enabling Human-Coding Agent Collaboration through Execution Traces
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled coding agents to autonomously perform complex software development tasks, yet their long-running execution remains difficult for users to inspect, understand, and steer. We present Vibetrace, an interactive trace visualization and intervention system for agentic programming built upon OpenCode. Vibetrace introduces a human-agent collaboration paradigm of Observe, Understand, Intervene, and Evolve. It (1) visualizes agent workflows as interactive execution traces for inspecting actions, intermediate states, and failures; (2) enables users to fork execution from prior steps and provide targeted corrections without restarting validated progress; and (3) distills traces and human feedback into reusable skills for continual agent evolution. On SWE-bench Verified, distilled skills reduce input tokens by 23.0% and cost by 15.5%, while improving pass rate from 65.0% to 68.0%. User studies further demonstrate improved accuracy and efficiency over conventional log-based interaction.

papers.title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product
papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) has attracted significant attention in the parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) landscape. However, its design suffers from two fundamental limitations. First, its invariance manifold induces flat directions in the loss landscape, creating an optimization bottleneck for adaptive optimizers. Second, its effective rank scales only linearly with the parameter budget. In this paper, we propose Scalable Morpho Adaptation (SaMA), a PEFT method grounded in a principled generalization of the Kronecker product. By relaxing the shared-block constraint in the perfect-shuffle factorization, SaMA spans from low to full rank and achieves a practical rank that scales quadratically with the parameter budget, up to full-rank. Furthermore, we show that its invariance manifold collapses to a diagonal group, making it structurally more optimizer-friendly. Empirically, SaMA consistently outperforms strong PEFT baselines on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning benchmarks while being more parameter-efficient.

papers.title: A Security Analysis of Verifiable Credential Verification Pipelines: Attack Surface Arising from JSON-LD/RDFC Canonicalization Compared with SD-JWT VC and mdoc
papers.abstract: We evaluate, at implementation level and under an explicit threat model, the verification pipelines of three Verifiable Credential (VC) formats: SD-JWT VC; the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with the Data Integrity cryptosuite eddsa-rdfc-2022 (W3C VCDM); and mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5). For W3C VCDM we identify and exercise three structural attack surfaces from remote context resolution and RDFC-1.0 canonicalization: denial of service (DoS) via poison graphs, context injection through @context, and server-side request forgery (SSRF) reachable via malicious URLs, all at default settings. A poison graph, whose blank-node references are symmetric enough to force RDFC-1.0 into deep recursion, raises it to 278x the baseline from five blank nodes in 527 bytes, and to 13.5 s from eight. Every experiment ran in four environments sharing runtime and library versions; the multiple moves with the machine (251--424x for one input), not with its speed. Cost tracks that symmetry rather than the node count: an acyclic input with 1,500 blank nodes stays at 462--714x. A call limit separates the two: every attack family aborts at 16 or below, every legitimate credential completes at 1, but a shallow, wide recursion, such as the acyclic control, passes whatever the bound. DoS does not presuppose adversarial input: with production education schemas, canonicalization costs 23--34x a simple credential in one environment, 16--49x across four. Effective mitigations are a static document loader, which removes the retrieval latency and both remote-context surfaces; a context allowlist; and a call limit with a size bound. SD-JWT VC and mdoc need neither canonicalization nor external references, and our verifiers resisted every vector evaluated. These are not format-specific defects but properties of the pipeline and its configuration.

papers.title: $τ$-Rec-Books: A Disclosure-Controlled Benchmark for Requirement Elicitation in Agentic Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: While conversational recommendation systems provide a more natural user interface, they face the challenge of progressively discovering a user's needs before they can recommend an item that satisfies them. To evaluate the ability of AI agents at this elicitation process, we introduce $τ$-Rec-Books, a benchmark that holds each user request fixed while varying only when the user reveals their requirements: all at the start (volunteer), one at the start and the rest when asked (mixed), or some never (hidden). A hidden requirement can be found only by proposing books and inferring it from the user's accept or reject verdicts. We generate 450 tasks over a catalog of 20,000 books from Wikidata, develop a rule-based simulated user to answer the agent, and score recommendations against catalog metadata without an LLM judge. Across four agents and two search interfaces, success rates fall for every agent and interface, on average from 0.975 (volunteer) to 0.756 (mixed) and 0.283 (hidden). Mixed tasks fail mainly because agents do not ask, and when told to ask, every agent reaches at least 0.931. On hidden tasks, most failures come from agents recommending a book they never proposed to the user. When told to propose first, agents only match a simple baseline that proposes popular books, and stay well below one that uses rejection to rule out possible requirements. We release the catalog pipeline, task generator, simulated user, validators, reference agents, and all agent traces at https://github.com/nbharaths/tau-rec/tree/main/data/tracks/books-wikidata-v2.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Adaptive Heuristic Search for Agile Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling
papers.abstract: Agile Earth observation satellites must coordinate imaging tasks within limited observation windows, while accounting for attitude maneuvering and onboard energy constraints. Competition among observation opportunities makes scheduling performance sensitive to the heuristic rules used for task selection. This letter proposes a large language model (LLM)-assisted adaptive heuristic search method for agile Earth observation satellite scheduling. The LLM generates an initial heuristic rule according to the characteristics of the scheduling instance. During the subsequent ant colony search, search performance and scheduling information are fed back to the LLM to refine the heuristic rule. The proposed modifications are evaluated through paired solution constructions before being incorporated into the search process. A unified scheduling procedure determines task selection, satellite assignment, and observation timing under the operational constraints. Experiments on six scheduling scenarios involving 50--200 imaging tasks demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 4.3\%--9.6\% higher mean observation benefit than the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Nuisance structure and the detection boundary for population size: how profiling can change a rate, not only a constant
papers.abstract: A system contains an unknown number $N$ of units, each failing at an unknown common rate, each unit is removed once it fails. The failure-rate declines as units are removed, but after only a few failures the decline is too slight to distinguish from a constant rate, and the maximum-likelihood estimate of $N$ is infinite with substantial probability. This is a well-known feature of the model, but its probability has not been quantified. We show that about $N^{2/3}$ failures are needed before a finite population can be distinguished from an inexhaustible one, and that at this scale the profile log-likelihood ratio converges to that of a Gaussian shift experiment, in which an infinite estimate occurs with a calculable probability. The exponent is not a property of the model alone. Profiling annihilates the Taylor terms that the nuisance-parameters can reproduce, and detectability is governed by the first surviving term. For example, unknown drift in testing-effort reproduces the linear term, leaving a quadratic survivor and raising the requirement to $N^{4/5}$; in general the critical scale is $N^{2q/(2q+1)}$ for a survivor of order $q$. We obtain the limiting-law of the estimator, the null likelihood ratio distribution, and confidence sets that may be unbounded.

papers.title: A Bayesian-Geometric Reading of Classical Model-Based Optimal Design
papers.abstract: The classical model-based optimal design criteria (D-, T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality) are usually motivated via the Cramér--Rao bound as optimizing scalar functions of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). This paper offers a complementary reading in which each criterion appears asymptotically as $N \to \infty$ as the leading-order term of an expected dissimilarity between prior and posterior, with the FIM entering through the Bernstein--von Mises limit. The Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence of the posterior relative to the prior recovers D-optimality (classically known); a reverse KL of the prior relative to the posterior recovers T-optimality (here defined as maximization of the trace of the FIM, following one common convention) and its weighted-trace generalization; and a first-order approximation of the squared 2-Wasserstein distance recovers L-, C- and A-optimality. The five criteria emerge as instances of a common Bayesian-geometric template, indexed by three choices: the dissimilarity, the prior parametrization, and the approximation scheme used to evaluate it (e.g.\ Taylor expansions of the matrix square root). For the weighted criteria, the Gaussian prior covariance encodes the criterion's weight matrix, so any choice of weights corresponds to a specific prior in the family. The T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality derivations appear novel to the best of my knowledge. A sixth criterion, E-optimality, is recovered not as an independent expected-dissimilarity limit but as a min-max robustification of C-optimality against uncertainty in the modeler's prior direction. The framework is extended to distinguish between a designer's prior over unknown parameters at design time and a modeler's prior used for posterior inference, recovering the classical expected information gain objective as a special case.

papers.title: Formalizing PTX in Lean to Prove GPU Kernel Correctness
papers.abstract: We present an approach to mathematically formalizing PTX, an approach that allows modeling and reasoning about patterns common in GPU kernels for Deep Learning, including acquire-release, tensor cores, proxies, async operations, multi-kernel pipelines and data-dependent control flow. We implement it in Lean and use it to prove the correctness of simple implementations of a WGMMA GEMM kernel, FlashAttention, and a 3-kernel MoE pipeline.

papers.title: Binary Huffman Coding with Unequal Letter Costs Is NP-Complete
papers.abstract: Binary prefix coding assigns prefix-free binary words to symbols to minimize their frequency-weighted cost. Huffman solved the equal-letter-cost case in polynomial time in 1952 [Proc. IRE'52]. For unequal letter costs, Karp gave an integer-programming formulation in 1961 [IRE Trans. Inf. Theory'61]. Exact polynomial-time algorithms for fixed integer costs were given by Golin and Rote [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory'98] and Bradford, Golin, Larmore, and Rytter [J. Algorithms'02]. For input-dependent costs, Golin, Mathieu, and Young gave a polynomial-time approximation scheme [SICOMP'12]. The exact complexity when letter costs are part of the input had remained unresolved. We resolve this $65$-year-old problem by proving that deciding whether there exists a binary prefix-free code of frequency-weighted cost at most a given threshold is NP-complete, even when the letter costs are consecutive positive integers $(M,M+1)$ supplied as part of the input. All frequencies, letter costs, and thresholds are encoded in binary. Consequently, finding an optimal code is NP-hard. Our proof uses two polynomial-time reductions, starting from Planar Independent Set. The intermediate problem prescribes the number of leaves at each depth of a full ordered binary tree and minimizes a signed linear score on their sorted right-edge counts. The first reduction represents an independent-set verification program by a tree growing level by level. A fixed-profile identity converts narrow coordinate restrictions into linear penalties that enforce the computation. The second reduction adds large dyadic terms to the symbol frequencies to force prescribed depths. These terms contribute a constant to the weighted number of ones, leaving smaller signed perturbations to reproduce the tree score.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum--Classical Pauli-Correlator Architecture for Image Reconstruction
papers.abstract: We introduce the Pauli-Correlator Autoencoder (PCAE), a hybrid quantum--classical architecture for image reconstruction. PCAE splits an image into patches and compresses each patch as a matrix product state (MPS). A small quantum circuit turns each compressed patch into a few measured numbers, and a classical neural network rebuilds the patch from these numbers and the patch position. A learnable energy term, taken from physics, is added to training and tracked as training proceeds. Two versions place the six qubits on a line (PCAE1D) or on a grid (PCAE2D). An averaging step makes the PCAE2D features follow rotations and reflections of the image exactly. Trained on one image at a time, PCAE2D rebuilds images from six public datasets with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 25.8 to 41.6 decibels. On CIFAR-10 images not used in training, a formula-based stand-in for the PCAE2D features performs within 1 decibel of several simpler classical methods. Five trained models also run on real IBM quantum computers without retraining, and rebuild images at 25.90 to 31.52 decibels. A short argument and a synthetic test show that, with a linear final layer, measuring qubits in pairs is needed for targets built from products of inputs. These results show that PCAE works as a hybrid model that rebuilds varied images and runs on today's quantum hardware at the six-qubit scale.

papers.title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet inflation. Starting from the quadratic perturbation actions, we construct the two-mode Hamiltonians and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing amplitudes and angles. Although the tensor speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss--Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We track the squeezing dynamics from the subhorizon to the superhorizon regime and evaluate the Nielsen wave-function complexity of the resulting two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation in the squeezing amplitudes, while the unwrapped squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Consequently, the circuit complexity is controlled mainly by the amplitude evolution. A positive coupling enhances the scalar complexity but slightly suppresses the tensor complexity for the benchmarks considered. These opposite trends show that scalar and tensor Gaussian states retain distinct information about the same modified inflationary background even when tensor propagation is luminal.

papers.title: Amplified transport variability in granular slope flows near the critical angle
papers.abstract: Mechanical disturbances such as seismic shaking can set a granular slope in motion. Understanding the resulting transport before arrest is important for predicting topographic change, assessing landslide hazards and controlling powder flows in industrial processes. Experiments show that smaller disturbances can trigger avalanches and larger areas are mobilized as slopes approach their stability limit. Yet how much transport varies between events under the same macroscopic conditions and forcing remains unclear. Here we use numerical simulations to show that transport variability is amplified near the critical angle. We apply identical basal pulses to static granular layers with the same macroscopic conditions but different initial particle configurations. Although the mean transport increases approximately in inverse proportion to the angular distance from the critical angle, the standard deviation increases even faster and can exceed the mean. Thus, identical forcing can produce widely different transport amounts. Deterministic constitutive laws that assign a unique response to given macroscopic conditions cannot capture this variability. We introduce fluctuations into the energy balance to develop a stochastic model that captures the main features of the broadening transport distribution. These results show that assessing transport near the critical angle requires considering its distribution, not just its mean, and motivate constitutive descriptions that incorporate fluctuations.

papers.title: Pick-up sticks problems for exponential and Pareto distributions
papers.abstract: We deal with the following two pick-up sticks problems: given an integer n greater than or equal to 3, we choose n sticks with independent random lengths from an exponential distribution or Pareto type I distribution, and we are interested in the probability that no three of them can be the sides of a triangle. In case of exponential distribution, this problem has been solved by other authors: the probability in question is equal to $n!/\big((F_3-1)(F_4-1)\cdots(F_{n+2}-1)\big)$, where $(F_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ is the sequence of Fibonacci numbers. We give a new, self-contained and detailed proof for this formula, which uses a different method compared to the earlier ones. In case of Pareto type I distribution, we derive new formulae for the corresponding probability.

papers.title: Movable Antenna Aided Robust Wireless Transmission: From Model-Based Optimization to Scalable Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This paper investigates robust joint antenna positioning and precoding for multiuser movable antenna (MA) systems under imperfect channel state information (CSI). First, we identify the mismatch between the spatial statistics of densely sampled MA channels and the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) basis used for conventional robust precoding. To address this, we develop a novel discrete prolate spheroidal sequence (DPSS)-based a posteriori channel model. By exploiting the spatial covariance structure of MA channels, this model is better suited to modeling MA channel uncertainty. Building on this model, we develop an efficient iterative algorithm for robust joint antenna positioning and precoding to maximize the expected sum rate. By transforming the coupled optimization of antenna positioning and precoding at each iteration into direct comparisons of closed-form scores, we design a low-complexity position replacement scheme that effectively reuses matrix computations across candidate sets. To further improve efficiency and scalability, we exploit the inherent tensor equivariance (TE) of the problem to develop a reinforcement learning framework. To explicitly account for channel uncertainty, we develop novel pairwise user-interaction and CSI-conditioned equivariant attention mechanisms to encode channel statistics and adaptively fuse them with the available CSI. We further introduce distance-biased spatial attention to incorporate the geometry of candidate positions into attention weighting, thereby enhancing spatial feature learning. Simulation results show that the proposed methods improve sum-rate performance while reducing online runtime under imperfect CSI. These methods also achieve near-optimal performance under perfect CSI, closely matching the exhaustive-search method. Moreover, the learning framework generalizes across different numbers of users and MAs without retraining.

papers.title: Universal Free-Electron-Sideband Control
papers.abstract: Advances in free-electron quantum optics are establishing free electrons as a versatile quantum resource. Photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) interactions and free drift provide elementary operations for shaping the longitudinal electron wavefunction, yet their full control capabilities remain unexplored. Here, we prove that a finite sequence of alternating monochromatic PINEM interactions and free drifts can approximate any prescribed inner-product-preserving map from a finite-dimensional input subspace into the full ideal electron-sideband Hilbert space to arbitrary accuracy. We therefore call the protocol PINEMAD (PINEM And Drift). This framework encompasses state preparation, unitary gates, and isometric encoding. We further show numerically that parameter optimization enables high-fidelity state preparation at finite electron energy spreads, using experimentally accessible coupling strengths and tabletop-scale total drift lengths. These results establish electron energy sidebands as a programmable quantum resource.

papers.title: Reducing the arithmetic cost of quantum derivative pricing with language-model circuit design
papers.abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation can estimate expected discounted payoffs with quadratically fewer oracle calls than Monte Carlo, but each call requires coherent computation. We use language-model-assisted circuit design to reduce reversible payoff arithmetic for a three-asset worst-of autocallable and a target accrual redemption forward (TARF). The constructions retain compact integer representations of market paths alongside contract history, reconstructing quantities temporarily for contract decisions and payoff-angle evaluation. Relative to matched internal references, the factor-sum autocallable and windowed TARF circuits reduce the product of Toffoli count and peak logical qubits $(N_{Tof} Q_{max})$ by factors of 2.39 and 4.84, respectively. At a second autocallable setting, fresh search recovers a 1.35-fold saving after the tested fixed adaptation loses its advantage. For the factor-sum circuit, we prove exact coherent execution of its integer specification for every input, incoming accumulator and measurement record, with clean workspace and phase cancellation. A separate lattice calculation gives a numerical angle-tolerance-violation probability of 6.248e-8 and evaluates pricing bias under the declared loading law, with bounded omission but no certified numerical enclosure. The results connect compact representations to lower-cost payoff arithmetic and separately assessed logical and financial correctness. Their resource scope excludes loading, payoff rotation and estimation.

papers.title: Annealing-Induced Structural and Optical Evolution of Ion-Beam-Sputtered Ta2O5 Films for High-Power Laser Applications
papers.abstract: Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) thin films deposited by ion beam sputtering (IBS) are essential components in high-power laser systems, where post-deposition annealing is routinely used to optimize film quality. In this work, we systematically investigate the structural and optical evolution of IBS-deposited Ta2O5 single layers subjected to post-deposition annealing at temperatures from 400 to 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The films undergo an amorphous-to-polycrystalline transition between 600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, accompanied by a marked increase in surface roughness. Argon bubbles inherently incorporated during IBS serve as structural markers: their size correlates positively with the surface roughness from the as-deposited to 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ but decouples at 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, revealing a transition from matrix-relaxation-dominated to surface-diffusion-dominated behavior. Transmittance spectra show a red shift at 400 and 600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ which can be explained by physical thickness increase. Weak absorption decreases from ~6 ppm in as-deposited films to ~2 ppm at 400-600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ due to annihilation of oxygen vacancies, rises markedly at 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ due to grain-boundary defects and then drops again at 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ as grain boundaries relax. We identify 400 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ as the optimal annealing window for IBS-deposited Ta2O5 single layers, with the lowest surface roughness and effectively reducing weak absorption while preserving the amorphous phase.

papers.title: Topology Does Not Determine Defect Mobility in Active Polar Matter
papers.abstract: Topological defects are commonly characterized by their charge, although defects with the same charge can have different internal morphologies. We study the annihilation of isolated $\pm1$ defect pairs in a two-dimensional compressible Toner--Tu model, varying the morphology of the $+1$ defect while keeping the initial charges and separation fixed. Activity produces a morphology-dependent mobility asymmetry: reversing the radial orientation of an aster reverses which defect travels farther, and asters show the strongest response. An early-time analysis reveals that the initial morphology selects distinct density modes whose gradients subsequently feed back on the polarization. Consistently, removing the density-gradient coupling strongly suppresses the asymmetry. These results establish defect morphology, in addition to topological charge, as a dynamical variable governing defect-pair motion in active polar matter.

papers.title: Reference-Beam-Assisted Perturbation-Resistant Imaging Through A Single Multimode Fiber
papers.abstract: Multimode fiber (MMF) imaging is highly sensitive to mechanical perturbations, which alter modal coupling and disrupt the speckle-to-target mapping. Here, we propose a reference-beam-assisted method for image reconstruction across multiple fiber configurations. An independent reference beam propagates through the same MMF as the imaging signal without target modulation, providing target-independent transmission-state information through its speckle patterns without requiring a separate configuration-sensing structure. A neural network jointly processes the signal and reference speckles to reconstruct target images. Experiments with MNIST and Fashion-MNIST across 10 fiber configurations demonstrate improved reconstruction quality, faster training convergence, and more accurate configuration identification. Further evaluation across 40 configurations confirms the reconstruction benefit of reference-beam assistance over a larger set of perturbed fiber states. These results provide a foundation for developing perturbation-adaptive MMF imaging systems for flexible endoscopy and minimally invasive optical diagnostics.

papers.title: On the most informative Boolean function under noise
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a uniform random bit string and $Y$ be obtained by flipping each bit of $X$ independently with probability $p$. Let $C$ be a random bit obtained as a function of $Y$. We show that $\mathbf{I}(C:X)\le \mathbf{I}(Y_1:X)$ for all $p\in[0,1]$, which resolves a conjecture posed by Courtade and Kumar in 2013.

papers.title: Verifier strength does not buy discovery quality: a pre-registered two-domain test of LLM-based automated research, with post-hoc evidence pointing to proposer-pool composition
papers.abstract: Automated research pipelines pair an LLM proposer with a verifier on an implicit bet: discovery quality rises with verification strength. Under a pre-registered protocol we test this bet in two real-data domains -- job-shop scheduling and vehicular edge offloading on Beijing T-Drive trajectories -- across 100 matched LLM/random pairs per domain and three verifier tiers. The manipulation binds -- a 429-case mutation battery shows scores rising across tiers -- yet the paired LLM-over-random advantage does not scale with it (A, one-sided p=0.1115; D, p=0.9994), and in D shrinks under the strict tier (margin contrast -0.040, p=0.0013). The two lower gates promote identical candidates in 100/100 and 99/100 pairs, so the strict order is untestable when they coincide. Constructively, LLM proposals carry a real paired advantage over random controls, but a post-hoc union-pool analysis shows the fastest path to better discovery is widening the pool, not tightening the gate: mixing the two pools adds +1.52 holdout-value units in domain A (one-sided Wilcoxon, n=100, p=0.0002) -- evidence that pool composition, not verification strength, is the lever. Criteria, ledgers and scripts are archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23308866).

papers.title: Stress-Testing Small-Scale Cosmological Inference With Empirical Galaxy--Halo Connection Models
papers.abstract: Small-scale galaxy clustering contains substantial cosmological information, but extracting it reliably requires robust modeling of the galaxy--halo connection. In this work, we compare two widely adopted families of empirical models, subhalo abundance matching (SHAM) and the halo occupation distribution (HOD), testing their predictions for galaxy clustering and their recovery of the input cosmology. Using Aemulus-$β$, a new multi-cosmology simulation suite with substructure merger trees, we fit multiple SHAM and HOD models to the small-scale clustering of a stellar-mass-selected mock galaxy catalog generated with the more physical semi-empirical model UniverseMachine. We then use cosmological evidence modeling to infer the structure growth parameter $S_8$. Our results show that the SHAM model, regardless of the treatment of numerically disrupted subhalos, is able to offer tight, unbiased constraints on $S_8$ with ~2-3% precision, using simulations of relatively small volumes that span a limited number of cosmologies.
