SCFT combines local spectral convolution, permutation-equivariant beam-set attention, and a query-based Transformer decoder to detect and classify line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) paths and estimate their observed delays, AoAs, and AoDs. Experiments on realistic ray-tracing data show that SCFT reduces the generalized optimal sub-pattern assignment (GOSPA) error by 13.4% compared with ResNet, the strongest competing baseline. We further demonstrate this advantage in independent snapshot positioning and radio SLAM, where SCFT reduces position RMSE by 18.5% and 65.0%, respectively, relative to ResNet. These findings highlight the importance of explicitly recovering multipath geometry, as improvements in MPC estimation can translate into substantial gains in downstream tasks.

papers.title: No infinite cluster at criticality for long-range percolation with fast-decaying interactions
papers.abstract: We consider independent long-range bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in which $x$ and $y$ are joined with probability $1-e^{-βJ(x-y)}$. Let $d\ge2$ and let $J$ be invariant under coordinate permutations and sign changes, positive on nearest-neighbour pairs, and satisfy $\liminf_{n\to\infty} n^d\sum_{\|x\|>n}J(x)=0$. We prove that there is no infinite cluster at the critical parameter. Together with Berger's theorem for heavy tails, this gives continuity of the phase transition for $J(x)\asymp\|x\|^{-d-α}$ for every $α>0$ except $α=d$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for every exponentially decaying kernel satisfying these hypotheses. Previously the fast-decaying case was known for nearest-neighbour and uniform finite-range kernels, in $d=2$ for finite-range and exponential kernels, and in high dimension for sufficiently spread-out kernels. The proof adapts a recent renormalization argument for nearest-neighbour percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ that is driven by a gluing inequality conjectured by Kozma and Nitzan. Long edges enter in two places: they can jump over the surfaces that a nearest-neighbour path must cross, and they let a cluster outside a box enter it from far away. We control the first with thick outer faces and the tail condition, and the second by measuring entrances through the total edge weight between a cluster and a box rather than through the number of boundary vertices.

papers.title: Low-Latency Joint Source-Channel Coding with Multiple Constant Curvature Curves
papers.abstract: We propose constant-curvature curve multicode (C3M), a multi-branch extension of constant-curvature curve tube (C3T) analog joint source-channel coding for one-shot transmission over fixed isotropic AWGN channels. Instead of mapping a scalar source to a single curve on the power sphere, C3M partitions the source interval across a union of constant-speed branch curves in even-dimensional Euclidean space. This construction increases the available geometric degrees of freedom while preserving a low block length analog encoding structure. We derive the induced mixture output distribution, posterior representation, MAP and MMSE estimators, and mutual-information decomposition into branch-identification and along-curve components. We then introduce geometry- and classification-aware branch allocation rules based on tube density, curve length, and branch-classification reliability. The resulting design procedure fixes the optimal C3T curve as a starting branch and sequentially selects additional branches, thereby reducing the combinatorial cost of exhaustive multi-curve search. We use NORM-inspired branch-conditioned spectral decoders based on Fourier-feature lifting of the received ambient vector. Numerical experiments in four and six dimensions show that adding candidate branch curves improves the finite-dimensional end-to-end signal-to-distortion ratio, with selected two- and three-candidate C3M systems outperforming the one-curve baseline at +10 dB SNR. The results show that multi-curve analog mappings provide a practical finite-dimensional design route for low block length joint source-channel coding.

papers.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: KPZ universality
papers.abstract: We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and positive representing measure, together with joint profile convergence at every prescribed finite parameter list. We also prove convergence of the height evolution from general upper-semicontinuous initial profiles to the half-space KPZ fixed point. The associated passage field converges locally uniformly to the half-space directed landscape, jointly with evolutions from finitely many initial profiles driven by the same environment. The convergence results cover the critical boundary window and every fixed subcritical boundary rate, including zero. All fixed subcritical rates produce the same limiting laws.

papers.title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Multi-User OFDM ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is envisioned as a key enabling technology for 6G networks. Efficient resource sharing between communication and sensing is a fundamental challenge in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) ISAC systems, particularly in multi-user scenarios, where channel diversity can be exploited to improve resource utilization. This paper investigates joint subcarrier assignment and power allocation for a downlink multi-user OFDM ISAC system, with the objective of minimizing the delay Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) subject to constraints on the normalized integrated sidelobe level (ISL) over the region of interest (RoI), per-user data rates, and total transmit power. We first derive a convex formulation for sensing power allocation given fixed subcarrier assignments, and then develop an equivalent mixed-integer conic formulation of the joint optimization problem. To obtain computationally tractable solutions, we propose a conic relaxation-guided fix-and-optimize (CRG-FO) algorithm that integrates continuous relaxation, power re-optimization under fixed subcarrier assignments, and restricted neighborhood search. Simulation results demonstrate that joint subcarrier and power allocation reduces the distance CRLB relative to uniform subcarrier and power allocation across the tested ISL thresholds, rate loads, and user configurations. Power optimization on uniform sensing supports captures most of this gain, while adaptive subcarrier assignment provides only modest additional improvement.

papers.title: Convergence of many-body truncations in the in-medium similarity renormalization group
papers.abstract: The in-medium similarity renormalization group (IMSRG) is a leading \textit{ab initio} method for describing atomic nuclei. Most applications truncate the flowing operators at the normal-ordered two-body level, neglecting induced higher-body terms. Convergence with increasing operator rank remains poorly understood, particularly in strongly correlated systems. We systematically assess the many-body truncation hierarchy in the single-reference and multi-reference IMSRG, retaining normal-ordered operators through the four-body and three-body levels, respectively. Using an exactly solvable pairing-plus-particle-hole model, we quantify successive higher-body corrections over a broad range of interaction strengths, spanning weakly to strongly correlated regimes. The multi-reference formulation exhibits faster and more robust convergence than its single-reference counterpart, with the advantage becoming most pronounced at strong coupling. In this regime, higher-rank irreducible density matrices play an essential role in achieving convergence of the many-body expansion.

papers.title: Cosmological rigidity via $p$-harmonic temporal functions
papers.abstract: We prove a splitting theorem for cosmological spacetimes which admit a globally $p$-harmonic Cauchy temporal function for some $p < 1$, without making any use of timelike lines. In Bartnik's context of cosmological and timelike geodesically complete spacetimes, we establish a Liouville-type unboundedness result which shows that globally $p$-harmonic temporal functions, $p < 1$, are necessarily Cauchy temporal. Moreover, using the theory of elliptic PDEs, we show that locally Lipschitz $p$-harmonic temporal functions with $p < 1$ are in fact smooth. Altogether, our work reduces the resolution of Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture to the global weak solvability of the $p$-d'Alembert equation for some $p < 1$ in the class of locally Lipschitz temporal functions.

papers.title: Local Limit Theorem for Branching Processes in Varying Environments
papers.abstract: Let $Z_{i,n}$ be the population at time $n$ descended from one particle at time $i$ in a branching process in a varying environment. Under two-sided bounds on products of offspring means, an integrable uniform second-moment tail condition, and nondegeneracy and unit positive-support gcd of all weak limits, we prove $\mathbb{P}(Z_{i,n}=k)\le C(n-i+1)^{-2}$ uniformly in $0\le i<n$ and $k\ge1$, and obtain a local limit theorem as $n-i,k\to\infty$ with $k\le L_0(n-i)$, without third-moment assumptions. These results extend the classical local probability estimates for critical Galton--Watson processes to varying environments.

papers.title: CipherFlow: Compiling AI Programs for Efficient Cryptographically Secure Inference
papers.abstract: Cryptographically secure inference faces two practical challenges: making secure programming accessible to AI developers and data scientists, and achieving efficient execution across deployment environments. Developers must compose cryptographic primitives correctly, while performance depends on hardware, networks, and evolving ciphertext states. We present CipherFlow, a compiler framework that takes a high-level AI computation graph, available cryptographic primitives, and a target hardware and network configuration to generate an executable, latency-optimized secure inference program. CipherFlow automates cryptographic execution decisions through three techniques: MicroBench profiles deployment-specific primitive costs; state-expanded planning jointly optimizes homomorphic encryption (HE) and secure multi-party computation (MPC) placement, conversions, and ciphertext maintenance under cryptographic-state constraints; and BlockFold summarizes branched regions to scale planning to Transformer graphs. Evaluation using measured HE/MPC backend costs across CPU/GPU and network settings shows up to 16.5$\times$ speedup on BERT-base and over 22$\times$ on ViT compared with static hybrid placement baselines. CipherFlow separates model programming from cryptographic execution decisions, enabling developers to express AI computations while the compiler constructs efficient secure programs.

papers.title: CONFIRM: Governing Scientific Reporting for Trustworthy Agentic Neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can autonomously run neuroimaging analyses from research questions to reported findings. Existing agentic systems use tools to check that code runs and reported values match its output, but rely on LLM judgment to decide which results warrant scientific reporting. We show that LLM judges endorse site-confounded findings even when the confound is presented as evidence. We present \textbf{CONFIRM}, a framework that separates running an analysis from deciding which findings to report. CONFIRM encodes each hypothesis as a machine-readable, pre-specified analysis plan that fixes the claim and its pass criteria before computing results. It then filters results through five deterministic gates (search history and multiplicity, confounds, power, analytic stability, and replication) under three configurable reporting standards, from least to most demanding: \textit{Screen}, \textit{Replicate}, and \textit{Full}. Failed claims receive diagnoses that guide follow-up analyses. To evaluate reporting decisions at the claim level, we introduce \textbf{NeuroClaimBench}, comprising 489 executable neuroimaging claims with frozen data, including literature-supported findings and 150 controls designed to violate individual methodological requirements. On NeuroClaimBench, CONFIRM falsely supports at most 3\% of controls, compared with 23--38\% for the baselines, while recovering up to 61\% of literature-supported claims. When auditing an existing agent, CONFIRM reduces false support on controls from 23\% to 0\% while retaining the agent's literature-supported claims. Its diagnostic feedback also produces more supported revisions than Self-Refine with fewer LLM calls. Together, CONFIRM and NeuroClaimBench show that basing reporting decisions on pre-specified analysis plans and deterministic gates is essential for trustworthy autonomous scientific discovery.

papers.title: Correctness and Predictive Uncertainty in Bayesian TSK Fuzzy Regression: A Reproducible Evaluation on Tabular and Building-Meter Data
papers.abstract: Uncertainty estimates from fuzzy regression are informative only when the implementation is correct and the comparison protocol makes the sources of variation visible. We revisit a first-order Takagi--Sugeno--Kang (TSK) regression implementation and rebuild its dense, conjugate Bayesian, BIC-based, and rule-level spike-and-slab estimators using corrected code. The corrected pipeline freezes the Gaussian membership partition at training time, uses a scaled conjugate prior, evaluates firing strengths in the log domain, and reports direct posterior-predictive quantiles for Bayesian methods. Across 30 outer 80/20 splits on three targets from two UCI regression datasets, corrected TSK-LS obtains $R^2=0.957$, $0.923$, and $0.786$ on Energy-Heating, Energy-Cooling, and Concrete, respectively; rule-level Gibbs sampling with Bayesian model averaging obtains $0.957$, $0.922$, and $0.784$. We then evaluate the same workflow on a bounded chronological sample of the Building Data Genome 2 meter data that covers 158 buildings across 17 sites. In a common-unit evaluation, every method is scored on the same 47,400 test rows and every trained model uses 94,800 train--validation rows. Persistence has RMSE $27.710$, compared with $29.083$ for both TSK-LS and Bayesian TSK; the pre-specified building-level mean RMSE difference between Bayesian TSK and persistence is $+0.0447$ with a 95% site-cluster bootstrap interval of $[-1.5536,1.5665]$. The Bayesian TSK 90% intervals have PICP $0.980$ and MPIW $116.469$. Taken together, the evidence supports a narrower conclusion: spike-and-slab model averaging is a reproducible implementation option, but it does not provide a demonstrated accuracy or calibration advantage across the tested tabular and building-meter settings.

papers.title: $p$-Wasserstein distance and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cramér-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$. We also determine the covariance bias under the uncorrected normalization and establish the corresponding Wasserstein bounds, lower bounds and moderate deviation estimates. The dimension and the model parameters are fixed.

papers.title: Precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with Weibull-type and lognormal-type random step sizes
papers.abstract: We prove precise large deviations for the symmetric elephant random walk with random step sizes. When the distribution of $|Z_1-1|$ is subexponential, we first show that, for each fixed$p\in[0,1]$, there exists a positive number sequence $b_n\to\infty$ such that \[ \mathbb P(S_n>x)\sim \mathbb P(S_n<-x)\sim \frac n2\overline F(x) \] uniformly for $x\ge b_n$, where $\overline F(x)=\mathbb P(|Z_1-1|>x)$. This existence result requires no moment assumptions and does not specify the growth rate of $b_n$. For $p\in[0,3/4]$, we further give explicit sufficient conditions on $b_n$ under Weibull-type and lognormal-type tail conditions with a regularly varying factor $x^γL(x)$, where $γ\in\mathbf R$ and $L$ is a positive measurable slowly varying function. Analogous results hold with $\mathbb P(|Z_1|>x)$ and non-strict tails.

papers.title: Transport for Conditional Sampling: Foundations and Applications
papers.abstract: Conditional sampling is central to Bayesian inference, generative modeling, and causal inference: given a joint law for random variables $X$ and $Y$ and an observation $Y=y$, one seeks to sample from the conditional law of $X\mid Y=y$. Even when the joint distribution is accurately represented, this task can be computationally difficult as it may require evaluating intractable normalizing constants or solving a new inference problem for each observation. Measure transport provides an approach to this problem by identifying a map with triangular structure that directly pushes forward a reference to the conditional of a joint distribution for any observation. This article reviews the theoretical, methodological, and algorithmic foundations of triangular transports, with the Knothe-Rosenblatt rearrangement as a canonical construction. We discuss methods for estimating triangular maps from finite samples, as well as their use in simulation-based inference and causal inference. While our primary aim is to review existing formulations, we also present new ideas and open questions for conditional sampling using transport.

papers.title: Boson sampling is fragile to loss
papers.abstract: Boson sampling experiments aim to demonstrate quantum computational advantage with increasing numbers of interfering photons. A central question is whether their computational hardness survives under photon loss. We show that even an arbitrarily small nonzero uniform loss rate permits efficient classical sampling in the average case when the rate remains fixed as the system grows. We exploit how loss suppresses correlations involving many photons to approximate the full output distribution using low correlation orders. The resulting samplers run in time polynomial in system size and inverse total variation error, with the error averaged over Haar random interferometers. The results apply to Fock state boson sampling with single-photon states in distinct input modes and arbitrary additional vacuum inputs, and to Gaussian boson sampling with equal squeezing of bounded strength in every input mode. Classical sampling is efficient even when the mean detected photon number grows linearly with system size, showing that large photon counts alone do not ensure computational hardness.

papers.title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
papers.abstract: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.

papers.title: Longest-Queue Policies in Dynamic Matching with Abandonments
papers.abstract: We study a dynamic two-way matching market in which agents of heterogeneous types arrive over time, wait to be matched according to a compatibility network, and abandon the system if their random patience expires. The decision maker collects match rewards and pays holding and abandonment costs, and seeks to maximize the expected net value over a finite horizon. We evaluate policies by their approximation ratio against a fluid benchmark, the optimal value of a linear-programming relaxation that upper bounds the expected net value of every policy. Under a general position gap (GPG) condition, which requires the unique optimal dual solution of this linear program to remain optimal under small perturbations of the arrival rates, we propose a longest-queue policy. The policy first uses this dual solution to identify a set of good match types and a set of critical agent types. Upon each arrival, it considers only good matches and matches the arrival to the critical partner with the longest queue subject to availabilities. In the high-volume regime, in which arrival rates are scaled by s, we prove that the policy attains an approximation ratio of at least 1-O(1/s) at every scale s >= 1 and every horizon T >= 1, so the ratio tends to 1 as s goes to infinity.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Minimax Prediction for Stationary Renewal Processes
papers.abstract: The minimax next-symbol Kullback-Leibler risk for stationary binary renewal processes is known to have order n^(-1/2). We give a polynomial-time predictor attaining this order for an arbitrary unknown finite-mean interarrival law. The construction uses a classical type-uniform renewal code. Its contribution is an exact dynamic program for censored prefix marginals, avoiding enumeration of gap histograms or binary completions. Combined with an established prediction reduction, it gives risk at most [log M_(n+1)+log(n+2)]/n, where M_N counts renewal types. Shared suffix updates reduce the total computation to O(n^3) arithmetic work and polynomial bit complexity, without tail, mixing, known-mean, or bounded-support assumptions. The statistical rate and its lower bound are prior results; the proposed advance concerns computation.

papers.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
papers.abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.

papers.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
papers.abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.

papers.title: Learning materials spectra across modalities and scales with structure-conditioned neural fields
papers.abstract: Spectroscopic observables encode rich information about material behavior across diverse, often high-dimensional domains of energy, momentum, and other experimental coordinates, providing critical insights into the physical properties underlying material functionalities and applications. However, learning these responses directly from atomic structures remains challenging due to the complexity of both structural configurations and spectroscopic observation spaces. Here, we develop a structure-conditioned neural-field framework that learns continuous spectroscopic response functions by coupling an equivariant structural encoder with a coordinate-conditioned network. The framework accurately predicts spectroscopic observables across diverse observation domains, ranging from one-dimensional densities of states to multidimensional scattering functions. We show that fine-tuning with limited spectral supervision captures strain- and composition-dependent spectral changes, with validated transfer to alloy configurations containing hundreds of atoms and computational scalability demonstrated for configurations exceeding $10^4$ atoms. Our work establishes a versatile and computationally scalable approach to learning structure-spectroscopy relationships, providing a foundation for spectroscopic analysis and future materials characterization, inverse problems, and experimental design.

papers.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.

papers.title: Gravitational dynamics and backward ray-traced shadows of bumblebee AdS black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the total observed frequency shift of photons emitted by massive geodesic particles in circular orbits near the event horizon of bumblebee AdS black holes. The cosmological effects of the bumblebee field are investigated through dynamical equations governing the evolution and characteristic features of the Universe. In addition, the bumblebee field generates cosmological anisotropies by acting as a source of anisotropy and selecting a preferred spatial direction. We formulate the characteristic equations for the innermost stable circular orbit using the effective potential approach. Further analysis is devoted to establishing a functional relationship between the BH mass and the observed redshift and blueshift of photons emitted from the accretion disk. Finally, we study the shadow cast by the bumblebee AdS BH using the backward ray tracing process implemented in the Arcmancer code, where photon geodesics are initialized at the observers location and integrated backward in time to generate BH images, typically illuminated by electromagnetic radiation from nearby accretion flows.

papers.title: Label-Free Performance Estimation of Deep Learning Based Radar Detectors in Time-Varying Environments
papers.abstract: Deep-learning-based radar target detectors can achieve strong performance in complex sensing environments. However, in time-varying environments, changes in clutter characteristics may cause the distribution of echoes to deviate from that of the training data, thereby degrading detector reliability. Timely identification of such degradation requires an accurate assessment of the deployed detector's performance; however, ground-truth labels for radar echoes are typically unavailable during deployment. This paper investigates label-free performance estimation for deployed deep learning-based radar target detectors. We first show that confidence-based estimators tend to overestimate detection performance under distribution shift because they fail to account for the discrepancy between the detector-induced pseudo-label distribution and the true label distribution. To address this limitation, we propose probabilistic optimal transport (POT), which assesses deployment performance by computing the Wasserstein distance between the detector's output probability distribution on unlabeled deployment echoes and the label distribution in the training data. We further develop thresholded probabilistic optimal transport (TPOT), which suppresses the influence of anomalous transport costs on the Wasserstein-distance-based estimate, thereby improving estimation robustness. Experiments on a publicly measured radar dataset demonstrate that POT and TPOT consistently outperform representative label-free baselines across deployment scenarios with varying degrees of data distribution shift.

papers.title: Leveraging high-performance head-only gradients to enable ~2-fold higher multiband acceleration in SMS-EPI and SMS-EPTI
papers.abstract: High-performance head-only gradient systems can substantially reduce echo spacing (ESP) in echo-planar imaging (EPI), but the resulting encoding speed is typically used to shorten readouts and reduce distortion. Here, we instead leverage the increased echo budget to enable denser k-space sampling and higher simultaneous-multislice (SMS) acceleration in SMS-EPI and SMS-EPTI. Fast k-space traversal with denser ky-kz sampling is achieved using peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS)-optimized gradient waveforms, while high-quality reconstruction is obtained using field-correcting GRAPPA (FCG). The resulting ESPs on MAGNUS 3T and Impulse 7T are approximately half those of high-performance whole-body systems, enabling approximately 2-fold higher multiband (MB) acceleration. This facilitates high-quality 2.5-mm isotropic whole-brain resting-state fMRI at 7T with MB28 and a repetition time (TR) of 123 ms.

papers.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for the sine-Gordon model in the subcritical regime
papers.abstract: We prove a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the massive two-dimensional sine-Gordon model throughout the subcritical range $0<β<8π$. For fixed mass, volume and arbitrary real coupling, the constant has a positive lower bound independent of the lattice spacing. When the dimensionless coupling is small, the lower bound is also uniform in volume and approaches the Gaussian constant as the coupling tends to zero. This extends the known range $β<6π$ and gives a rate of entropy decay for the reversible Langevin dynamics that remains positive as the cutoff is removed. The proof follows the Polchinski flow to a positive physical scale, where the Hamiltonian is a bounded perturbation of a uniformly convex one. For interactions invariant under constant field shifts, spatial differences bound their curvature by the gradient energy. For the oscillating part, we compare Gaussian integration with an average in which the original cosine phase fluctuates independently of the remaining variables. We estimate the comparison error at an intermediate scale, then differentiate the remaining Gaussian density. This preserves both phase damping and spatial decay without assuming bounds on second derivatives of the incoming local terms. The resulting strict gain between scales closes the estimates for every fixed $β<8π$.

papers.title: Plasmon modes in three-dimensional multifold semimetals. II. Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl and Kramers-Weyl nodes
papers.abstract: We investigate collective charge excitations in three-dimensional multifold semimetals in which multiple bands cross the Fermi level at a positive chemical potential, focusing on pseudospin-3/2 Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl semimetals and on Kramers-Weyl semimetals. Both systems host multiple concentric Fermi surfaces at positive chemical potential. Within the random-phase approximation, we analyse the density response, Drude weights, dielectric function, plasmon modes and their Landau damping, and Friedel oscillations, considering both small and arbitrary momentum transfers. In our companion work, arXiv:2610.18629, we investigated pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals, with and without a quadratic correction to their dispersion, as well as Hopf and Weyl semimetals. Comparing these systems allows us to elucidate the distinct roles of band dispersions and eigenstates in shaping collective charge dynamics. Our results demonstrate that collective charge excitations can distinguish multifold nodes with multiple Fermi surfaces and reveal information encoded in their eigenstates beyond that contained in the single-particle dispersion.

papers.title: Beyond-RTA magnetoconductivity of multifold semimetals under generic orientations of electromagnetic fields
papers.abstract: We present an exact solution of the linearised semiclassical Boltzmann equation (SBE) beyond the relaxation-time approximation for multifold semimetals under arbitrarily oriented electric and magnetic fields. The framework treats the Berry curvature, orbital magnetic moment, Lorentz-force operator, and scattering terms on equal footing. Momentum-independent scattering-amplitudes couple the Fermi-surface sheets through intranode, interband, and internode processes. The scattering kernel has a finite rank and the SBE reduces to a linear system for a few moments, which is closed by the electron-number constraint. We apply this approach to four systems involving quadratic-corrected triple-point, Weyl, and Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl nodes, including tilted triple-point nodes. We obtain analytical results at zero field and to leading orders in the magnetic field, alongside numerical solutions for the full field dependence. Our results elucidate the roles of the topological properties, Lorentz-force operator, tilt, and intra- and internode scatterings in shaping the magnetoelectric conductivity. It cures severe shortcomings of previous treatments like incomplete ansätze and incomplete treatment of the Lorentz-force operator.

papers.title: Artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice: a tricritical bridge from square to kagome
papers.abstract: Artificial spin ices (ASIs) are arrays of interacting nanomagnets in which phase transitions can be imaged and controlled. Studies of the thermodynamic have focused mainly on the square and kagome lattices, and on their variants. Here we study artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice, formed of squares and octagons. At fixed lattice constant, the ratio $r$ of the square and octagon link lengths tunes the interactions strongly while changing the geometry only slightly. Magnetic force microscopy and Monte Carlo simulations show a continuous bridge from square-ice-like to kagome-like behavior. At small $r$ the system has a single ordering transition, whereas at large $r$ it passes from a correlated paramagnet to charge order and then long-range order. The two regimes meet in a multicritical region, accurately modeled by a Blume-Capel model of the octagon toroidal moments. From this picture, we design a comparative magnetometry protocol that unambiguously separates interaction effects from single-nanomagnet effects in thermally active samples. Finally, the charge-ordered region maps onto a tunable dimer model, with a Coulomb phase and pinch points along the line between two ordered dimer phases. The CaVO ASI thus provides access to a rich phase diagram only through geometric tuning, without requiring extreme experimental conditions.

papers.title: The Costs and Benefits of Leveraged ETFs
papers.abstract: We study the costs and benefits of leveraged ETFs (LETFs), focusing on five determinants of performance: volatility drag, fees, financing costs, product launches, and market timing. Long broad-equity-index LETFs generated more than 100 billion US dollars in investor gains, including over 40 billion US dollars relative to counterfactual investments in the underlying assets, due to modest structural headwinds and rising markets. Single-stock LETFs, however, are launched on stocks near the top of the volatility and past-return distributions. This caters to retail demand for lottery-like payoffs, but it also creates larger volatility drag, higher financing costs, and greater exposure to losses from poor market timing.

papers.title: A GPU-Accelerated and Geometry-Aware Quantum-Classical Framework for Optimized PES Scans with CUDA-Q
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical workloads, particularly Potential Energy Surface (PES) scans in quantum chemistry using batched VQE and QAOA, involve many structurally similar Hamiltonians differing only in coefficients. Existing warm-start and meta-optimization strategies reuse parameters between instances but still consume fixed quantum-classical resources, ignoring cross-instance structural similarities. We present OptiPESS, a GPU-accelerated runtime system for adaptive resource allocation in hybrid quantum-classical execution. OptiPESS introduces the Locality-Occupancy-Variance (LOV) metric, a lightweight, geometry-aware measure of Hamiltonian similarity, coupled with efficient alignment and Pauli-classification passes. Using LOV, OptiPESS performs distance-aware scheduling of iteration and shot budgets, predicting which instances can be skipped, quick-solved, or fully optimized. Implemented atop CUDA-Q with persistent multi-GPU execution and near-linear scaling, OptiPESS reduces classical and quantum evaluations by up to 78.3\% and wall-time by up to 74.8\% while maintaining baseline accuracy. This demonstrates how lightweight static analysis and adaptive scheduling can transform quantum-classical co-execution from fixed-budget loops into a predictive, resource-aware runtime.

papers.title: Distributed Pinching-Antenna Architecture for Communication and Target Positioning
papers.abstract: We propose a pinching-antenna system (PASS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework for joint downlink communication and target positioning. The dielectric waveguides enable flexible signal radiation through activated pinching antennas (PAs), while the reflected echo signals are collected by a sensing receiver. A unified waveform is adopted to support both data transmission and sensing-echo processing. In particular, a two-stage procedure is developed for target localization using time-sum-of-arrival (TSoA) measurements, where the signal propagation distances are first estimated through de-chirp processing and beat frequency extraction. Then, the target position is obtained based on TSoA measurements using the weighted linear least squares(WLLS) technique. To characterize the fundamental limits of the PASS-assisted ISAC system, a Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRB) is derived, which captures the impact of PA activation. Furthermore, the PA activation problem is formulated to jointly optimize the communication spectral efficiency (SE) and sensing performance. To address this, a low-complexity heuristic greedy selection algorithm is proposed to determine the activated PA pattern. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms random PA selection, achieving gains of up to 81% improvement in communication SE.

papers.title: The light curve modeling of eclipsing cataclysmic variables: from period bouncers to nova-likes
papers.abstract: I describe the basic concepts used in developing the computer code CVlab V2.0, which simulates the light curves of close binary systems with accretion-disk structures. I provide a detailed description of the code, including its underlying assumptions, limitations, and applications, as well as prospects for future development.

papers.title: Decay of Correlations for Multiplicative Functionals of Determinantal Point Processes
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is an upper bound on the correlations of multiplicative functionals of determinantal point processes. In particular, for the sine process, the correlations of a multiplicative functional associated with a rapidly decaying function decay quadratically. It follows that the spectral density of such functionals belongs to the Sobolev space $H_1$.

papers.title: Sharper Bounds for Graphical Two-Choice Allocation
papers.abstract: In graphical two-choice allocation, vertices are bins, and each arriving ball must be placed irrevocably at one endpoint of a uniformly random edge. The objective is to keep the maximum-minus-minimum load gap small at every time. On cycles, endpoint-local monotone rules incur polynomial gaps at long time horizons, whereas global rules can achieve polylogarithmic gaps. We prove a joint exponential-moment inequality for the orthogonal contrasts of a binary partition tree, controlling all contrasts along a root-to-leaf path simultaneously. Applied to the Bansal--Feldheim strategy, it improves the gap on every $κ$-edge-connected $d$-regular graph from $O((d/κ)\log^4 n\log\log n)$ to $O((d/κ)\log^3 n\log\log n)$. We give an explicit strategy on the $n$-cycle with expected gap $O(\log^2 n)$ uniformly over deterministic times and exponential tails at each such time. An Euler-tour projection yields $O(\bar d\log^2(2M))$ for every connected graph with $M$ edges and degree-proportional capacities. For lower bounds, we introduce a stochastic cut workload: the expected largest normalized overload forced by the requests, plus an indivisibility term. For every online integral strategy, the supremum over time of the expected gap is at least one sixth of this benchmark. Regular rings of cliques attain $Ω((d/κ)\log n)$ along an explicit family, improving the prior additive lower bound. With unequal capacities, the workload need not control the gap: one family has constant relative cut slack, bounded workload and gap $Ω(\log\log n)$; another has workload at most $20$ but forces gap $Ω(\log n)$ even for clairvoyant fractional allocations that remain irrevocable.

papers.title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
papers.abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm.

papers.title: Logical-Class Diagnostic Layer for Stabilizer Codes and Decoders via Supercharge Structures
papers.abstract: We develop a decoder-agnostic logical-class diagnostic layer for abelian Pauli stabilizer codes, motivated by fault-tolerant quantum computing. An ancilla fermionic register defines a nilpotent supercharge whose clean degree-zero harmonic sector is the code space. Projected-return blocks derived from graded commutators organize the recovery test of whether a decoder-selected correction preserves every encoded input for every error in a declared same-syndrome family; the passing syndromes form the certified faithful window. Demoting the supercharge to an exact binary diagnostic formulation classifies residuals modulo stabilizers, separating a check violation, a harmless stabilizer residual, and a syndrome-silent nontrivial logical action, with a two-sector form for CSS codes. Because the unknown fault cancels, the relative logical class of two record-compatible candidates is computable online. We verify the diagnostic formalisms on the Steane code and specify a static--circuit bridge audit protocol for the Gross bivariate-bicycle quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code. The method supplements existing decoders without additional physical qubits for software use.

papers.title: An Introduction to Financial Derivatives: Open Lecture Notes
papers.abstract: These lecture notes give a broad introduction to financial derivatives at the level of a Masters program in quantitative finance. Topics include forward and futures contracts, no-arbitrage bounds and put-call parity, the binomial model, the fundamental theorems of asset pricing, Brownian motion and Itô calculus, the Black-Scholes model, the Greeks, variance swaps, local and stochastic volatility models including Heston, and static hedging of barrier options. Each chapter ends with exercises, and complete solutions, including Python code for the computational exercises, are provided in an appendix. The notes are open source: the LaTeX source is available at https://github.com/mattlorig/intro-financial-derivatives, and readers are invited to submit corrections and additions.

papers.title: Infinite Quantiles Inference under Local Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: We study simultaneous quantile inference under local differential privacy for a number of target probabilities that grows with the sample size. Each user participates once, so learning unknown quantile locations and calibrating their joint uncertainty must share the same private information. We fuse complementary cumulative distribution function (CDF) scores from a single tree report using their exact covariance; the variance at the correct anchor is no larger than that of either score, and anchor error incurs only quadratic excess variance. Three consecutive cohorts then localize the quantiles, estimate their densities, and supply fresh scores for a one-step correction and joint multiplier calibration. Under mild conditions, a uniform representation controls localization and density errors and yields asymptotically valid simultaneous coverage. A fixed-privacy regime permits every polynomially growing target grid. Simulations show consistent same-report precision gains, while comparisons with CDF-band inversion expose the sample cost of learning target locations. Census microdata illustrates how the resulting joint intervals support wage-percentile ratios.

papers.title: FACET: Feasibility-Automaton Complete Enumeration and Truncation-Free Scoring of Molecular Formulas from MS/MS
papers.abstract: Determining the neutral molecular formula of a precursor ion from its tandem mass (MS/MS) spectrum is the first step in identifying an unknown small molecule. Existing methods trade recall, whether the correct formula is among the candidates, against the cost of examining each candidate. Methods that examine each candidate in depth must first shorten the list, by limiting element counts or truncating it, and that is where the correct formula is lost. End-to-end regressors are fast but guarantee neither validity nor recall. We present FACET, which separates deciding which formulas to consider from deciding which one to choose. A feasibility automaton builds a formula one element count at a time and admits exactly the formulas that fit the precursor mass and satisfy the ring-and-double-bond and valence constraints. Run as an exhaustive search, it enumerates the complete feasible set, so every candidate is valid and recall is fixed by the chemical constraints rather than by a trained model. A small neural scoring head then ranks every feasible formula from one pass of a pretrained spectrum encoder, so no candidate is discarded. On the NPLIB1 benchmark FACET reaches top-1 accuracies of $0.859$ with the adduct known and $0.729$ with it unknown, compared with $0.766$ and $0.660$ for the strongest established method, and its recall is the highest. On the external CASMI 2022 set its recall is $1.000$, and with the adduct unknown it is the most accurate of the methods compared.

papers.title: Graph-Covariant Bottom-Up Scale-Bridging Reconstruction of Ground and Excited States of Extended Systems
papers.abstract: We propose a hierarchical scale-bridging construction for building first principles electronic structure models of extended molecular aggregates with disorder, and its practical realization in exciton systems. The general construction, referred here as to the encapsulation, is based on a recursive operator-valued hierarchy cast in a dual graph-theoretic (discrete) and configuration-space (continuous) structure, in which variables associated with a coarser level parameterize operators governing the degrees of freedom at the next finer level in a graph-covariant, geometry-preserving fashion. In an exemplary application of this scheme, aggregate-level ground- and excited-state operators are constructed through a many-body expansion (MBE), with matrix elements evaluated in a basis comprising the aggregate ground state and local Frenkel excitations. The required monomer and dimer building blocks are obtained from DFT and TDDFT calculations, yielding aggregate-level 1-particle transition density matrices as well as Hamiltonian, dipole moment and other operators that can be evaluated at the level of the building blocks. Starting from structural models obtained from experiment or molecular dynamics, this approach generates aggregate-level operators in a bottom-up fashion without fitting parameters to spectroscopic data or performing calculations on larger system cutouts. A numerical demonstration is given for an excitonic manifold in crystalline quaterthiophene. In particular, through its intrinsic configuration-dependence encoded in the encapsulations, it will provide a bridge between static electronic structure calculations for realistic, structurally disordered aggregates and quantum or quantum-classical simulations of exciton-vibrational dynamics.

papers.title: Sentiment sensing: comparative analysis of multilingual sentiment dynamics
papers.abstract: Cross-country sentiment analysis faces three fundamental challenges: language-specific biases distort comparisons, compositional data constraints invalidate standard statistics and temporal dynamics lack rigorous testing frameworks. We introduce sentiment sensing, a framework that addresses these gaps through integrated statistical methods. By combining compositional data analysis, functional data methods, and non-parametric inference, sentiment sensing enables valid multilingual comparisons and statistically defensible detection of sentiment shifts. Our framework has been tested in two case studies, analyzing news articles from the 27 countries of the European Union on the topics of energy and artificial intelligence. Sentiment sensing focuses on multilingual sentiment analysis enabling rigorous comparative science.

papers.title: Stochastic Euler Products in the Paley-Wiener Space
papers.abstract: General sufficient conditions, in terms of stochastic Euler products, are given for a realization of a point process to have finite excess or finite deficiency in the Paley-Wiener space.

papers.title: J-Anchor: Defending Against Prefill Attacks via J-Space Selective Refusal Restoration
papers.abstract: Prefill jailbreaks can cause safety-aligned language models to continue an unsafe assistant prefix even when they would refuse the same request under normal decoding. We study how the model's internal harmfulness and refusal signals evolve along this attacker-controlled trajectory. Using the Jacobian lens, we track vocabulary-grounded harmfulness and refusal signals from the assistant header through prefilling and subsequent generation. We identify a characteristic phenomenon, which we call refusal-state erosion: both the refusal signal and the harmfulness signal weaken as the prefill progresses, but the refusal signal progressively declines to the benign baseline by the end of the prefill, while the harmfulness signal remains above its benign baseline and detectable during subsequent generation. Motivated by this observation, we introduce J-Anchor, a training-free inference-time defense that uses the model's pre-attack harmfulness and refusal signals as a request-specific anchor and selectively restores weakened refusal in J-space during prefilling and decoding. J-Anchor substantially reduces attack success under both fixed and deep prefill attacks across different model families. J-Anchor largely preserves benign behavior and reasoning ability, and ablations highlight the importance of targeted restoration in the J-space refusal subspace. Our results suggest that preserving latent refusal dynamics offers a promising route to robust defense against prefill jailbreaks.

papers.title: Bilinear Hulls for Support Splitting: Characterization, Optimization, and Applications
papers.abstract: Sendrier's Support Splitting Algorithm (SSA) is the standard solver for the Permutation Equivalence Problem (PEP); its cost is dominated by a term that grows exponentially in the hull dimension. We study, mathematically, how much this cost can be lowered by replacing the standard inner product, on which the hull is defined, with an alternative bilinear form. Two structural results give a complete answer: only a narrow two-parameter family of bilinear forms produces a hull on which SSA can still operate, namely those whose matrix in the standard basis is a linear combination of the identity and the all-ones matrix; and even within this family the hull dimension drops by at most one (with the reduction achieved on every self-dual code whose length is coprime to the field characteristic). Together, these results give a tight upper bound: since SSA on a code with hull dimension $h$ has cost dominated by $q^h$, replacing the standard hull with $\mathrm{Hull}_M$ lowers this dominant term from $q^h$ to at best $q^{h-1}$, so no bilinear-form generalization of the inner product can reduce the SSA cost by more than a factor of $q$, the field size. Going beyond this requires invariants outside the bilinear framework. As an application, we verify that PEP-based SPECK admits the factor-$q$ cost reduction, while LEP-based LESS and PKP-based PERK lie outside our framework. A SageMath implementation of the bilinear-hull preprocessing confirms feasibility at SPECK's recommended length $n = 252$.

papers.title: Floods and the Duplication of Production: Evidence from the Global Car Industry
papers.abstract: Floods are becoming more frequent and can disrupt global supply chains. We study how multinational car makers adapt vehicle and key parts production to flood risk, and how their choices interact with insurance and public flood defences. Using plant-level data and a manually verified flood record in a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that car makers duplicate production rather than move it away from flooded plants. Even more than five years after a flood, an engine is 19 percentage points more likely to be made in two or more plants, usually abroad and for cars assembled nearby, while the flooded plant's output shows no persistent decline beyond a temporary loss in the flood year. Firms duplicate only where adjustment costs are low, i.e. when a plant of theirs abroad already makes the same engine family. Flooded vehicle model versions are duplicated only temporarily, and transmission programs are not duplicated. Suggestive evidence that firms duplicate more where insurance is likely expensive and plants lack flood defences points to substitution between redundancy, insurance and public protection.

papers.title: Theoretical estimation of nonlinear response function and ultrafast optical spectroscopy of nitrogen vacancy centers
papers.abstract: The theoretical description of the ultrafast optical response of nitrogen-vacancy centers has traditionally been developed using the nonlinear response function formalism based on a displaced harmonic oscillator model. However, restrictive defect geometries that lead to rich phonon mode distributions can limit the validity of this model. Here, we extend this framework by incorporating state-dependent oscillator modes characterized by different frequencies. We demonstrate that, as a consequence, the nonlinear response function is modified by a straightforward correction term that can be evaluated using operator algebraic techniques. These modifications directly impact two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy, which serves as a vital characterization tool for color centers by resolving ultrafast correlated electron-vibrational dynamics.

papers.title: Floquet engineering of quantum relaxation
papers.abstract: Dynamical decoupling suppresses decoherence by averaging selected interactions between a quantum system and its environment. Here, we extend this notion through a general Floquet formalism that maps periodic control onto relaxation and dephasing channels. Environmental fluctuations are decomposed into Floquet components that sample the noise spectrum at distinct frequencies, with coupling strengths determined by control-induced Floquet coefficients. We experimentally investigate this approach using a single nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond under multi-pulse control. By tuning the drive and detuning, we reshape the coupling to environmental fluctuations and create isolated operating points where the dominant decoherence channel vanishes, strongly suppressing Floquet dephasing. The resulting coherence enhancement follows the predicted Floquet coupling coefficients and can be shifted by modifying the control sequence. These results establish Floquet driving as a general framework for engineering transverse and longitudinal relaxation through the design of quantum control protocols.

papers.title: Trajectory Design and User Scheduling for Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: Finite antenna movement speed introduces repositioning delays that can limit the performance gains of pinching-antenna systems. In this paper, a trajectory based scheme is proposed for a time division multiple access (TDMA) based pinching-antenna system, allowing transmission during both movement and stationary operation. A discrete-time model is developed to characterize periodic antenna trajectories and antenna-user service association under practical movement constraints. For a single-waveguide scenario, the expected average achievable rate is derived. The rate loss relative to instantaneous positioning and the rate improvement over a fixed antenna are further analyzed, with an upper bound on the former and a lower bound on the latter established. To improve fairness among users, a minimum average rate maximization problem is formulated through joint trajectory design and user scheduling. To address the coupling between these variables, an alternating optimization (AO) framework is adopted. Specifically, a successive convex approximation (SCA) based algorithm is developed using concave rate lower bounds, while a game based scheduling algorithm employs an ordered user-rate vector as the common utility. The convergence of the SCA objective value and the finite termination and stability of the scheduling algorithm are established. Simulation results demonstrate the gains achieved by the joint design and show that the proposed system can approach instantaneous-positioning performance under finite antenna movement speed.

papers.title: Before the First Bond: Depletion-Assisted Stochastic Capture at the Onset of Endocytosis
papers.abstract: In a crowded extracellular environment, viruses and nanoparticles must reach the cell membrane within a few nanometers before the first ligand-receptor bond can form. Crowders generate an entropic depletion attraction, yet continuum models usually assume contact is already established or treat the approach deterministically. We formulate a thermodynamically consistent stochastic theory for this pre-contact stage. The sphere-plane depletion geometry uses the exact Asakur-Oosawa spherical-cap overlap, rather than a fitted cap, with either ideal van 't Hoff or pressure-only Carnahan-Starling osmotic pressure. A spatially varying near-wall mobility introduces a noise-induced drift that is essential for thermodynamic consistency and is often omitted. The first specific reaction is modeled by a Robin radiation boundary; the outer boundary is reflecting or absorbing. Three first-passage problems are solved analytically by quadrature: the mean reaction time, the reaction-before-escape probability, and the conditional success time, the last encoded by a Doob transform that exposes the selection bias of conditioning on capture. The theory separates thermodynamic inputs from conditional parameters and reveals a reaction-limited to diffusion-limited crossover controlled by the local Damköhler number. For typical virus and nanoparticle parameters, the depletion well reaches $2$-$6\,k_{\rm B}T$, capture times are $0.1$-$1\,{\rm ms}$, and the conditional success time is measurably shorter than the unconditional mean. Finite-volume and Chebyshev schemes reproduce the analytic results within their discretization errors and satisfy the radiation-boundary mass balance. This provides a quantitative theoretical framework for crowding-assisted capture prior to membrane wrapping and a reference for comparing crowding, near-wall mobility, and surface reactivity in endocytosis.

papers.title: Introducing Aurora: A New Black Hole Seeding Model With Explicit Environmental Coupling
papers.abstract: We present Aurora, a black hole seeding module for the Mimic semi-analytic framework, in which the seed mass of each newly resolved halo is set by its environment. Motivated by evidence that early quiescent galaxies and overmassive black holes assemble in dense environments, Aurora replaces the fixed seed masses of conventional prescriptions with a continuous spectrum, coupling the seed mass to two environmental parameters, the local overdensity and the radial skewness of the surrounding haloes, and to the halo mass at seeding. Requiring only halo masses and positions, it applies to dark-matter-only simulations. Calibrated against Sage on the Millennium merger trees, this prescription leaves a lasting signal. Massive black holes are assembled from the seeds of many progenitors, seeds supplying 29 per cent of all black hole mass formed by $z=0$. A seed-dominated growth pathway, distinct from the accretion-dominated majority, emerges among galaxies assembled rapidly in dense, asymmetric environments. Environment-dependent seeding raises the quiescent fraction of seeded galaxies in massive haloes at $z \simeq 3.1$ by up to 70 per cent, with the excess concentrated in overdense environments, and a deficit in voids. Scrambling the seeding environments while preserving the mass spectrum erases this gradient. The two environmental couplings imprint separable signatures, broadening the scatter of the galaxy-black hole mass relation while preserving the stellar-halo mass relation and other Sage summary statistics. We discuss applying Aurora at gigaparsec scales and higher resolution, to understand the origins of massive black hole systems in contemporary deep surveys.

papers.title: Hidden selection rules and amplitude ceilings in quantum Fourier models
papers.abstract: Quantum models with Pauli data encodings compute trigonometric polynomials whatever channels, ancillas and outcome-averaged measurements follow, so their expressivity depends on the Fourier coefficients a circuit can reach. We identify two kinds of structure that settle this before training. An antiunitary time-reversal rule and a unitary reflection rule remove frequencies. For gate-level circuits, deciding whether such a rule exists reduces to a linear system over GF(2), solvable in polynomial time, and the time-reversal rule holds in 17.6% of 6,120 configurations of standard templates. Single-upload encodings cap the top coefficient at $2^{-m}$ for every channel, and we compute the tight ceiling for every frequency and a depth-independent re-uploading bound. Frozen before training, these bounds were never violated on a non-linearity benchmark, and they predicted trained performance on real data. On IBM processors the rule held on a 65-qubit chain, and we switched rule-breaking relaxation noise on and off by design.

papers.title: Accuracy Is Not Risk: Why Medical AI Should Not Report Only Its Most Likely Label
papers.abstract: Background. Many medical AI models are trained to reproduce a single reference label and hand the most likely label to the next step in a clinical workflow. A classifier can select that label correctly while providing an inadequate summary for estimating downstream risk. Methods. We use Jeffrey's rule of conditioning to specify when probabilities over intermediate states, such as diagnoses or imaging categories, can be carried forward to an outcome risk. We separate two errors of reporting only the most likely label, discarding the probability of the other states and applying the risk of patients who have the leading diagnosis to a patient who only probably has it. We also give conditions under which the label and the full distribution lead to the same decision, and we propose guardrails for device developers, regulatory reviewers, and health insurers. Results. In a hypothetical chest-pain differential, reporting only the benign leading diagnosis greatly understates the patient's risk of death or cardiac arrest, so a patient who warrants evaluation could be discharged or denied imaging. In a hypothetical BI-RADS example, the most likely category is "probably benign," yet the propagated malignancy risk exceeds the ceiling that defines that category. Conclusions. A predicted label is not an observed state, and a calibrated classifier is not automatically a valid outcome model. Clinical and insurance coverage decisions should rest on the patient's outcome risk, judged against a threshold justified by the consequences of acting and not acting. Developers should state what each model output means and check that every step between the model and the decision preserves the patient's risk.

papers.title: Heavy quark thermalization using phonon-heavy quark EFT
papers.abstract: The description of heavy quarks inside the QGP medium, especially at low momenta, remains challenging from first principles, due to large coupling strength and gluon occupation numbers. An alternative way to formulate a description in terms of perturbative degrees of freedom is the interaction of the heavy quarks with the collective excitations of the medium in the form of phonons. This description is derived as an effective field theory (EFT) and therefore allows for a natural occurring power counting of the allowed interactions. This EFT has already been established in our previous work, where we have derived the phonon-heavy quark interactions and calculated their thermal scattering cross section. In this work, we use these results, together with the heavy quark expansion, to calculate the heavy quark drag coefficient. Subsequently, we compare our results with the drag coefficient obtained from AdS/CFT calculations to determine the previously unknown Wilson coefficients for the quark-phonon coupling. Finally, we will use these coefficients to solve the Boltzmann equation for the heavy quark distribution, studying its thermalization in the QGP via soft phonon interactions.

papers.title: Maximum purity of absolutely separable and absolutely PPT states in qutrit--qudit systems
papers.abstract: A bipartite state is absolutely positive partial transpose (APPT) if it remains PPT under every global unitary transformation, and absolutely separable if it remains separable. For every qutrit--qudit system $\mathbb{C}^3\otimes\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge3$, we prove that the maximum purity is the same for absolutely separable and APPT states and equals $\max\{(3n+8)/(3n+2)^2,\,3/(8n)\}$. The maximizing ordered spectrum is unique and contains exactly two distinct eigenvalues: the larger one has multiplicity one for $3\le n\le8$ and multiplicity $n$ for $n\ge9$. We also derive, in terms of the purity, an upper bound on the minimum partial-transpose eigenvalue achievable by global unitary transformations, and characterize all states for which the bound is attained. These results confirm the inscribed-polytope purity conjecture of Ahiable, Kothakonda, and Winter for all qutrit--qudit systems. They also give a lower bound, sharp over explicit purity ranges, on the global depolarizing noise needed for absolute separability or APPT.

papers.title: Lightest-mass suppression and weaker Majorana cancellation in Froggatt--Nielsen textures
papers.abstract: The effective Majorana mass is the length of a sum of three complex electron-flavour contributions. A mass-generation model determines both their sizes and how they cancel. We compare direct effective coefficients with a three-right-handed-neutrino seesaw measure at fixed Froggatt--Nielsen charges and common lepton conditions. In the normal-ordering benchmark truncated-normal ensemble, seesaw generation lowers the lightest-mass median by a factor of 3.2 while raising the effective-mass median by 13\%. A comparison reweighted to a common lightest-mass distribution locates nearly all of the coherent mean-square increase in weaker destructive solar-pair interference. In a fixed-amplitude phase-exchange control, the response follows the conditional phase law. A second texture exposes the competing spectral effect: smaller amplitudes can outweigh weaker cancellation in the original mean square. The interference information also affects how a prediction can be used. Replacing induced phases by independent uniform phases at unchanged posterior masses and electron weights raises the benchmark direct median by 29\%. The matrix ensemble therefore predicts a joint arrangement of amplitudes and phases whose coherent information is lost when only masses and electron-flavour weights are retained.

papers.title: Accelerating posterior sampling in Bayesian inverse problems with diffusion models: an online-offline perspective
papers.abstract: Bayesian inverse problems require both informative prior models and computationally feasible posterior inference. Score-based diffusion models provide expressive learned priors, but their use for inversion introduces a conditioning problem: the score of a noised posterior is generally unavailable from a prior score alone. This selective survey reviews the principal approaches to that problem, including likelihood guidance, spectral and projection methods, sequential Monte Carlo corrections, and amortized conditional training. We organize methods by how they split cost between offline preparation and online inference, and compare their assumptions, advantages and limitations, with emphasis on computational speedups. Some ongoing directions and open questions are gathered at the end.

papers.title: Exponential suppression of bit-flip errors in dissipative cat qubits
papers.abstract: We study the infinite-dimensional Lindblad generator $L_ε=D[a^2-α^2]+εD[a]$, describing a dissipative cat qubit subject to single-photon loss. For sufficiently large $α$ and sufficiently small $ε>0$, we identify a two-dimensional spectral subspace near zero and establish an upper bound on the slow decay rate that decreases exponentially with $α^2$, uniformly in $ε$. This proves exponential suppression of bit-flip errors.

papers.title: From First Bond to Stable Adhesion: Multivalent Bond Stabilization in Receptor-Mediated Endocytosis
papers.abstract: After a particle forms its first receptor--ligand bond near a cell membrane, stable attachment often requires a threshold number of additional bonds. This paper develops a biophysical kinetic theory of this post-capture stage. The bond-number dynamics are modeled as a finite birth--death chain on $n=0,1,\dots,m$, where $0$ is loss of the initial bond and $m$ is the stabilization threshold. The mesoscopic rates $λ_n$ and $μ_n$ encode the local energy landscape, accessible receptor--ligand pairs, steric and orientational constraints, and cooperative interactions within the growing cluster. The probability of reaching the threshold before losing the first bond is derived in closed form for general rates and, in the constant-ratio case, reduces to a geometric series controlled by the free-energy bias $ρ_n=μ_n/λ_n$. The mean time to failure or stabilization follows from a tridiagonal backward equation. Conditioning on successful attachment is treated as a trajectory-selection effect: the conditioned chain is a Doob $h$-transform whose dissociation rate at $n=1$ vanishes, because successful trajectories cannot lose the first bond early. A minimal interface between the spatial first-capture probability and the bond-number chain is formulated, together with the conditions under which the stable capture probability factorizes into their product. The analysis shows that hitting probabilities constrain only the rate ratios, whereas the absolute rate scale requires time-resolved or dwell-time data. The threshold $m$ is a model-defined stabilization criterion, not a directly measured ligand count. The rates and threshold are effective parameters specified independently or inferred from kinetic data. The theory provides a quantitative framework for interpreting attachment probabilities, lifetimes, and the transition from first bond formation to stable multivalent adhesion.

papers.title: Model-Based Fast Calibration for a Nitrogen Vacancy Center QPU
papers.abstract: We present a simulation-informed calibration workflow for NV quantum processing units that combines a digital twin, optimal control pulses, and a Fisher-information-guided experiment design into an iterative parameter estimation feedback loop. We find that using this framework, we obtain the same calibration precision as standard techniques with up to 4x reduction in measurement time.

papers.title: An analytical model to explain under which conditions home batteries create new load peaks in the local grid
papers.abstract: Simulation studies find that price-responsive home batteries and electric vehicles create new load peaks in low-voltage grids; with endogenous wholesale prices most of these peaks disappear. This paper explains both findings with an analytical model of the coincident peak at the transformer. The model is algebraic and solved in closed form, so the parameters that determine whether a new peak emerges and how large it becomes can be identified; they are few. The peak is the background load in the critical hour plus the charging of the local fleet. Under exogenous prices the charging equals the rated power of the fleet. Under endogenous prices the national fleet fills the trough of residual load until the price is flat; the depth of the fill follows from an energy balance in which the price function does not appear. For a V-shaped trough the local charging peak is the share of the grid in national flexibility times the square root of flank gradient times national flexibility. Rated power, price level, network charge and market size do not enter. The model reproduces simulated peaks for a German case within a few percent.

papers.title: The Prodigal Elephant Returns: Last-Return Laws in the Superdiffusive Regime
papers.abstract: Let $(S_n)$ be the one-dimensional elephant random walk with memory parameter $p\in(3/4,1)$ and first-step probability $q=\mathbb{P}(S_1=1)\in[0,1]$. Set $a=2p-1$, and let $f_{q,a}$ denote the density of the almost-sure limit of $S_n/n^a$. We prove that the last return time $T_0=\sup\{m\geq0:S_m=0\}$ satisfies: $\mathbb{P}(T_0\geq n)\sim f_{q,a}(0)\sqrt{\frac{8}{π(2a-1)}}n^{-(a-1/2)}$. Reflection gives $f_{q,a}(0)=f_{1,a}(0)$, so the constant is independent of $q$. For future walks started from admissible states $(n,x_n)$ with $x_n/\sqrt n\to z$, we establish functional convergence of the centered martingale-normalized paths to a time-changed Brownian motion. Uniform control of late hitting times then gives the eventual-return kernel $2Φ(-\sqrt{2a-1}|z|)$, uniformly on bounded scaled windows, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The same last-visit asymptotic holds uniformly for nonempty deterministic targets $F_n\subseteq[-r_n,r_n]\cap\mathbb{Z}$, $r_n=o(\sqrt n)$, held fixed during each trajectory. Conditionally on $T_0\geq n$, we identify the joint limit of $S_n/\sqrt n$, the next return divided by $n$, and the last return divided by the next return. The last ratio converges to $A^{-1/(2a-1)}$, independently of the other two limiting coordinates, where $A$ has the arcsine distribution on $(0,1)$.

papers.title: Programmable Droplets as Active Matter in a Reconfigurable Environment
papers.abstract: Exploring systems that bridge the gap between non living and living matter requires a reconfigurable environment coupled to synthetic systems capable of autonomous motion, adaptive behaviour and persistent dynamics. Self propelled droplets provide a minimal platform for such life like behaviour, but quantitative measures capturing both persistence and adaptability to enable closed loop reconfiguration remain lacking. Here we introduce an autonomous closed loop robotic platform to characterise and dynamically program the autonomous behaviour of multicomponent oil in water droplets. We explored two chemical composition spaces, with and without external pH perturbations, analysing droplet behaviour in real time and iteratively selecting formulations. To quantify this behaviour, we introduce two descriptors, persistence and diversity. Persistence is quantified by mapping temporal dynamics in a speed shape complexity space, where we identify a persistence domain that distinguishes active from inactive droplets. Diversity captures spontaneous or environmentally induced variation in motion and the propensity of droplets to reorient or adapt under perturbation. We show that persistence and diversity are constrained by a behavioural trade off: high persistence limits diversity, whereas high diversity reduces persistent activity. Our results provide a quantitative framework for navigating and programming life like behaviours in active droplets and show how closed-loop experimentation can uncover organising principles in complex active matter.

papers.title: Strong gravity physics of dynamical horizons in black hole mergers and its imprint in their gravitational radiation
papers.abstract: In a binary black hole merger, the inspiral portion of the gravitational waveform corresponds to two distinct horizons orbiting each other, and the merger and ringdown signals correspond to the final horizon being formed and settling down to equilibrium. However, we still lack a detailed understanding of the relation between the horizon geometry in these three regimes and the observed waveform. In this thesis, we show that the well-known inspiral chirp waveform has a clear counterpart on black hole horizons, namely the shear of the outgoing null rays at the horizon. The shear behaves very much like a compact binary coalescence waveform with increasing frequency and amplitude, and the parameters of the system estimated from the horizon agree with those estimated from the waveform. We then track the source multipole moments of the dynamical horizons in simulations of several binary black hole mergers and calculate the corresponding Love numbers for axisymmetric modes. Unlike the (field) tidal Love numbers of non-spinning black holes, these do not vanish. We present evidence that, at least for modest mass ratios, their behaviour is universal.
