In both examples the singular Green function is precisely the perturbative expansion of the Hadamard parametrix; the additional logarithms arise from momentum-singular homogeneous data. For the exactly soluble first profile, the standard flat-normalized plane-wave prescription gives a vanishing renormalized stress tensor away from the impulsive surface. Smooth-front regularizations of both profiles reproduce, at the calculated orders and away from the characteristic zero mode, the singular structure of the matched impulsive propagators without generating inverse transverse-momentum poles.

papers.title: First Light with the Dark100 Array of PANOSETI Telescopes at Palomar Observatory
papers.abstract: Dark100 is the first phase of an extensive array of Panoramic SETI (PANOSETI) telescopes at Palomar Observatory, California. PANOSETI telescopes are small, 0.5-m Fresnel lens telescopes instrumented with 1024-pixel silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) cameras. The telescopes were originally designed to search for ultra-fast optical transients, but they also function as cost-effective imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs). Dark100 will use seven of these widely separated IACTs to map the ultra-high-energy (UHE) gamma-ray sources on the Galactic Plane at high resolution. Dark100 will also leverage the IACT technique to search for evidence of ultra-heavy dark matter in a mass range that extends beyond 100 TeV. Deployment of the first four telescopes and enclosures was completed in December 2025, and commissioning of the next three is scheduled to finish by the end of 2026. The array has so far collected more than 100 hours of 3-telescope data on sources including the Crab Nebula and Markarian 421. Here we present the current status of Dark100.

papers.title: Color transparency effects on the deuteron spin observables in the hard $pd \to ppn$ reaction
papers.abstract: The pionless breakup of a deuteron induced by 15 GeV/$c$ beam proton is considered theoretically in the kinematics where both outgoing protons are fast and the neutron is slow in the rest frame of the deuteron. Significant influence of color transparency on the deuteron vector and tensor analyzing powers is expected.

papers.title: RFLocMatch: Reference-Conditioned Residual Learning from Angle-Delay Spectra for Accurate Localization
papers.abstract: Radio fingerprint localization supports mobile robots and location-aware services when satellite positioning is unreliable. Angle-delay power fingerprints capture power distributions over angles and delays, but localization remains vulnerable to spatial ambiguity and measurement perturbations. Reflections and blockage can produce similar fingerprints at distant locations, while noise in query fingerprints can alter query-reference rankings despite a clean reference library. These effects can place a distant reference first in the ranking, creating tail errors. Similarity scores can generate plausible candidates, but reliable selection requires candidate-specific residual evidence and comparison across alternatives. This separation motivates RFLocMatch, which uses complementary joint and link-specific matching to preserve candidate locations supported by different links. Reference-conditioned residual learning then scores each candidate using the query and reference fingerprints, their absolute difference, and their element-wise product, while candidate-context modeling compares alternatives. Tail-focused training emphasizes costly errors, and inference replaces the initial match only when a candidate's score advantage exceeds a validation-calibrated threshold. On ray-tracing-generated data, RFLocMatch reduces dual-transmitter 99th-percentile error by 75.2% under link and receiver perturbations relative to the best-performing baseline. On real-world single-transmitter channel impulse response (CIR) measurements with motion-assisted angular-spectrum estimation, it attains 8.25-m 90th-percentile error and 3.83-m mean absolute error.

papers.title: Feasibility of Common-Stream-Only Sensing in ZF-RSMA with Imperfect CSIT
papers.abstract: Reusing the Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) common stream for sensing eliminates dedicated probing signals in Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC), but creates a feasibility bottleneck: the common-power fraction must simultaneously support common decoding, private decoding, and target detection. This paper investigates this tradeoff in downlink zero-forcing RSMA with imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). With the common beam fixed over a sensing dwell through sensing geometry, the common-power fraction becomes the sole design variable. We prove that the communication-feasible set is either a closed interval or empty. Analytical outage expressions localize these endpoints, revealing a high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) floor-ceiling effect: common decoding dictates a common-power floor, while imperfect CSIT and SIC impose a private-decoding ceiling. For sensing, the conditional detection constraint is affine, preserving the interval structure. A geometry-matched common beam ensures monotonic detection improvement, reducing joint-feasibility check to the communication-feasible upper endpoint. Simulations validate our analysis, identifying regimes where common-stream-only sensing is viable.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Emission from LS 5039: A 30-500 GeV Excess and Phase-Resolved Broadband Spectral Modeling
papers.abstract: LS~5039 is a well-studied $γ$-ray binary exhibiting strong orbital modulation from GeV to TeV energies. We present a phase-resolved analysis of 17.3~yr of \textit{Fermi}-LAT observations and identify an additional $γ$-ray excess in the $\sim30$--$500$~GeV at a significance of $\sim7.9σ$. The phase-resolved spectra show pronounced orbital dependence above $\sim10$~GeV, with the inferior-conjunction more complex than the superior-conjunction. To investigate the broadband spectral energy distribution, we combine the \textit{Fermi}-LAT spectra with published H.E.S.S.\ and HAWC measurements and compare purely leptonic and lepto-hadronic models using the Bayesian information criterion. In both intervals, relativistic-Maxwellian and magnetospheric components dominate below $\sim10$~GeV, while shock-accelerated electrons account for much of the GeV--TeV continuum. The purely leptonic fits leave residuals at $30$--$500$~GeV and underpredict the HAWC measurements above $\sim100$~TeV. In the local one-zone intrabinary shock apex model, synchrotron cooling and Klein-Nishina suppression make the ultra-high-energy emission difficult to reproduce, although more complex leptonic scenarios remain possible. Adding a phenomenological proton component improves the broadband description, with stronger relative support during superior-conjunction than inferior-conjunction. However, the proton parameters remain weakly constrained and the fast-escape hadronic interpretation is energetically challenging, so a hadronic origin is not uniquely established. Future high-sensitivity, phase-resolved observations at multi-TeV and ultra-high energies will be required to test this interpretation.

papers.title: $K$-tropical curves, Riemann-Roch and Serre duality
papers.abstract: We endow a tropical curve with the structure of a ringed space and establish analogues of Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for these ringed spaces. As a corollary, we give a cohomological proof of the tropical Riemann-Roch theorem.

papers.title: Long-term variability of the 35-day cycle in Her X-1
papers.abstract: Her X-1 is an eclipsing X-ray binary system consisting of an accreting neutron star and an optical component HZ Her. In addition to the 1.24-s X-ray pulsations and the 1.7-d orbital period, the system also shows a 35-day X-ray variability related to the precessional motion of a tilted and twisted accretion disk around the neutron star. The long-term persistence of the 35-day X-ray variability suggests the presence of a stable clock mechanism, most likely free precession of the magnetized neutron star. We have studied the long-term behavior of the 35-day cycle of Her X-1 using all available CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, MAXI data and archival turn-on moments of the 35-day cycle spanning more than 50 years. We have used a sliding-window averaged X-ray phase light curve and the classical O-C (observed minus calculated) diagram for individual 35-day turn-ons to inspect the long-term trends of the O-C diagram. The O-C diagram demonstrates two similar parabolic trends separated by an anomalous low state (ALS) of the source suggesting a secular decrease in the 35-d precession period with $\dot P_\text{35} =(-1.3\pm0.2)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ and $\dot P_\text{35} =(-4.7\pm0.1)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ before and after the ALS, respectively. We conclude that the decay of the 35-day period as inferred from the O-C analysis can be interpreted in terms of the direct relationship between the change of the precessional period of the accretion disk to the long-term decrease of the period of the free precessional neutron star - due to continued accumulation of accreted matter.

papers.title: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled Study of OLMo 2
papers.abstract: Whether a language model was trained on a document matters for copyright, privacy, and benchmark contamination. Yet most membership-inference (MI) evaluations on language models collect members and non-members after the fact, so success may reflect distribution shift and failure is inconclusive. We re-ran OLMo 2 1B's official 50-billion-token mid-training stage, replacing selected training chunks with documents from 7,814 pairs matched on domain and difficulty. For each pair, a coin flip determined which document was inserted and which was held out. The run released by the Allen Institute for AI (AI2) from the same seed saw identical data everywhere else and serves as the counterfactual. One exposure raises a previously unseen document's likelihood on average but rarely identifies it. Using the counterfactual as reference, the reference ratio has an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.767 but, with one threshold across domains, catches 3.8% of members at a 1% false-positive rate (FPR). In contrast, 13 matched pairs give a paired test 80% power at the 5% level to detect training on a collection, given same-domain non-members and a close reference. A reference trained with another seed recovers 92% of the counterfactual's AUC advantage over chance, whereas reference-free attacks stay within 0.07 of chance when pooled over domains. The full official post-training recipe, re-run on both models, leaves 89% of the average effect. Even with a closely matched reference, substantial document-level variability limits individual membership inference. We will release the checkpoints, per-token log-probabilities, and the evaluation documents; the code is available at https://github.com/ali-bana/OLMo-Twin.

papers.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
papers.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.

papers.title: SN 2025dys: A luminous supernova explosion from a partially stripped helium star
papers.abstract: We present well-sampled multi-band imaging and low- to medium-resolution spectroscopic observations of the early-discovered Type~II supernova (SN)~2025dys. The photometric evolution exhibits a rise time of $\sim$\,18 days ($r$ band) and a rapid decline transitioning to the radioactive decay tail at $\sim$\,70 days. SN~2025dys is among the high-luminosity events with a peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm opt}=8.57\times10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Early X-ray emission was identified, displaying a luminosity of $7.55\times10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The observational investigation points to a dense, hydrogen-rich circumstellar medium with a mass of $M_{\rm CSM}\approx0.5$--$0.7\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, suggesting a partially stripped, hydrogen-poor inner ejecta with a relatively low mass of $M_{\rm ej}\approx2.5\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The explosion possessed a kinetic energy of $E_{\rm k}\approx0.3\text{--}0.5$~foe and yielded a synthesized nickel mass of $M_{\rm Ni}\approx0.042_{-0.011}^{+0.012}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. These physical parameters indicate an extreme mass-loss episode before the explosion, characterized by a high mass-loss rate of $\dot{M} \gtrsim 0.01\,\mathrm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$. SN~2025dys represents a stripped progenitor, intrinsically resembling a Type~IIb or even a Type~Ib SN, that exploded within a dense, hydrogen-rich circumstellar environment.

papers.title: Deformations of Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms
papers.abstract: Recent work of Brantner and Taelman shows that derived deformation theory and period maps can recover strong mixed-characteristic lifting results. In this paper, we develop a prismatic version of this method for Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms, constructing compatible deformations over $A/I^n$ for every $n$ under suitable hypotheses. We also apply our method to $F$-split Calabi--Yau varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. In particular, we consider an $F$-split smooth proper variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$, with $H^{d-1}(X,O_X)=0$ and trivial canonical bundle. We show that $X$ admits a lift to $W_3(k)$.

papers.title: Relative Du Bois complexes over higher dimensional bases
papers.abstract: We extend the notion of the right relative Du Bois complex to a smooth base of arbitrary dimension. We further show that this complex satisfies base change in the sense of Kovács--Taji, for flat families with strict higher Du Bois fibers, extending the result by Ning over a smooth curve.

papers.title: Evaluating Instrument-Centered AI Agents for Table-Top Science Experiments
papers.abstract: Reliable evaluation of AI agents for table-top science experiments has remained elusive because live instruments are hard to reset and share at scale, while instrument statefulness and safety constraints complicate evaluation. We introduce instrMCP and q-devBench, an evaluation stack for instrument-centered AI agents in table-top experiments. instrMCP connects coding agents to scientific instruments through the Model Context Protocol, serving as the instrument-access harness. q-devBench reconstructs 37 real experimental tasks from condensed-matter physics as virtual QCoDeS instruments covering quantum electronic transport, scanning probe imaging, and calibration workflows. q-devBench exposes reproducible failure modes in laboratory-agent systems while preserving realistic instrument-control workflows. Across a range of commercial coding-agent configurations, current systems already show substantial operational competence, satisfying 70-83% of measurement-related rubric criteria. The main bottleneck is scientific analysis, where performance falls to 28-46%. In an analysis-only ablation in which agents receive clean reference datasets without running the virtual measurement session, analysis performance improves substantially, closing roughly two thirds of the difference between the measurement and analysis scores. This suggests that much of the deficit arises from the measurement-session context, including tool-use overhead, longer context, measurement-planning decisions, and possible acquisition errors, while a residual scientific-reasoning gap remains. Together, instrMCP and q-devBench provide a practical sandbox for benchmarking, diagnosing, and improving laboratory AI harnesses, and establish a route from controlled virtual evaluation to future live-hardware validation.

papers.title: On-the-fly $Δ$-machine learned force fields for warm dense matter using a Yukawa reference model: Application to magnesium
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for on-the-fly $Δ$-machine learned force field ($Δ$-MLFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of warm dense matter (WDM). In particular, we employ a Yukawa reference model that captures the dominant screened-Coulomb interactions between the ions, with its parameters fit on the fly to Kohn--Sham density functional theory (DFT) data, and an MLFF scheme based on the kernel method and Bayesian linear regression that learns the differences in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses between the Yukawa model and Kohn--Sham DFT. We verify the accuracy and performance of the formalism by comparing the predicted properties of warm dense carbon with Kohn--Sham DFT results in the literature. In so doing, we demonstrate that $Δ$-MLFF has significantly lower errors in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses than the standard MLFF scheme at a comparable cost, while accelerating ab initio MD simulations by up to three orders of magnitude. We apply this framework to calculate the equation of state, structure, and transport properties of magnesium at densities of 5.22 to 10.44 g/cm$^3$ and temperatures of 600 kK to 1.5 MK. We find that the pressure, self-diffusion coefficient, and shear viscosity obey power laws in temperature and density, that the dynamic structure factor exhibits a well-defined ion-acoustic mode whose negative dispersion is characteristic of strongly coupled liquids, and that the Stokes--Einstein relation holds to within 10% over the conditions considered.

papers.title: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors
papers.abstract: AI control relies on monitors to catch a capable model that sabotages its work. These monitors are evaluated on their ability to differentiate honest from backdoored code. We show that on a standard evaluation dataset, simple features beat most monitors without ever running the code, outranking 20 of 24 open-weight models prompted as monitors. The dataset gives its labels away in two ways. People wrote the honest solutions and older language models the backdoors, so the style of the code reveals the class. Additionally, problems that LLMs can backdoor have different characteristics, so basic facts about the problem reveal it too. Swapping one class at a time for code by Claude Sonnet 5 shows that these features reward a contrast between authors, since human code against Sonnet 5's backdoors is easier to separate than the original pairs, 0.95 against 0.79. One in seven backdoors in the standard test set fails our validity checks, which distorts comparisons between attackers. A Sonnet 5 monitor appears to catch 77% of the older models' backdoors but 37% of Sonnet 5's, and 78% against 61% once both are verified. We do not show that published monitors rely on these shortcuts, but our findings suggest that a high score on such a dataset is not by itself evidence of sabotage detection. We release the rebuilt dataset and checks.

papers.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
papers.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

papers.title: From fleet trajectories to single-cell promises: hierarchically weighted conformal prediction for battery SOH monitoring
papers.abstract: Interval predictions from conformal prediction are usually read as "90% coverage", but on nested battery data that number promises the fleet average, not the individual cell. We measure the gap on 124 public LFP cells under a preregistered three-tier reporting protocol (fleet, batch, cell): pooled coverage looks healthy (0.875-0.906 across splits) while the worst cell is covered 0.1-2% of the time, with exact binomial tests against the nominal level. We then repair part of the gap with a hierarchically weighted conformal engine whose weights consume only side information frozen at prediction time - signature features, batch labels, cycle indices - and never touch residuals. The preregistered repair criterion passes: 10th-percentile cell coverage moves 0.750 to 0.830 (53% of the gap), the worst cell 0.642 to 0.694, with zero deferrals and a flat sensitivity spectrum. What the engine does not repair is localized rather than left open: under protocol drift the frozen weights harm monotonically on the SOH scale (the absolute scale is reported in full), a structural dead end we report instead of tuning away; and repair capacity is bounded by calibration-pool battery diversity, measured on both datasets. On a cross-chemistry external set the calibrated intervals collapse (0.286), while the within-domain skeleton replicates (pooled 0.933, worst cell 0.686). The deliverable is a reporting protocol - three tiers of promise anchored to measured regimes, worst-cell statistics, deferral share - that makes per-cell interval claims auditable before deployment.

papers.title: Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes
papers.abstract: We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. For uniform finite inputs, we derive a controlled high-SNR expansion of the information variance and determine its limiting ratio to the mutual information deficit. The mutual information expansion specialises arbitrary input fading results and gives an explicit remainder. Standard random-coding and second-order achievability tools relate these quantities to reliability over independently faded Alamouti blocks. All alphabets preserve symbol-wise maximum-likelihood detection at the Alamouti level. Numerical energy, mutual information, and error-rate comparisons support the analysis. Centred comparisons with classical Alamouti, Golden, and Silver codes illustrate the trade-off between reliability, symbol rate, and decoding effort.

papers.title: Pair density waves via interband pairing --- a perspective from superfluid weight
papers.abstract: Pair density waves (PDW) are superconducting states that exhibit a spatially modulated pairing order parameter, corresponding to Cooper pairs carrying finite center-of-mass momentum. While some recent studies have emphasized the role of quantum geometry in stabilizing PDW order in certain multiband systems, we here present a systematic investigation of an alternative, geometry-independent mechanism: PDW order driven purely by interband Cooper pairing. Using the superfluid weight (SW) as a diagnostic, we study two canonical models. The first is the classic Fulde-Ferrell model of an $s$-wave superconductor subject to a Zeeman splitting field, which realizes pure interband pairing between two rigidly shifted bands; the second is a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor $f$-wave pairing, a modified version of which was recently found to exhibit PDW instability in density-matrix renormalization-group simulations. In both models the SW receives no quantum geometric contribution at the mean-field level, yet it can be greatly suppressed or even turn negative, signaling a tendency toward pairing with spatial phase modulations. For the first model, we establish that the SW is increasingly suppressed as the Zeeman field grows, drastically turning negative upon the emergence of extensive gapless excitations, i.e., the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. For the honeycomb $f$-wave model, we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, vanishing quantum-geometric SW and an invariably negative total SW. Our results thus establish the SW as a qualitative indicator of the tendency toward PDW order, and provide a microscopic rationale for the interband-pairing-driven PDW instability.

papers.title: A variational phase-field theory of cohesive fracture at finite deformation
papers.abstract: This paper formulates a kinematically and variationally consistent phase-field theory for cohesive fracture at finite deformation. The theory introduces an independent compliance-damage field, which accommodates both diffuse distributions and singular concentrations. The phase-field is thereby freed from the dual burden of describing crack geometry and material degradation. A rank-one additive split of the deformation gradient makes separation explicit through independent crack-strain and reference-normal fields. All fields are governed by a single principle of minimum potential energy, which consistently couples nonlinear bulk deformation, crack separation, and crack-plane rotation. One-dimensional energy comparisons show that minimization favors Dirac-type concentration of compliance damage and crack strain. Strong displacement discontinuities thus emerge naturally at a finite phase-field length without being prescribed a priori, while the phase-field remains continuous. The concentrated energy recovers the exact bulk--interface structure of a sharp-crack cohesive zone model. General objective hyperelastic bulk potentials and admissible mixed-mode cohesive laws can therefore be prescribed independently, with the nominal traction--separation law unaffected by the bulk law or phase-field length. Diffuse damage can coexist with concentrated cracks, retaining deformation modes for bulk-energy relaxation during nucleation. Two- and three-dimensional examples validate the theory across large stretches, finite rotations, and complex crack paths. Notably, the computed near-tip Cauchy stress closely matches the analytical 1/r crack-tip asymptotic solution of Long et al. (2011) outside the cohesive zone.

papers.title: Limitation of Bessel Beams in Near Field Communications: A Depth of Field Perspective
papers.abstract: Bessel beams have recently been explored as a candidate complement to focused beams in radiative near-field communications due to their non-diffracting and self-healing properties. However, recent work has shown that the practically useful range of finite-aperture Bessel beams can occupy only a fraction of the radiative near-field region, establishing the existence of a finite propagation limit. In this paper, we establish such a limitation analytically from a depth-of-field perspective for Bessel beams generated by finite circular and square apertures. To quantify the Bessel beam depth, we first derive analytical expressions for the normalized array gain and use them to establish absolute and peak-normalized $3$-dB depth-of-field criteria. These criteria reveal critical cone-angle thresholds that partition the Bessel-beam configuration space into (i) undefined, (ii) finite, and (iii) infinite depth-of-field regimes. Our analysis further reveals that the maximum usable non-diffracting range under the proposed depth-of-field criterion is limited to $\approx22\%$ and $\approx19\%$ of the Fraunhofer distance for circular and square apertures, respectively. Numerical results confirm the accuracy of the derived limits for discrete planar arrays, providing practical engineering guidelines for the design of finite-aperture Bessel beams in future near-field communications.

papers.title: Fooling Relying Parties of the EUDI Wallet Architecture: Credential Pooling Attacks and CRESTA, a Standard-Compliant Countermeasure
papers.abstract: The European Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet will let millions of EU citizens prove who they are and what they are entitled to, disclosing only what is needed. Many services need several credentials at once, such as an identity card and a university degree, so combined presentations are essential. We present credential pooling attacks on relying parties of the EUDI Wallet reference architecture. Colluding users, each holding some credentials in their own wallet, cooperate through a proxy that acts as a single synthetic user and presents all the requested credentials, although no single user holds them all. Every signature is genuine and computed by certified hardware, and nothing is extracted or forged. We ran the attack against the European Commission's reference implementation, also on two Android phones. The attack would fail if all credentials of a user carried the same public key, but colluding relying parties could then link all presentations of that user. For this reason, the Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF) requires a fresh key for each credential and recommends batches of single-use copies, each with its own key: precisely what makes pooling possible. One might think that preventing pooling requires giving up unlinkability or adopting non-standard cryptography, such as zero-knowledge proofs. We show that this is not the case: we present CRESTA (CREdential STApling), an efficient countermeasure that uses only standard cryptography and credential formats and preserves unlinkability. In CRESTA, an ordinary issuer checks at issuance that a set of keys was generated in the same secure hardware, and certifies it in a binding attestation: a standard credential whose attributes can be selectively disclosed. CRESTA works entirely within the EUDI Wallet framework and costs a relying party one additional signature verification per presentation.

papers.title: Secure Deterministic Identification with Feedback and Sensing over State-Dependent Wiretap Channels
papers.abstract: Identification differs from classical transmission in that the receiver determines whether a particular identity was sent rather than recovering a message. We study secure deterministic identification over state-dependent discrete memoryless wiretap channels with private noiseless feedback and a sensing distortion constraint. The encoder has no local randomness and uses only the identity and past feedback. A symbol-wise input restriction guarantees the sensing constraint. We show that the secure deterministic identification capacity equals its non-secure feedback counterpart when the admissible main channel has positive ordinary transmission capacity and H(Y|Z,X=x)>0 for some fixed admissible input x. This equality does not require positive classical wiretap secrecy capacity. For achievability, noiseless feedback generates common randomness for identification and enables secret-key extraction by privacy amplification. The extracted key one-time-pad encrypts a short identification tag, whose reliable transmission requires only a sublinear number of additional channel uses. We also present an alternative construction in which feedback-generated randomness replaces the local randomization of a stochastic wiretap encoder. We further prove that secure identification capacity vanishes whenever non-secure identification capacity is zero. We also identify a class of channels with input-independent wiretapper observations that achieves full non-secure identification capacity even when the private conditional feedback entropy is zero, illustrated by a binary state-dependent wiretap channel. Thus, feedback can support both identification and secrecy without local encoder randomization while satisfying sensing constraints.

papers.title: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term
papers.abstract: We study the rapid-turn regime of multifield cosmology coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. We derive the corresponding modified relations between the inflationary Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, in the two-field case. These relations show that including the Gauss-Bonnet coupling broadens the possibilities for realizing rapid turn inflation and for satisfying the swampland conjectures. We also derive a consistency condition relating the scalar field-space metric to the scalar potential and the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, which two-field slow-roll and rapid-turn inflationary solutions have to satisfy. Finally, we find general conditions under which phantom-like behavior is possible in multifield dark energy models coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. Notably, although we do not consider a direct interaction between dark matter and dark energy, dark matter is crucial for the occurrence of a phantom regime.

papers.title: Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks
papers.abstract: Biochemical networks propagate the signals that regulate cellular behaviour, and which routes carry them depends on cellular context: a shift in context rewires the network's effective dynamics. Mechanistic simulators are misspecified here because the effective dynamics emerge from an interaction structure that is only partially known. Model discovery instead learns the dynamics from data, but sparse, correlated measurements poorly identify a full network model. What matters is narrower: the portion the context rewires. We introduce conditionally coarse-grained ODEs (Co$^2$ODE), which model that portion as a sparse neural or symbolic ODE: a conditional mask selects the markers carrying the rewiring, and a variational autoencoder compresses the remaining markers into a learnt closure term. On single-cell phosphoproteomic data spanning 30 cancer-relevant overexpressions, Co$^2$ODE compresses a 30-marker panel into a 10-dimensional state while matching the predictive accuracy of a neural ODE fit to the full panel. The closure absorbs what the mask drops, hence the accuracy is insensitive to which markers are kept. Adding a prior score to the loss shifts the selected markers at no cost in fit, indicating the data are not interventional enough to identify the underlying biology.

papers.title: Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids
papers.abstract: We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.

papers.title: An approximate separation of the electron and positron degrees of freedom in the Dirac-Heisenberg-Wigner formalism
papers.abstract: Here we study the quantum relativistic phase-space description of the Dirac field referred to as the Dirac--Heisenberg--Wigner (DHW) formalism. By applying a systematic expansion procedure in weak electromagnetic fields (compared to the Schwinger critical field) and slow temporal and long spatial scales (compared to the Compton scales), the 16 scalar phase-space functions of the DHW equations can be reduced to 8 scalars. By making a further change of variables, the equations can be interpreted as four evolution equations for the electron degrees of freedom and four for the positron degrees of freedom. We refer to these equations as the weakly coupled electron-positron (WCEP) limit of the DHW equations. Unlike the case after a Foldy--Wouthuysen transformation has been made, the electron and positron degrees of freedom remain weakly coupled. Naturally, further approximations can be made on the 4+4 equations so that only 4 equations for one particle species remain. Importantly, the expansion scheme can be carried out to all orders, in which case the reduced 4+4 model, contrary to other reduced models, will cover most quantum relativistic effects. Specifically, this includes vacuum polarization, a phenomenon that otherwise has been added phenomenologically, but here appears naturally as a feature of the general expansion scheme.

papers.title: Counting kinks and magnons with the lattice: magnetoelastic effects in Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$
papers.abstract: We report low-temperature dilatometry and ultrasound measurements on the frustrated quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnet Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$ across the entire cascade of field-induced magnetic phase transitions. The whole phase diagram can be recovered from these lattice probes, with distinct anomalies observed at each phase boundary. Elongation along the principal chain axis is found to closely track magnetization throughout the phase diagram. This behavior is interpreted in terms of kinks in the Néel structure and magnons in the transverse-ordered magnetic-BEC phases, each carrying a fixed lattice distortion. A simultaneous analysis of ultrasound and striction data allows us to quantify the strength of magnetoelastic coupling.

papers.title: Static and dynamic density correlations of interacting active Brownian particles
papers.abstract: We develop a stochastic Dean--Kawasaki field theory to predict the static structure factor and collective intermediate scattering function of interacting active Brownian particles. Starting from the microscopic overdamped dynamics, we derive coupled stochastic equations for the density and polarization fields using an angular-moment closure. Gaussian linearization then yields closed analytical expressions for static and dynamic density correlations in terms of propulsion speed, mean number density, interaction potential, translational and rotational diffusivities. The coupling between density and polarization predicts a crossover from exponential relaxation to damped oscillations despite the absence of inertia. For Gaussian-core potential, the predictions contain no fitting parameters. Brownian dynamics simulations show quantitative agreement at low activity and long wavelengths, and reproduce the crossover behaviour. For Weeks--Chandler--Andersen potential, the nonintegrable core makes both the Fourier transform of the potential and the self-interaction correction term in the Dean--Kawasaki field theory ill-defined. We therefore introduce an approximation that replaces the interaction potential with a passive direct-correlation function fitted separately at each density and temperature. This approximation requires no additional activity-dependent fitting parameters.

papers.title: Dynamic-Aware LC-DMA Beam Tracking for LEO Satellite Communications
papers.abstract: Liquid crystal (LC)-based dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) offer a power-efficient, low-cost, and scalable solution for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications where large apertures are needed to compensate for large path loss in the Earth-satellite link. However, beam tracking with LC-DMAs is governed by two coupled dynamics: the required time-varying beam direction caused by user and satellite mobility, and the finite response time of the LC phase shifters. This raises the question of whether LC-DMAs can reconfigure sufficiently fast to support high-mobility LEO satellite links. To address this problem, we develop a dynamic-aware beam-tracking framework that explicitly accounts for both dynamics. In particular, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the cumulative received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over a predictive tracking horizon subject to the physical dynamics of the LC unit cells as well as transmit power constraints. To solve this non-convex problem efficiently, we develop an alternating optimization framework combining a closed-form maximum ratio transmission (MRT) digital precoder and maximum ratio combining (MRC) with a parallel, closed-form dynamic-aware phase-shift update. Simulation results show that when the time response of LC-DMAs is properly accounted for, it can support practical mobility scenarios. Moreover, the proposed dynamic-aware algorithm maintains stable SNR and outperforms conventional designs, particularly at high vehicle velocities and low orbital azimuth angles.

papers.title: Hierarchy of Electromagnetic Gauge Field Quantum Geometries
papers.abstract: The conventional Bloch quantum geometric tensor (QGT) describes electric-dipole geometry for spatially uniform perturbations and vertical Bloch transitions. We develop a broader framework linking quantum geometry to local and nonlocal electromagnetic response in gauge-field space, placing this tensor within a hierarchy of electric and magnetic multipole quantum geometries. The intrinsic antisymmetric adiabatic response in every electromagnetic channel is a Berry curvature in the space of its conjugate fields. The field-dependent projector uniquely fixes the QGT for that channel, pairing the response curvature with a quantum metric. This construction extends to spatially nonuniform perturbations, whose finite momentum transfer induces nonvertical Bloch transitions. We explicitly construct the current--current QGT connecting Bloch states at $\mathbf{k}\pm\mathbf{q}/2$, providing a unified metric and curvature description of nonlocal current response. In the doubled Brillouin zone, tangential derivatives generate conventional momentum-space QGT multipoles, whereas normal derivatives connect finite-momentum geometry to uniform electric- and magnetic-multipole-pair QGTs. We derive this connection through second order in $\mathbf{q}$. The finite-momentum curvature governs the intrinsic nonlocal Hall response, while an inverse-frequency moment of symmetric optical absorption probes the index-symmetric metric sector.

papers.title: Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) Semiconductors: A First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Optical, and Energy-Related Properties
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. The calculated dielectric functions, refractive indices, absorption coefficients, reflectivity, optical conductivities, and electron energy-loss spectra reveal systematic changes in optical response across the chalcogen series. The absorption onset shifts toward lower photon energies, from approximately 2.4 eV in Y2CdS4 to 1.7 eV in Y2CdTe4. Thermoelectric calculations indicate promising Seebeck coefficients and power factors, with Y2CdSe4 exhibiting a favorable balance of transport properties. Charge-density distributions, electron localization functions, and Bader charge analyses suggest increasing covalent bonding contributions from sulfide to telluride. These findings highlight the potential of Y2CdX4 compounds for tunable optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications.

papers.title: Microscopic structure at the morphotropic phase boundary in lead-barium meta-niobat
papers.abstract: Lead-barium niobate Pb$_{1-x}$Ba$_x$Nb$_2$O$_6$ is a tetragonal tungsten-bronze ferroelectric that exhibits enhanced functional properties near a morphotropic phase boundary separating orthorhombic and tetragonal phases. Using first-principles electronic-structure calculations combined with ab initio molecular dynamics, we investigate how Ba substitution modifies cation-site occupancy, local distortions, and polarization behavior across the solid solution. By explicitly accounting for vacancy ordering and the inequivalent $A$-site cages intrinsic to the tungsten-bronze framework, we identify the structural origin of the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition. Increasing Ba content progressively weakens the cooperative in-plane off-centering of Pb ions in the pentagonal channels and promotes out-of-plane displacements of Nb and $A$-site cations, leading to a rotation of the spontaneous polarization from [110] to [001]. The transition occurs near $x \approx 0.6$, in quantitative agreement with experimental phase diagrams. These results provide a microscopic interpretation of the morphotropic phase boundary in Pb$_{1-x}$Ba$_x$Nb$_2$O$_6$ and establish a clear structure-polarization relationship for tungsten-bronze ferroelectrics.

papers.title: Underdamped Stochastic Optimal Transport with Landauer boundary conditions: machine learning and analytical solution
papers.abstract: Finding optimal transport protocols for underdamped stochastic processes is a difficult yet important problem in control theory. In this paper we develop a direct method, based on machine learning, to find the optimal solution of the problem in the presence of non-linear boundary conditions, including those modelling the Landauer bit-erasure problem. The dynamics is steered from a single-peak to a double-peak distribution in position space, by only acting on a controllable external potential. The problem is highly non-linear, and analytical solutions are not available in general. We benchmark our numerical results with a perturbative expansion, which is expected to hold in a suitable overdamped limit.

papers.title: Finite-time Mpemba crossings with imperfect preparation
papers.abstract: Two preparations evolving under the same thermal Markov generator can reverse their ordering in relative entropy even when the hotter state retains a nonzero slow-mode component. We derive a sufficient finite-time crossing condition for arbitrary finite irreducible reversible systems. The condition compares the preparations' weights in the entire slowest eigenspace, including degeneracies, and gives an explicit upper bound using the separation from the next distinct decay rate. Exact finite-amplitude entropy comparisons also yield all-mode enclosures and bounds based on a retained spectrum with a controlled omitted tail. A preparation-error inequality converts finite-time sign margins into explicit probability tolerances; extensions account for temperature, generator, and stationary-reference uncertainty. We test the bounds on 2000 predefined network draws with four graph families and 4--64 states. There are 86 numerically located crossings, of which 45 satisfy the simple sufficient condition. In a selected eight-state example, retaining two nonstationary modes certifies a crossing before 1.55163, improving a certified slow-sector endpoint of 2.53951; the located crossing is near 1.26943. A reflecting diffusion in an asymmetric potential supplies a separate physical example, with systematic mesh refinement. Independent interval arithmetic certifies selected spectral bounds, finite-grid first crossings, and an entire preparation-temperature rectangle in a three-state benchmark. The theorem does not require exact slow-mode cancellation, while its numerical sharpness and detection coverage remain model dependent. These results concern relative-entropy relaxation and do not predict water-freezing times.

papers.title: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging
papers.abstract: Physics-informed Gaussian process (GP) methods provide a probabilistic framework for PDE solving. Existing approaches incorporate PDE information in different ways: pointwise conditioning uses the governing equation only at finitely many selected locations, globally constrained GPs restrict the admissible functions to satisfy the PDE exactly, and residual-penalized methods control the PDE mismatch over the whole domain through an additional penalty weight. What is still missing is a GP formulation that directly incorporates global PDE-residual information of the entire domain into its covariance structure, while retaining model flexibility and standard GP conditioning without a separate residual-weight parameter. To solve this issue, this study proposes PDE-residual-informed Kriging (PRIK) based on a PDE-residual kernel. The PDE-residual kernel is constructed by equipping a kernel-section space with an inner product defined by the $L^{2}$ inner product of PDE residuals. This construction makes PRIK yield the posterior mean with minimum integrated squared PDE residual. It also provides direct statistical interpretations: the variance-scale estimate equals the normalized PDE-residual energy (i.e., the integrated squared PDE residual of the posterior mean divided by the number of labeled observations), and the profile likelihood balances this residual energy against model complexity. Under the stated regularity and stability conditions, we establish $H^{2}$-quasi-optimality and convergence rates for the posterior mean, together with a nonasymptotic bound for its PDE-residual norm. We further show that the normalized posterior kernel converges to a variational Green-type kernel and derive a uniform nonasymptotic contraction bound for the posterior variance. Numerical studies provide empirical evidence consistent with the theory and demonstrate the PDE-solving capability of PRIK.

papers.title: Mirror-symmetry engineering of altermagnetism based on monolayer hexagonal lattices
papers.abstract: Altermagnetism (AM) is a novel collinear antiferromagnetic phase characterized by spin-polarized bands and zero net magnetization. However, realizing AM in monolayer hexagonal lattices is strongly constrained by lattice symmetry. Here, we propose a mirror-symmetry-based design principle and implementation scheme for realizing AM based on monolayer hexagonal lattices and validate it using holey graphyne (HGY) as a representative system. By examining hydrogenated nonmetal units X$-$H (X = B, C, N, P, and S) introduced along the mirror-symmetry axis and extending the analysis to N$-$F, we identify the configurations that form two antiparallel spin sublattices related by mirror reflection. The N$-$H structure forms a stable altermagnetic ground state, with a momentum-dependent spin splitting up to 148.2 meV. The magnetism originates from $π-π$ superexchange interactions, and H/F functionalization stabilizes intrinsic AM by regulating the local charge distribution. Our work offers insights into the design of light-element altermagnetic materials.

papers.title: Reliability-Weighted Direct Preference Optimization: Penalized Weights for Robust Preference Learning
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) treats every reported comparison as correct, yet preference data contain reversed, tied or otherwise noisy comparisons. RW-DPO gives each comparison an unknown reliability weight $w_i\in[0,1]$ that enters the likelihood linearly -- DPO is $w\equiv1$, a reversed comparison $w_i=0$ -- and estimates the weights jointly with the policy under a minimax-concave penalty on $-\log w_i$. The penalty keeps every comparison the model agrees with at exactly $w_i=1$ and acts only on those it contradicts, through closed-form weight updates at negligible cost over DPO. We prove that recovering all flipped comparisons from a single annotation per comparison requires margins of order $\log n$. Furthermore, in a linear-index model, starting from an initial fit pointing in the correct direction, our estimator jointly consistently recovers the preference direction and weights, as well as identifies the flipped comparisons above this margin scale, even when a fixed fraction of comparisons is flipped. In simulations RW-DPO has the lowest average estimation error among DPO, noise-rate corrections and recent robust methods, with far more precise flags than recent label-correction methods. In DPO fine-tuning of a language model with 10-30% flipped labels, its win rate does not fall as the flip rate grows and exceeds that of DPO trained on clean labels, matching the strongest recent method with corrections concentrated on the flipped labels.

papers.title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
papers.abstract: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.

papers.title: Novel thermodynamic topological subclass from inverse-temperature asymptotics
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic topology of the charged McGuigan--Nappi--Yost black hole in the canonical ensemble at fixed electric charge, identifying equilibrium black hole solutions as zeros of the thermodynamic vector field constructed from the generalized off-shell free energy. The inverse Hawking temperature diverges as the extremal limit is approached and approaches a finite positive value in the large-horizon limit. The zero points of the thermodynamic vector field reveal a thermodynamic phase structure consisting solely of a locally stable branch with positive winding number ($w=+1$). The innermost small black hole state is locally stable in the low-temperature limit. As the temperature increases, the stable branch extends toward the outermost large black hole regime, while no black hole states exist in the high-temperature regime beyond the finite upper Hawking temperature. This distinct asymptotic behavior of the inverse temperature places the thermodynamic defect structure outside the established topological (sub)classes, although its topological number agrees with that of the standard $W^{1+}$ class. We therefore identify this defect structure as a new thermodynamic topological subclass, $\breve W^{1+}$. This finding extends the existing classification to include a finite, nonzero large-horizon limit of the inverse Hawking temperature and suggests that distinct asymptotic behaviors in other black hole families may reveal further topological (sub)classes and thermodynamic phase structures.

papers.title: A Common Type II Origin of Galilean and Carroll Superstrings
papers.abstract: We show that the relativistic Type-II superalgebras, once the fundamental-string winding charge is retained alongside the momentum, admit a single non-Lorentzian contraction whose two translation ideals carry Galilean and magnetic-Carroll supersymmetry, respectively. The complementary vector charge required for this structure is thus intrinsic to string theory. The IIA realization is particle-like and the IIB realization string-like, a distinction fixed by chirality, and spacelike T-duality relates the two while preserving each non-Lorentzian structure. The same contraction is finite on the doubled Green--Schwarz action, including all fermion terms and local kappa symmetry, where the two supersymmetries appear as the two polarizations of a single worldsheet theory. These results unify two distinct non-Lorentzian corners of string theory within a common Type-II origin and open a route toward a broader web of non-Lorentzian dualities and possible holographic generalizations.

papers.title: Learning Joint Synchronization, Channel Estimation, and Decoding: Comparison with a Finite-Blocklength Achievability Bound
papers.abstract: Learned schemes that jointly perform tasks such as synchronization and decoding have achieved promising results for short-packet communication. However, it remains unclear how close their performance is to information-theoretic bounds. To investigate this question, we extend the turbo autoencoder (TurboAE) proposed in Dörner et al. (2023) to a single-input single-output waveform channel with an unknown delay and memoryless block fading, for which an achievability bound from finite-blocklength information theory is available. Our extension incorporates a pilot-free, model-guided neural synchronizer and enables joint synchronization, channel estimation, and decoding. At a blocklength of $64$ complex symbols and a rate of one bit per channel use, the proposed TurboAE achieves a lower bit error rate (BER) than all evaluated pilot-assisted 5G baselines, with gains of $1.9$ dB at a BER of $10^{-3}$ over a baseline involving a low-density parity-check (LDPC) code and $1.7$ dB over a baseline involving a polar code and successive cancellation list decoding (list size $8$). In terms of block error rate (BLER), the TurboAE outperforms the LDPC-coded baseline, but lags behind the polar-coded baseline by about $0.8$ dB at a BLER of $10^{-3}$. Moreover, all evaluated schemes remain at least $2.1$ dB away from a pilot-assisted achievability bound, indicating substantial room for improved designs.

papers.title: Group Physical-Layer Authentication and Confidential Beamforming in Non-Terrestrial Networks
papers.abstract: Coordinated high-altitude platform station (HAPS) networks need to authenticate group responses and protect private data under shared power constraints. This paper studies joint group physical-layer authentication (PLA) and confidential beamforming using a fresh secret tag superimposed on private data. For received attacks independent of the current tag, we derive exact finite-block expressions for false acceptance and legitimate rejection. These expressions translate authentication error targets into a required tag signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). We establish a nonzero asymptotic tag-energy floor and analyze residual frequency offset and peak-power restrictions. The legitimate receiver removes the tag by orthogonal projection, which discards one temporal dimension. For colluding eavesdroppers, we identify the spatial coverage condition under which artificial noise (AN) keeps their SINR bounded as data and AN powers increase together. We jointly optimize the private beams, tag beam, and AN covariance to minimize transmit power under authentication, secrecy, and per-HAPS power constraints. The method combines semidefinite relaxation (SDR), exact private-beam rank reduction, and feasible successive convex approximation. A corrected dual lower bound measures the remaining optimality gap. Numerical results show that increasing the tag length from 16 to 64 symbols reduces the required tag SINR by 7.16 dB. Joint beam design reduces mean transmit power by 27.4% relative to an optimized fixed-tag-direction baseline. The authentication guarantee requires fresh secret tags and excludes relays of the current response.

papers.title: Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $Γ$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.

papers.title: Phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices in the oscillating axion background
papers.abstract: We investigate the effect of an oscillating axion background on thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model. Through its coupling to the gauge field, the axion sources an electromagnetic response in the presence of vortex magnetic flux, modifying the dynamics of the vortices. We study this system using Langevin lattice simulations with dissipation and stochastic noise. It is shown that the phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices, namely the pair creation of vortex and antivortex under thermal fluctuations, can be significantly modified in the oscillating axion background. We find that the axion background shifts the rapid increase in the vortex density to lower temperature. In particular, this transition temperature becomes smaller as the oscillation frequency of the axion increases. The temperature dependence of the correlation length is also modified. These features provide a new experimental approach for the axion dark matter using superconducting devices.

papers.title: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
papers.abstract: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Thélène, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
papers.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. At high nitrogen coverage, the N2 admolecules are formed, weakly attached to the surface. The calculated electronic properties of the single-adatom systems include the band diagrams of the slabs in real and momentum space, the energies of the quantum states. In addition, the overlaps of the quantum states of the nonmetal adatoms and the nearest topmost surface Ga atoms are given. The full coverage data include the atomic configurations and the bond energies of the adsorbed layers. The electronic properties include the above-mentioned data for single adatoms, together with additional properties related to interactions between adsorbed atoms. The evaporation stability analysis confirms that the adatoms stabilize the topmost Ga atoms against detachment because of the high energy barrier of DE > 3 eV which is further increased to DE > 4 eV by coverage located at H3 sites. Thus, growth simulations should employ unreconstructed Ga-terminated surfaces covered by nonmetal atoms located at on-top positions.

papers.title: Poly Versus Polyval
papers.abstract: We revisit the basic construction of polynomial evaluation based hash function, which we call Poly, over binary extension fields over $GF(2^n)$, where $n=64k$ and $k\geq 2$. Unlike GHASH, the NIST standard polynomial evaluation based hash function for $n=128$, Poly does not perform the unnecessary bit reversals of each $n$-bit block, and consequently is faster than GHASH. Further, Poly differs from Polyval, -- a faster alternative to GHASH, -- in that Poly performs usual reduction, while Polyval performs Montgomery reduction. We identify suitable choices of the field representing irreducible polynomials which makes usual and Montgomery reductions efficient. We provide detailed algorithms, and associated proofs of correctness for both kinds of reductions. Based on the algorithms, we report carefully optimised assembly implementation of both Poly and Polyval for $n=128,256$ and $512$. Our theoretical analysis and experimental timing results show that for $n=128$, Polyval is faster than Poly, while for $n=256$ and $512$ (as well as for higher values of $n$), Poly is faster than Polyval. The cases $n=128$ and $256$ are of current relevance due to the ongoing NIST process for developing cryptographic accordions.

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. I. Clean surface properties
papers.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to elucidate the properties of the polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors, i.e., metal- and nonmetal-terminated. The systems considered were clean wurtzite gallium nitride (i.e. (0001) and (000-1) GaN surfaces), zinc blende gallium phosphide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaP), gallium arsenide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaAs), and (111) and (-1-1-1) GaSb surfaces. The calculated data include the crystallographic structure and the electronic states of the termination atoms on both sides, i.e. their positions, energies, and occupations. All nonmetal-terminated surfaces exhibit no reconstruction, and their broken-bond states are located in the vicinity of the valence band maxima (VBM), pinning the Fermi level. The Ga-terminated surface exhibited (4 x 4) reconstruction related to the division of termination atoms into sp3 and sp2 hybridized in proportions of 6 to 10, based on charge redistribution according to the electron counting rule (ECR). Thus, the broken-bond state is separated into two sets, occupied and empty, with the Fermi level located between them in the vicinity of the conduction band minimum (CBM).

papers.title: On $t$-designs supported by self-orthogonal codes
papers.abstract: We study self-orthogonal $t$-$(v,k,λ)$ designs satisfying the condition that the codes generated by the designs are self-orthogonal codes whose codewords of minimum weight $k$ correspond to the blocks. A classification of such designs is given under the conditions that $t\geq \lfloor k/4\rfloor+1\geq2$ and $t \le 11$. This yields a classification of self-orthogonal codes of minimum weight $k$ whose codewords of minimum weight form a $t$-design under the same conditions.

papers.title: DeepWeave: Weaving Neural and Symbolic Evidence for ML-Based Network Intrusion Detection System
papers.abstract: Machine learning-based network intrusion detection systems can recognize complex traffic patterns, but often require substantial labelled attack data, degrade under deployment shift, and provide limited evidence for analysts. We present DeepWeave, a probabilistic neuro-symbolic Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) that makes logic an integral part of detection. DeepWeave automatically constructs and validates interpretable rules, represents neural predictions as probabilistic predicates, and reconciles both evidence sources through explicit coupling policies over packet-, flow-, and hybrid-views. The resulting proofs provide intrinsic explanations for rule-supported alerts. Across multiple datasets, DeepWeave improves low-data detection, false-positive control, transferability, and robustness. With only 50 labelled packet observations per attack class, it improves macro-F1 from 0.632 to 0.924 and reduces the attack false-positive rate from 0.075 to 0.008 over the matched neural baseline. Its proofs are also more stable than post-hoc neural attributions, while batched inference keeps probabilistic reasoning practical. These results demonstrate label-efficient, adaptable, and inspectable neuro-symbolic intrusion detection.

papers.title: Beyond Typical Strings: Sampling the Complexity Landscape
papers.abstract: Uniform random sampling of strings is overwhelmingly dominated by high-complexity strings, leaving the much smaller set of low- and intermediate-complexity strings largely unexplored. Here, we adapt the nested neutral set estimator (NNSE), a Monte Carlo rare-event sampling method, to estimate the distribution P(K) of complexity values for binary strings of fixed length. NNSE allows us to explore the full complexity landscape, including exponentially rare low-complexity regions that are inaccessible to direct sampling, for string lengths up to several hundred. We apply the method to several widely used complexity measures: Lempel-Ziv 76 (LZ76), Lempel-Ziv 78 (LZ78), context tree weighting (CTW), the block decomposition method (BDM), and block entropy. We further introduce uniform complexity weighting (UCW), which gives equal weight to different complexity levels rather than to individual strings. This approach provides a dataset-independent framework for comparing complexity measures across their full range and reveals substantial differences between measures for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are largely hidden by conventional uniform sampling. Using the NNSE to perform UCW sampling allows us to compare complexity measures across their full range in a dataset-independent way. This reveals differences in their behavior for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are practically inaccessible to conventional uniform sampling.

papers.title: Hadronic Molecules: Theory
papers.abstract: Since the turn of the century it becomes evident that the naive quark model is not capable to describe the rich phenomenology of hadrons, especially in the doubly heavy sector. For a large number of those states a molecular structure appears to be a natural description. In these proceedings I review the theory of hadronic molecules, how they can be described systematically in effective field theories and what imprint this structure leaves in observables. On two examples I explain non-trivial predictions emerging from the molecular hypothesis that can be tested in future experiments and lattice QCD calculations, promising deep insights into the inner workings of QCD.

papers.title: The Generalized Twin Image: Understanding Regularized Phase Retrieval
papers.abstract: Image priors can dramatically improve phase retrieval reconstruction, but their effectiveness strongly varies between imaging modalities. We introduce the generalized twin image, which extends the classical twin-image ambiguity from Fourier phase retrieval to any invertible sensing operator, to understand this effectiveness. The ambiguity extends to undersampled and oversampled measurements, remaining exact under undersampling and for oversampled coded Fourier measurements. We show that it provides a simple criterion to assess regularization effectiveness: the image prior should favor the ground truth over its generalized twin image. We propose the total-variation ratio as a simple measure of this preference, and derive closed-form estimates for structured random phase retrieval models. Experiments with a pretrained denoiser demonstrate that the ratio predicts regularized reconstruction performance across different sensing models.

papers.title: High-efficiency photonic GHZ measurements with linear optics
papers.abstract: Probabilistic and destructive Bell-measurements, also known as fusions, constitute a fundamental primitive for photonic quantum technologies. These operations rely only on pairwise photonic interference, whereas the computational power of photonic quantum systems originates from many-body interference. Here, we introduce a family of high-efficiency linear-optical GHZ measurements based on four-mode interferometers and show that incorporating many-body interference into this ubiquitous primitive leads to more efficient entangling operations. For the four-photon case, the success probability is $9/32$, and adaptive variants ensure that unsuccessful events project onto useful stabilizer states. We further show that the approach naturally generalizes to larger GHZ measurements, yielding an exponentially higher success probability than previous linear-optical schemes. Finally, we demonstrate practical advantages for graph-state resource generation, entanglement distribution between remote spin-photon interfaces, and fusion-based quantum computing. Our results establish high-efficiency many-body measurements as a new primitive for scalable photonic quantum information processing.

papers.title: A Hybrid Message-Passing and Electric-Field Representation for Electrostatic QM/MM Embedding with Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Within a hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics approach a small region of a large atomistic system is described quantum mechanically, while the rest of the system is represented by a classical force field. Despite this, the computational cost of the quantum calculation severely limits the accessible simulation and sampling time. Replacing the quantum calculation with a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) trained on quantum reference data can greatly increase the accessible simulation time. However, the accuracy and efficiency strongly depend on the specific way in which the MLIP incorporates information about the classical (electrostatic) environment. Here, we demonstrate that existing strategies based purely on features derived from an external electric field fail to distinguish certain environments, ultimately limiting their accuracy. As a solution, we propose an extension to the equivariant TensorNet architecture that mitigates this shortcoming by incorporating classical atoms close to the quantum region into the message-passing scheme, combined with features derived from the electric field for describing the environment farther away. We show that this combination achieves higher accuracy than either approach alone.

papers.title: eCAS: An Orbital Embedding Method for Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Future fault-tolerant quantum computers will allow us to calculate electronic structures of atomistic systems. However, these systems will be intrinsically limited in size, requiring embedding theories for many systems because of the unfavorable scaling of the number of terms describing the electron-electron interaction in the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. Quantum embedding theories address this challenge by partitioning a quantum system into a region of interest, the impurity, and its (larger) complement, the environment. However, currently available quantum embedding methods place restrictive demands on near-future quantum computers, such as the need to measure reduced density matrices or the need for repeated evaluations. Here, we introduce the new orbital embedding method eCAS that steers clear of these pitfalls by constructing a multi-CAS problem, the active spaces of which are localized and can be solved independently of each other with any quantum algorithm. This also allows for the development of comparatively simple gradient expressions. eCAS leverages the Schmidt decomposition to construct initial impurity and bath orbitals and augments them with localized environment orbitals, based on a mutual correlation criterion. The mutual correlation criterion makes eCAS systematically improvable without the need for any iteratively determined quantities.

papers.title: Potentials of individual atoms by convergent beam electron diffraction
papers.abstract: In convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) on two-dimensional (2D) materials, the intensity distributions within the individual CBED spots map the local atomic arrangements within the probed region. In this study we demonstrate that the average intensities within the CBED spots essentially depend on the scattering parameters by a single atom, thus, offering the possibility of the direct measurement of such parameters. Scattering potential of an individual atom can be approximated by the Gaussian function and its parameters, the standard deviation and the maximal phase shift, can be recovered from the ratio of the intensities in the zero- and higher orders spots in CBED pattern. In order to demonstrate this, we simulated CBED patterns and extracted the atomic scattering parameters from such patterns. In the simulated examples, no weak phase object approximation is applied and the proposed method provides accurate results even for materials with large phase shifts up to 1.5 rad, as for example tungsten. The scattering parameters recovered from the experimental CBED patterns of graphene and twisted graphene-hBN structure show good agreement with the theoretically obtained values.

papers.title: Disk-Corona Energy Balance Evolves with Flux State in the Quasar PDS 456
papers.abstract: We investigate the long-term X-ray spectral evolution of the highly luminous, radio-quiet quasar PDS 456 using AstroSat observations obtained in 2019 and 2021 together with archival XMM-Newton, NuSTAR and Suzaku observations spanning 2001-2024. The AstroSat observations provide valuable coverage following the bright flaring state observed in 2018, revealing that the source underwent a relatively quiescent phase in 2019 before re-brightening in 2021. During the AstroSat epochs, PDS 456 exhibits a harder-when-brighter spectral trend, whereas the long-term XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, and Suzaku observations confirm the overall softer-when-fainter behavior. This behavior is consistent with the presence of a very cool corona (~15 keV), possibly driven by a strong incident photon field for upscattering, as suggested by a prominent big blue bump. Broadband spectral modeling of simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations, complemented by the 2021 AstroSat flaring epoch and interpreted within the self-consistent physical framework reXcor, indicates that the disk-corona energy balance evolves with flux. In low-flux states, the spectrum is reflection-dominated, implying efficient illumination of the inner accretion disk by a compact corona. In contrast, high-flux states show an enhanced contribution from the warm Comptonizing region at larger coronal heights.
