This supports planar models of healthy gait, while a repeatable, task-dependent coupling index may serve as a measure of gait quality. The simple models are wrong, but useful enough.

papers.title: Global and crustal properties of neutron stars
papers.abstract: We investigate how the treatment of the neutron star crust affects both the global properties of the star and the properties of the crust itself. Three approaches are compared: a direct connection between a fixed crust and the core equation of state (EOS), a smooth crossover between them, and a unified EOS in which the crust is computed within a compressible liquid-drop model with the same nuclear empirical parameters of the relativistic mean-field model used for the core. For each approach, we consider four values of the symmetry energy slope, $44 \le L \le 92$ MeV. For a $1.4\,M_\odot$ star, some global properties are weakly to moderately affected: the radius and the moment of inertia agree within 1\% among the three approaches. On the other hand, the tidal deformability obtained with the direct connection is up to 21\% lower than the unified one for $L = 92$ MeV. A much larger contrast comes from the crustal properties. Relative to the unified EOS, the direct connection yields a crust that is 15--36\% thinner, 6--12 times less massive, and that carries a fraction of the total moment of inertia 5--8 times smaller (0.3--1.1\% instead of 2.8--6.2\%). The differences between crust treatments are thus comparable to or larger than those arising from variations in $L$ for crustal properties, while they remain subleading for global ones.

papers.title: Incorporating deep neural networks into lepton-nucleus interaction modeling
papers.abstract: We present a scheme to incorporate precise inclusive cross-section predictions from a deep neural network trained on electron--carbon scattering data into a Monte Carlo event generator. The inclusive prediction is decomposed into independent exclusive interaction channels using the generator's theoretical models, and the resulting events are reweighted accordingly. We apply this scheme to investigate nuclear effects in inclusive and semi-exclusive electron-scattering measurements.

papers.title: Triplon thermal Hall response in a honeycomb-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions
papers.abstract: We investigate triplon topology and the thermal Hall transport in a columnar valence-bond solid of a spin-$1/2$ honeycomb-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet. Inequivalent triangular sublattices, modeled by $J_2^A\neq J_2^B$, remove inversion symmetry at nearest-neighbor bond centers and allow in-plane Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interactions. We identify the two symmetry-allowed in-plane DM vector patterns and present detailed results for the pattern parallel to the bonds including an out-of-plane magnetic field. Within a harmonic bond-operator treatment, we determine the triplon bands, their Berry curvatures and Chern numbers, and the triplon thermal Hall conductivity. The DM interaction and magnetic field generate nonzero Berry curvatures, but the numerically integrated Chern number of every isolated triplon band vanishes. Nevertheless, the energy-dependent Bose weighting of positive and negative Berry-curvature regions produces a finite thermal Hall response at nonzero low temperatures. We delimit the dilute-triplon regime in which the harmonic transport calculation is expected to be reliable. These results show that a vanishing Chern number band does not directly constrain the triplon response of a valence-bond solid. We also comment on the effects on the columnar valence-bond solid phase of a DM interaction between next-nearest-neighbor spins characterized by an out-of-plane vector pattern.

papers.title: Facets of Gravity: A journey exploring spacetime from Planckian to cosmological scales
papers.abstract: What does it mean to quantize gravity, and what can a quantum theory of spacetime actually predict? This thesis explores these questions through complementary non-perturbative approaches, from the geometry of quantum spacetime to the emergence of cosmological physics. Within Causal Dynamical Triangulations, we develop observables to investigate effective topology, statistical homogeneity, and curvature in strongly fluctuating geometries, where conventional differential-geometric tools are unavailable. Tests in two-dimensional models reveal distinct coarse-graining behaviours and provide new ways to probe the emergence of familiar geometric properties. We then turn to the Functional Renormalization Group and Asymptotic Safety, developing flow invariants to characterize ultraviolet-critical surfaces and introducing Flow Invariant Neural Networks as a computational method for reconstructing them. In scalar-tensor gravity, we investigate how ultraviolet consistency conditions can constrain infrared interactions, obtaining an inflationary scenario compatible with cosmological observations. Finally, we question whether the metric must be the fundamental variable of quantum gravity. We formulate a lattice statistical approach to purely affine gravity, in which the connection is fundamental and the metric, when it exists, is emergent. Monte Carlo simulations provide exploratory results in two dimensions, while a four-dimensional homogeneous and isotropic construction yields preliminary evidence for de Sitter-like geometry and allows the study of curvature correlations. Together, these investigations develop complementary tools for studying quantum spacetime, testing its possible continuum behaviour, and connecting fundamental gravitational theories with observable physics, while identifying the conceptual and computational challenges that remain.

papers.title: The Importance of Curium-250 to the $γ$-Ray Signature of $r$-Process Remnants
papers.abstract: Identifying the astrophysical sites of the heavy rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) remains one of the most prominent unsolved problems in nuclear astrophysics. Emitted $γ$-rays from the decay of unstable nuclei have been identified as a potential observable marker on both prompt and delayed timescales which could provide conclusive evidence of the presence of $r$-process activity. In this work, we identify and discuss the importance of $^{250}$Cm to the $γ$-ray spectra of remnants, showing that the decay spectrum of $^{250}$Cm dominates the $γ$-ray spectra of $r$-process ejecta across a broad timescale ($\sim$ 2,000 - 20,000 years). We highlight the uncertain nature of this spectra: $^{250}$Cm may decay via $α$-decay, $β$-decay, and spontaneous fission, but the decay branchings are not experimentally known, and each decay channel produces unique spectral lines which may be observable. We examine the potential for observation of the most prominent spectral signatures, finding that for conventional neutron star merger remnants, $γ$-ray lines will be detectable in current and future detectors only in the very near galaxy ($\sim$ 1 kpc), but other sites which could produce a larger ejecta mass may have greater observable distances. Our findings highlight the potential of actinide decay chains to indicate r-process nucleosynthesis and further underscore the necessity of measuring the nuclear properties that define their characteristic spectral signatures.

papers.title: Optical Quantum Memory Processing for Quantum Hashing
papers.abstract: Sender authentication is an important requirement for secure quantum communication networks. We propose programmable photon-echo quantum memory processing of a multi-time-bin photonic qudit for implementing a quantum-hash-based verification protocol. In this approach, using QM, sender (Alice) generates a quantum hash state by transforming a single stored photonic wave packet into the programmable photonic qudit. Bob's memory coherently maps the received time-bin photonic qudit into a single output mode according to phase encoding. Our scheme relies on a time-resolved coherent detection method introduced here, in which the coherent responses from individual time-bins are sequentially accumulated within Bob's spin coherence prior to the final sender verification. The key advantage of this coherent detection for quantum hashing is shown, and its potential applications are also discussed. The performed analysis demonstrates that experimentally verified parameters of contemporary optical quantum memories enable a proof of principle realization of the proposed architecture. These results reveal an additional role for quantum memories, serving not only as synchronization and repeater resources for long-distance quantum communication, but also as active elements for quantum hashing in conventional quantum key distribution systems.

papers.title: Metadevices that compute: mathematical foundations and experimental implementations for neuromorphic nanophotonics
papers.abstract: Wave-based analog computing has re-emerged as a compelling alternative to digital electronics for specific linear-algebraic and machine-learning workloads, promising massively parallel, high-bandwidth, and energy-efficient information processing. Metamaterials, metasurfaces, and integrated metastructures (collectively, metadevices) now perform mathematical operations, solve integral and differential equations, multiply matrices, and implement trainable photonic neural networks directly in the wave domain. This focused review consolidates the mathematical foundations that underpin such devices, i.e., the mapping between linear operators and wave scattering, the feedback architectures that realize equation inversion, and the inverse-design and scientific machine-learning toolchains that make their synthesis and training tractable, and connects them to the rapidly growing body of experimental demonstrations, from free-space diffractive processors to reconfigurable guided-wave metastructures. We conclude with open problems and opportunities for this emerging neuromorphic nanophotonics ecosystem.

papers.title: Stars Can Quench Superradiance Around Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abstract: Light scalar fields trigger an instability around rotating black holes which drives the rapid growth of high-density bound states on astrophysically short timescales---a phenomenon known as black hole superradiance. This process is usually tacitly assumed to happen independent of the local environment. Around supermassive black holes, however, orbiting stars and compact objects act as a perturbation that drains energy from the cloud, potentially preventing its formation altogether. In this work, we quantify under what conditions this happens, focusing on bound-free state transitions. We first compute the rate of energy dissipation due to gravitational interactions, finding that the superradiance growth rate almost always dominates the environmental depletion. The two rates are, however, close enough that the conclusion could be overturned once bound-bound transitions are included. Also, the environment dissipates the cloud faster than gravitational-wave emission, implying that stellar environments must be accounted for in a variety of indirect search strategies. We then investigate the impact of the scalar's quadratic couplings to nucleons and electromagnetism, showing that these interactions can greatly enhance energy dissipation, preventing the cloud's formation. This work highlights the importance of accounting for the local environment in studies of superradiance around intermediate and supermassive black holes.

papers.title: Stress-enhanced diffusion in Yukawa crystals
papers.abstract: Self-diffusion in crystallized Coulomb (Yukawa) plasmas proceeds by the thermally activated formation of vacancy-interstitial pairs and the migration of these defects through the lattice, commonly known as Frenkel pairs in the materials literature. Molecular dynamics has recently resolved an Eyring law for diffusion in unstrained crystals, which we generalize to deformed crystals in this work. We simulate sheared Yukawa crystals and show that a static elastic strain exponentially enhances diffusion due to the additional elastic energy stored in the region that participates in Frenkel pair formation relative to the unstrained crystal: $D(\varepsilon)=D_0(Γ^{*})\exp[V^{*}σ/k_{\rm B}T]$, with $σ=\tfrac12μ\varepsilon^{2}$ the elastic energy density stored by the shear strain $\varepsilon$ and $V^{*}$ the activation volume. We find a single activation volume $N_{\rm act} = n_iV^{*}\simeq31$ suffices for typical astrophysical screenings with a reduction at higher screening. This suggests Frenkel pair formation requires only a brief coordination of the nearest neighbors at a thermal maximum in oscillation. Stress-enhanced diffusion supplies a microphysical mechanism for creep in strained neutron star crusts and crystallizing white dwarf cores.

papers.title: Truncated Grassmannians: polytopes, representations, and Cauchy formulas
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to develop algebraic and combinatorial techniques for studying the geometric properties of truncated Grassmannians, a class of algebraic varieties obtained via certain projections of classical Grassmannians within their Plücker embeddings. We introduce a class of cyclic representations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of the general linear Lie algebra, which are proved to serve as duals of the homogeneous components of coordinate rings of truncated Grassmannians. We prove that the characters of these representations are computed via truncated Cauchy formulas and establish a connection with coordinate rings of complete collineations. We also construct monomial bases of these representations in terms of certain generalized chain polytopes and use the RSK correspondence to establish connections with Cauchy-type formulas and with Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.

papers.title: ChatGPT as a Surveillance Assistant? An Exploratory Case Study of AI-Assisted Surveillance Risks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate detailed guidance, functional code, and persuasive text at scale. As one of the most widely used consumer language model products as of 2026, ChatGPT gives broad public access to these capabilities, motivating concerns about its potential use in surveillance-related tasks. We present an exploratory case study of what potentially harmful surveillance assistance looks like in ChatGPT's public web interface. We contribute a taxonomy of seven surveillance risk categories based on prior LLM risk research and reports of deployed surveillance systems, instantiated as 110 prompts, along with a manually reviewed analysis of ChatGPT's responses. Prompts were issued using two approaches: 55 jailbreak prompts drawing on five types of elicitation strategies, and 55 plain-language direct prompts, each run alone, and if unsuccessful, again with a short fixed prefix. We find that ChatGPT provides substantive surveillance guidance for 40 of the 55 jailbreak prompts and for 33 of the 55 direct prompts without any prefix. Compliant responses also rarely included policy mentions or suggestions for privacy-preserving alternatives. We manually review every response and find that even when ChatGPT states a refusal, it may still supply detailed instructions, working code, or architectural guidance alongside brief ethical caveats.

papers.title: Robust-by-Design Distributional Learning from Contaminated Samples
papers.abstract: Modern data analysis pipelines increasingly rely on large datasets assembled through retrieval, scraping, automated filtering, and post-hoc curation, where the observed sample is often a contaminated mixture rather than the target population. Standard distributional objectives either ignore contamination and converge to the wrong target, or retain only a small trusted subset and discard most of the data. We study supervised and unsupervised learning when a clean reference sample is compared with a pooled sample from $r=(1-ε)q+εz$, where $q$ is the latent target distribution and $z$ is an unknown contaminant. Motivated by settings with noisy membership scores for all observations and exact labels for a small audited subset, we propose contamination-corrected maximum mean discrepancy (CC-MMD), a design-based estimator that combines proxy scores with audited residual corrections to recover the oracle MMD that would have been computed from the latent clean sample. CC-MMD requires no calibration assumption on the proxy scores and no structural assumptions on the contaminant beyond standard kernel regularity. We prove finite-population design-unbiasedness of the corrected kernel sums, establish asymptotic normality of the audit correction, and show consistency for the target discrepancy $\mathrm{MMD}^2(p,q;k)$. Empirically, CC-MMD tracks the oracle under increasing contamination, improves parameter recovery and prediction in contaminated regression, and enables generative models trained on heavily corrupted mixtures to recover the clean target distribution. These results show that contaminated data need not be discarded or treated as the estimand. With sparse trusted labels and abundant noisy supervision, distributional objectives can be made robust by design.

papers.title: Subsonic terahertz plasmon instability in space-time plasmonic crystals
papers.abstract: We investigate collective plasma-wave dynamics in a two-dimensional electron fluid subected to a travelling periodic modulation of the effective plasma velocity. Using a hydrodynamic description combined with Floquet-Bloch theory, we show that the travelling modulation acts as a moving plasmonic crystal whose band structure is governed by an effective drift velocity in the comoving frame. We demonstrate that the closure of the Bragg gap at the edge of the Brillouin zone gives rise to an exceptional point and triggers a Krein-type instability through the coupling of positive- and negative-energy modes. Analytical expressions are derived for the instability threshold and growth rate, revealing that self-amplification can occur even when the electron drift remains subsonic in the laboratory frame. Numerical simulations of the nonlinear hydrodynamic equations confirm the theoretical predictions and show the evolution towards a saturated regime dominated by a coherent Floquet-Bloch mode. These results identify travelling plasmonic crystals as a novel platform for wave amplification and non-Hermitian band dynamics in electronic fluids.

papers.title: Transverse momentum correlations and QED effects in TMD determinations
papers.abstract: Extractions of the non-perturbative, transverse momentum dependent (TMD) hadron's structure from experimental measurements of vector-boson spectra at hadron colliders are strongly influenced by correlations across boson's transverse momentum bins and by Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) effects, both from photon emission and from the photon-photon collision background. We present a Monte Carlo framework to take this into account, and illustrate the results with a comparison of theoretical predictions with the high-precision LHCb measurements of $Z$-boson production in the forward rapidity region. We discuss the relationship with the CMS data set at central rapidities.

papers.title: Hilbert space in the flat limit of AdS/CFT. II. Massless particles
papers.abstract: Building on Part I of this series, where we described the emergence of massive scattering states, we demonstrate how unitary lowest-weight representations $\mathcal D(Δ,s)$ of the conformal group with fixed dimension $Δ$ and arbitrary integer spin $s$ contract to massless Poincaré particle representations. This requires combining the Inönü--Wigner contraction $\mathfrak{so}(2,3) \to \mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$ with an infinite boost, in which case massless scattering states naturally emerge in a carrollian basis. For $Δ>s+1$, we find that $\mathcal D(Δ,s)$ contracts to the direct sum of massless particles of all spins $s'\leq s$. At the unitarity bound, lower-spin states become null so that $\mathcal D(s+1,s)$ contracts to a single massless particle representation carrying the two maximal helicities $J=\pm s$. In both cases, the inner product converges to the Poincaré-invariant one after a single helicity-independent rescaling, so that unitarity is preserved throughout the contraction.

papers.title: The Standard Model with Non-Anticommuting $γ_5$ in the BMHV Scheme
papers.abstract: The Breitenlohner-Maison/'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme provides a treatment of $γ_5$ in dimensional regularisation (DReg) that is guaranteed to be self-consistent at all orders, but it breaks gauge and BRST invariance at the regularised level, which must be restored by suitable counterterms. We present the complete 1-loop renormalisation of the full Standard Model in the BMHV scheme in general $R_ξ$-gauge, including all singular and all finite symmetry-restoring counterterms. We further analyse the impact of evanescent gauge interactions, which allow the photon and gluon currents to be treated either 4- or $D$-dimensionally. We show that QCD always contributes to the symmetry breaking, so that the Standard Model must be treated as a whole, and we recommend a purely 4-dimensional treatment of electroweak gauge interactions. Our results provide a necessary step towards multi-loop electroweak precision calculations with a fully consistent treatment of $γ_5$.

papers.title: A systematic study of hydrodynamic attractors in periodically driven systems at weak and strong couplings
papers.abstract: We study equilibration and hydrodynamic response in conformal systems undergoing periodic expansion and contraction along one spatial direction. Using strongly coupled holography (AdS/CFT), weakly coupled kinetic theories (relaxation-time approximation, scalar $φ^4$ theory and the Yang--Mills sector of QCD effective kinetic theory) and hydrodynamics (Navier--Stokes, Müller--Israel--Stewart (MIS) and rBRSSS), we investigate the shear response to a periodic drive of varying amplitude $A$ and frequency $ω$, both analytically in linear response and numerically. We find that, at the linear level, $A\ll 1$, periodically driven systems approach a cyclic attractor that in general differs from Navier--Stokes behaviour. This attractor is universal among kinetic theories and accurately described by MIS theory: for slow driving, $ωτ_π\ll 1$, where $τ_π$ is the shear relaxation time, it approaches the Navier--Stokes limit, whereas for fast driving the shear stress saturates at its non-interacting (free-streaming) value. In strongly coupled holographic systems, the periodic drive excites non-hydrodynamic quasinormal modes, which produce a characteristic ringing in the approach to the cyclic attractor, in contrast to the purely exponential approach found in kinetic theories. This difference is a direct consequence of the distinct non-hydrodynamic spectra of the two classes of theories. Moreover, unlike in kinetic theory, the holographic response is sensitive to the curvature terms of second-order hydrodynamics. Over longer times, non-linear viscous heating, which is quadratic in the drive amplitude, raises the temperature and thereby lowers $ωτ_π$, since $τ_π\sim 1/T$. This induces a slow drift of the cyclic attractor, which eventually converges towards Navier--Stokes hydrodynamics at asymptotically late times.

papers.title: FOMO-Z. Optimal galaxy classification, photometric redshifts, and reconstruction of population distributions
papers.abstract: We present FOMO-Z (Flexible Optimizer of Multi-dimensional Operators and photo-$z$s), a set of statistical methods implemented in Python for galaxy classification and probabilistic inference from photometry. The methods use a reference sample with known galaxy properties. They rely on explicit, physically interpretable criteria and make no assumptions about the functional form of the color distributions. Binary selections are calibrated using either linear color conditions, particularly suited to background galaxy selection, or flexible color--color grids, seeking to maximize completeness given a threshold on purity. For probabilistic inference, the code identifies reference objects with compatible colors within photometric uncertainties to estimate each test galaxy's probability of satisfying user-defined criteria, as well as probability density functions of continuous properties such as redshift. The code also reconstructs property distributions of selected galaxy populations using photometrically similar galaxies in the reference sample. This framework supports prior weights and reference redshift probability distributions. A built-in feature-selection method identifying informative colors is also introduced. We demonstrate applications to background galaxy selection, galaxy population classification, tomographic redshift calibration, and photometric redshift estimation. The code achieves results consistent with those obtained through machine-learning approaches, such as self-organizing maps, while remaining computationally efficient, making it suitable for large photometric surveys and future Stage IV cosmological analyses. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/GiorgioLesci/FOMO-Z.

papers.title: Proof of the entropic $c$-theorem
papers.abstract: We prove an entropic $c$-theorem in two dimensions by constructing a $c$-function from the mutual information between spacelike separated wedges, defined through the relative entropy. The proof follows Casini and Huerta's, with strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy replaced by increasing differences of the mutual information, which we prove directly in the continuum from the split property and standard properties of relative entropy. The benefit of relative entropy is that every quantity we use is finite and no cutoff ever needs to be introduced. The assumptions of the theorem are only the standard axioms of algebraic quantum field theory, the split property with finite mutual information across a gap (both implied by modular $p$-nuclearity), and a finite ultraviolet bound on the resulting $c$-functions. We also note that, formally, the $c$-function is proportional to the minimal averaged null energy of a state that reproduces the vacuum correlations between the two wedges.

papers.title: GraphTFactor: A graph-based approach for proteins transcription factor prediction
papers.abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) play an important role in regulating gene expression, making their identification a fundamental task in computational biology. In this work, we propose GraphTFactor, a novel end-to-end framework that models protein sequences as graphs and directly classifies transcription factors. By encoding sequences into graph structures, the proposed approach naturally handles variable-length inputs while preserving relevant relational information, without imposing length constraints. Experimental results show that GraphTFactor outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of graph-based representations for TF prediction while providing interpretable insights into the sequence regions contributing to the model's predictions. To support reproducibility and practical adoption, we release an open-source software package and an interactive web application that let users easily perform TF prediction on custom sequences.

papers.title: Phenomenological Chiral Effective Field Theory for Neutrino Event Generators
papers.abstract: Single-pion production is a crucial interaction channel for accelerator-based neutrino experiments, which rely on neutrino event generators for its cross sections. However, no model implemented in current generators provides a consistent and systematically improvable description of the resonance region. In this work, we develop a phenomenological chiral effective field theory model of pion production, built from nucleons, pions, and the $Δ(1232)$ with consistent, spin 3/2, gauge-invariant couplings, and we implement it in a fully automated pipeline from the Lagrangian to events using FeynRules, UFO 2.0, and Sherpa. We validate our results with pion photoproduction data and compare against neutrino bubble chamber, MINERvA, T2K, MicroBooNE, MiniBooNE, and electron-carbon scattering data. The framework can be systematically improved by extending the Lagrangian with higher-order operators and additional degrees of freedom, and by refitting couplings and form factors as new data become available. Combined with nuclear model interfaces, our approach opens a path to resonance-region predictions that meet the needs of next-generation experiments.

papers.title: Quantum Monte-Carlo study of spin-valley ferromagnetism in rhombohedral graphene
papers.abstract: Recent capacitance measurements in bilayer and trilayer rhombohedral graphene reported large magnetic entropy above the Curie temperature, suggesting the formation of fluctuating local moments. Further experimental support comes from scanning tunneling microscopy experiments in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, which directly visualized honeycomb electron-crystal order that strengthens upon heating before melting, related to the Pomeranchuk effect. Motivated by these experiments, we construct spin-valley local-moment Hamiltonians for the quarter-metal and half-metal phases. We extract their couplings from constrained Hartree-Fock calculations, and solve their finite-temperature thermodynamics with stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo. For the quarter metal we find a continuous 2D-Ising transition at $T_c \approx 0.7$ K, an order of magnitude smaller than the Hartree-Fock estimate (~30 K) and closer to the experimental scale of a few kelvin. For the half metal, we study the field-induced magnetization as a function of temperature with and without proximity-enhanced spin-orbit coupling. When spin-orbit coupling is negligible, intervalley Hund's coupling enhances the magnetic response. Strong spin-orbit coupling, as can be induced by a neighboring transition-metal dichalcogenide, gives rise to the standard spin-canted ground state at zero temperature. Upon heating, the in-plane polarization decreases more rapidly than the out-of-plane polarization. Surprisingly, despite the itinerant nature of the electrons, local-moment models with microscopically determined couplings appear to capture key finite-temperature magnetic properties of rhombohedral graphene without any fitting.

papers.title: Theory of Convective Diffusion
papers.abstract: We obtain a hydrodynamic theory of diffusive-scale dynamics in one-dimensional systems with interacting sound modes in the absence of self-interactions. Chaotic systems generically feature three distinct Gaussian relaxation processes: besides normal diffusion, driven by microscopic noise stemming from fast-decaying non-hydrodynamic modes, collisions between sound modes lead to two additional channels: convective diffusion manifesting as an effective multiplicative temporal noise, and an effective additive noise generated by the surrounding hydrodynamic modes. Our theory also includes, as a subclass, integrable systems described by generalized hydrodynamics, representing a pure realization of convective diffusion. Focusing on convective diffusion, we obtain an exact closed-form expression for the higher-point dynamical correlation functions and contrast their structure with those of normal diffusion. Additionally, we show that in convective diffusion each sound mode features a universal non-Gaussian distribution of charge transfer in its comoving frame, thereby establishing anomalous fluctuations as a characteristic feature of diffusive-scale dynamics in integrable systems.

papers.title: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs
papers.abstract: We study first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph. For strongly observable graphs, [ACBDK15] establishes a minimax regret of $\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{αT})$, where $α$ denotes the independence number of the graph and $T$ denotes the horizon. On the other hand, the best existing first-order bound scales as $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{(κ+1) L^\star})$ [LLZ20], where $κ$ denotes the clique partition number, satisfying $κ+1\geqα$, and $L^\star$ denotes the cumulative loss of the best arm, leaving a gap between the graph dependence in worst-case and first-order guarantees. In this paper, we bridge this gap by obtaining an expected regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$. Our first result is an algorithm for the special case of self-aware graphs, in which every vertex has a self-loop. The algorithm combines the update of EXP3 [ACBFS02] with a sampling rule inspired by exploration by optimization [LS20]. More specifically, we construct a map whose fixed points yield sampling distributions that control the one-round regret remainder in terms of the learner's loss and the graph's independence number, which is crucial in deriving optimal first-order guarantees. We further show that a sufficiently accurate fixed point can be computed in polynomial time by a geometrically convergent iteration. Finally, we extend the algorithm to general strongly observable graphs and achieve the same $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{αL^\star}+α)$ guarantee by adapting the two-level aggregation approach of [LLZ20].

papers.title: Maxwell-Consistent 3-D Magnetic Field Camera using Scalar-Potential-Based Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Various applications require accurate 3-D characterization of magnetic fields with high spatial and temporal resolution. Building on our previously introduced spherical magnetic field camera employing 86 three-axis Hall sensors arranged on a spherical surface, we present a novel magnetic-field reconstruction approach based on the magnetic scalar potential and its spherical harmonic expansion. Unlike the previous reconstruction method that expands each vector component separately, our scalar-potential-based formulation is inherently consistent with Maxwell's equations for source-free fields by design, yielding curl-free and divergence-free field models. Using a simulated magnetic gradient field generated by two permanent magnets, we demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher reconstruction accuracy, improved robustness to sensor noise and failure, and substantially reduced non-physical divergence and curl compared to the component-wise baseline. Furthermore, the scalar-potential approach attains superior performance with fewer coefficients, indicating a more efficient use of measurement data allowing higher-degree polynomial representations.

papers.title: From Quantum Field Fluctuations to High-Redshift AGN: Semiclassical Origins of Halo Mass Function Constraints in the JWST Era
papers.abstract: We develop a continuous framework connecting quantum field fluctuations in the early Universe to the abundance and observable properties of galaxies and active galactic nuclei (AGN) at cosmic dawn. Beginning with quantum fields in curved Friedmann Lemaitre Robertson Walker spacetime, we follow inflationary vacuum fluctuations into the primordial curvature spectrum, linear matter power spectrum, mass variance $σ(M,z)$, mass peak height $ν(M,z)$, and the statistics of nonlinear halo formation. The Press-Schechter and Sheth-Tormen formalisms provide an analytic description of halo abundance and its dependence on peak rarity. A complementary high redshift halo mass function calibrated with the GUREFT simulations of Yung et al. (2024) provides a numerical description specifically constructed for the cosmic dawn regime probed by JWST. The comparison between these analytic and simulation calibrated prescriptions provides a direct measure of the sensitivity of predicted halo populations to the observations. We separate this cosmological supply of halos from the astrophysical and observational mappings that produce stars, ultraviolet luminosities, and active galactic nuclei. Controlled numerical experiments show that a percent level perturbation in the primordial fluctuation amplitude produces only a modest change in $σ$ and $ν$, but can strongly amplify the exponentially suppressed high $ν$ tail of the Halo Mass Function. This sensitivity increases toward high halo mass and high redshift, identifying rare cosmic dawn populations as potentially powerful probes of primordial statistics while simultaneously exposing the importance of uncertainties in halo abundance. High redshift AGN population statistics and the Ultraviolet Luminosity Function provide additional constraints on the primordial power spectrum and dynamics of primordial inflation theory.

papers.title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
papers.abstract: Estimating biased finite-memory sources from a single trajectory is a fundamental problem with practical impact, for example in estimating entropy for cryptography. We study order-$d$ binary sources whose conditional probabilities have bias at most $ε$, and establish *sharp* sample complexity bounds: relative accuracy $γ$ with confidence $1-δ$ needs $γ^{-2}\,(\tfrac12-ε)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\tfrac1δ)$ samples up to constants depending on $ε$, with matching upper and lower bounds and no dependence on mixing time or spectral gap. The proof rests on a sharp bound on expected hitting times of the sliding-window (de Bruijn) chain, which stay of order $1/π(w)$ uniformly in $d$ exactly when $ε<\tfrac3{10}$, and on majorization of the window masses by those of independent biased coins. Applied to published entropy-source validations, the bounds show that their trace lengths may be underpowered: $10^6$ bits cannot resolve all transitions of an $8$-bit model to better than about $4.5\%$ relative error.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic flow in the gut hinders the fixation of beneficial mutants but accelerates their invasion
papers.abstract: Gut bacteria experience a spatially structured environment with hydrodynamic flow. Using a branching-process approach, we show that beneficial mutants arising randomly upon division have a reduced fixation probability compared to the well-mixed case. The suppression factor is set by the spatial heterogeneity of mutant fate across the gut. In contrast, the invasion of mutant lineages that avoid early stochastic extinction is accelerated in the gut compared to a matched well-mixed case. Stronger advective flow decreases fixation probabilities while accelerating mutant invasion.

papers.title: Bounds on the minimum orbital period of general static spherical black holes: a sharp upper bound and a conditional lower bound
papers.abstract: We investigate bounds on the minimum orbital period around four-dimensional general static spherical black holes. For all static spherically symmetric black holes with an event horizon, asymptotic flatness and non-negative energy density outside the horizon, we prove $T_{\min}\leq 6\sqrt{3}\,πM$. The bound is sharp and is saturated by the Schwarzschild solution. The lower bound requires an additional condition on the exterior matter: under the tangential pressure condition $p_τ\geq(κ/2)ρ$ with $κ>1$, imposed for all $r\geq r_{g}$, where $r_{g}$ is the largest radius at which $T(r)$ attains its global minimum, we prove $T_{\min}\geq c(κ)M$ with $c(κ)=6\sqrt{3}π(κ-1)\sqrt{κ+2}/κ^{3/2}$. In summary, both bounds apply to the same geometric class and differ only in what they demand of the matter: non-negative energy density suffices for the upper bound, while the lower bound is established under the additional tangential pressure condition.

papers.title: Unitarity and Positivity Constraints on C- or P-odd Anomalous Quartic Couplings
papers.abstract: In this work, we provide a comprehensive study of partial-wave unitarity and positivity constraints in the dimension-eight genuine anomalous quartic gauge coupling (aQGC) sector of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We extend previous partial-wave unitarity analyses to include all C- or P-odd operators, thereby completing the coverage of the full basis of 34 operators. We also derive an analytical set of necessary forward-limit positivity bounds that include all CP-odd Wilson coefficients. We demonstrate that non-vanishing CP-odd Wilson coefficients require non-vanishing contributions from the CP-even sector to satisfy the derived positivity conditions. Combining the positivity conditions with partial-wave unitarity, we obtain stronger bounds on twenty-three of the thirty-four Wilson coefficients in this sector of the SMEFT.

papers.title: Galaxy cluster thermodynamics at z=1.7: Resolved tSZ and X-ray analysis of CL J0459.6-4946
papers.abstract: Measurements of the entropy and temperature distribution of the intracluster medium (ICM) of local clusters have proven pivotal for the study of cluster astrophysics. Here, we extend these measurements to $z=1.7$ with a resolved analysis of the ICM in ACT/SPT-CL J0459.6-4946. By combining high-resolution thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich measurements using new, deep ALMA Band 1 and 3 observations, with archival X-ray data, we conclude that the cluster has (i) an ICM with a flat and relatively high ($\approx 200$ keV cm$^2$) entropy distribution out to $\approx 0.3\,r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, (ii) a hot core ($T_{\mathrm{e}} \simeq 14$ keV) with a declining temperature profile, (iii) a short effective path length along the line of sight of $l_{\mathrm{eff}} \simeq (0.75 \pm 0.05) \times r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, and (iv) a clumpiness factor $C = \langle n_{\mathrm{e}}^2 \rangle / \langle n_{\mathrm{e}} \rangle^2 \simeq 1.17 \pm 0.05$ within $r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$. Its dynamic nature and high redshift suggest that the cluster is still thermalising its ICM, consistent with a relatively large hydrostatic mass bias of $b = 1 - M_{500,\mathrm{c,HE}}/M_{500,\mathrm{c,WL}} = 0.27^{+0.32}_{-0.67}$ that we measure with respect to the weak lensing mass. Furthermore, a region with low entropy and high density to the south of the cluster centre is observed in the X-rays yet absent in the Compton-$y$ map, indicating pressure equilibrium; we interpret this as a sloshing cold front -- the first such detection at high redshifts. This case study demonstrates that $\approx 3$h-long ALMA observations, combined with comparatively "short" X-ray exposures ($\approx 122$ ks), can fully characterise the ICM at high redshift, opening a path towards the thermodynamics of young and distant galaxy clusters for larger samples.

papers.title: Joint Estimation and Network Configuration in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Distributed consensus-based sensing enables a multi-agent system to collaboratively estimate an unknown state by combining local measurements with information received from neighboring agents. In practice, however, the communication network, transmission delays, and finite-rate communication directly affect the disagreement among agents. On the other hand, agreement among agents does not ensure accuracy, particularly when sensors have different measurement uncertainties. We develop a sampled consensus-plus-innovations framework under realistic wireless network constraints that jointly accounts for inter-agent disagreement and estimation inaccuracy. We derive a computable upper bound on the worst-case steady-state estimation error that captures consensus disagreement due to the communication graph, quantization error, and transmission delay, together with estimation inaccuracy, which accounts for measurement uncertainty against the true state. We then use this bound as a network design objective and propose a semi-distributed auction-based algorithm that jointly modifies the communication graph and link-rate allocation. The proposed method preserves connectivity, converges in finite time to a locally auction-stable network configuration, and reduces the bound on the estimation error at every accepted change. The proposed method has been evaluated on various test cases, and the results show that it reduces the estimation error while maintaining fewer links and allocating moderate link rates in a short time.

papers.title: The signature-changing soft-gluon term as a possible source of non-planar $ζ_2$ terms at small $x$ in the non-singlet quark-plus-antiquark splitting function
papers.abstract: A relation underlying resummations at small momentum fraction $x$ predicts the highest logarithms of quark-plus-antiquark flavor-difference splitting functions from lower orders. Complete three- and four-loop results violate it at third-highest logarithms by pi-squared terms suppressed for many colors, of unexplained origin and color structure. At four loops Moch and Vogt suggested a squared imaginary phase. We retain the signature-changing soft-gluon term also in positive signature in Kirschner and Lipatov's double-logarithmic equations for forward quark-antiquark scattering, without derivation, with their printed negative-signature sign and adjoint Born term. We show that the proposed equations reproduce both violations in full color for quark-plus-antiquark flavor differences at zero power of $x$, fixed coupling and first order in pi squared, for defining-representation quarks of special unitary groups with at least three colors. The proposed equations at third-highest logarithms use one wave per exchanged color and signature, the retained term at lowest-order strength as the positive-signature color-neutral channel's only new source of these violations, no such terms from gluons across the softest exchanged quark-antiquark pair at comparable or larger transverse momentum, and unchanged quark-pair normalization in the splitting function. This agreement gives three independent tests of one system with no continuous coefficient adjusted to the violations, although corresponding non-quartic quark-minus-antiquark terms are missed. In the proposed equations, the retained term weighted by this phase is a possible origin of both violations. The equations predict these full-color five-loop quark-plus-antiquark terms if the relation otherwise holds and no new source first acts at five loops. Confirmation would support the retained term as the origin of the violations through five loops.

papers.title: The Yottascale at Tera-$Z$: Petascale SUSY?
papers.abstract: As experimental and theoretical advances are made, the paradigm of grand unification faces growing challenges. In light of what has been learned at the LHC, from Higgs mass measurement and direct searches for supersymmetry, we contrast the current theoretical predictions in a simplified supersymmetric grand unified theory against present and future experimental precision, focussing on threshold corrections and renormalisation group effects above the electroweak scale. More precisely, the theoretical precision is juxtaposed to the experimental one. Especially, the impact of a future Tera-$Z$ factory such as FCC-ee is examined, while also considering the expected future improvement of proton decay constraints. We find that the improvement on the measurement of the gauge couplings expected at Tera-$Z$ will yield sensitivity to higher loop orders in the evolution of the couplings up to the Yottascale, calling for further theoretical efforts. In a minimal $\rm{SU}(5)$ scenario with nearly degenerate SUSY spectrum, we study the impact of the proton decay constraint on the SUSY scale, comparing 2- and 3-loop analyses. While the 2-loop results point to a SUSY scale around 1 PeV, the 3-loop analysis seems to exclude the model entirely. This follows from the fact that at 1-loop in the GUT threshold corrections, the mass of the colour-triplet Higgs is completely determined by the IR parameters. This \textit{IR determination} is not accidental, but rooted in the group structure and breaking of the GUT theory.

papers.title: All Symmetries and Boundaries of the Two-Dimensional Free Scalar from Continuous Flat-Gauging
papers.abstract: We propose a remote detectability criterion for two-dimensional conformal field theories, which asserts that any local operator outside of the product of the left- and right-moving Virasoro algebras can be detected by some topological line defect. We discuss its relationship to existing results in the conformal net literature. We then use this criterion to argue that the known $SU(2)$ moduli space of unitary conformal boundary conditions and the $SO(4)$ moduli space of unitary topological line defects of the $SU(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model completely capture all unitary conformal boundaries and unitary topological lines of the theory. Invoking the fact that the non-compact boson conformal field theory can be obtained from $SU(2)_1$ by "flat-gauging" a $U(1)$ symmetry, we are also able to completely classify the unitary conformal boundaries and unitary topological line defects of the two-dimensional free scalar field. In particular, we find a 4-dimensional moduli space of topological line defects, most of which were not known previously. We support our proposed classifications by writing down concrete Lagrangian descriptions of all of the boundaries and lines of the non-compact boson. For every boundary condition, we calculate the corresponding boundary state, and for each pair of boundary conditions, we calculate the corresponding interval Hilbert space. We verify that the annulus partition functions of the theory respect open/closed duality. We also calculate the fusion rules of the topological line defects, their action on local operators, their action on the boundary conditions by parallel fusion, and their corresponding twisted-sector Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
papers.abstract: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.

papers.title: Integral Hodge structures and atoms of fourfolds
papers.abstract: Following the recent work by OpenAI on the irrationality of very general cubic fourfolds in Hassett divisors, we prove some compatibility of Iritani's blow-up formula with the classical blow-up decomposition of integral Hodge structures. As a consequence, we express OpenAI's birational invariant in terms of the theory of atoms developped by Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu. We also show that, for every smooth complex rational cubic fourfold, the primitive cohomology is isometric as an integral Hodge structure to the twisted middle cohomology of a K3 surface and we prove irrationality of the very general Verra fourfold.

papers.title: Beyond the Kubo formula: unification of adiabatic and isothermal response in quantum systems
papers.abstract: The static limit of the Kubo susceptibility describes the adiabatic response of an isolated quantum system, in which energy-level occupations remain unchanged, and generally differs from the isothermal susceptibility, where these occupations readjust to thermal equilibrium. In this work, we introduce a single dynamical framework in which the adiabatic and isothermal responses arise naturally as two distinct limiting regimes. This can be done by considering explicitly an open system version of the Kubo approach in which the dissipation is governed by a typical thermalization rate of the system. By exchanging the order of the static limit and of the vanishing thermalization rate limit, the protocol yields either the adiabatic or isothermal response. This protocol has a solid physical motivation in terms of the thermalization dynamics and is valid for generic systems. We apply it to the case of the magnetic response of the electron gas and reproduce the expected results.

papers.title: Tate and Artin--Tate Motivic Tensor-Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: We compute the Balmer spectra of geometric Tate and Artin--Tate motives with $\mathbb{F}_p$-coefficients over any field whose characteristic differs from $p$. For Tate motives, we find the bigraded comparison map to be a homeomorphism to the homogeneous spectrum of the motivic cohomology of the base field. For Artin--Tate motives, we describe the spectrum as a gluing of the spectrum of Artin motives computed by Balmer--Gallauer with the punctured Tate spectrum. We determine all specialisations between these pieces and the resulting topology. Under the hypothesis that the spectrum of rational Tate motives is a singleton, we also compute the integral Tate spectrum after inverting the exponential characteristic of the base field. As a consequence of our results, we identify the punctured Tate spectrum as an open subspace of the spectrum of the category of geometric Voevodsky motives, and draw some conclusions concerning the latter. Finally, we include an appendix where we define generalised periodicity in the context of tensor-triangular geometry, and explore its applications in motivic settings.

papers.title: Fock-space delocalization and its control in scarred-vs-ergodic dynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum many-body scarred dynamics in Rydberg-atom arrays is characterized by revivals, in which the system repeatedly returns to its initial state despite its many-body complexity. But how extensively does the wave function explore the space of allowed configurations between revivals? We address this question by quantifying the fraction of configurations occupied during PXP dynamics initialized from the paradigmatic polarized and Néel states, which respectively exhibit thermalizing and scarred dynamics. Despite their striking revivals, dynamics from the Néel state spreads over exponentially many configurations, yet occupies a vanishing fraction of the full space in the thermodynamic limit. Dynamics from the polarized state, by contrast, occupies a finite fraction of the configuration space, close to anticoncentration and random-state statistics, although chiral symmetry limits this fraction to one third. A weak quasiperiodic field enables the polarized state to occupy half of the configuration space by lifting the constraint imposed by chiral symmetry. The Néel state, however, requires a stronger field to reach a comparable anticoncentrated regime. As the field increases further, the occupied fraction decreases for both initial states, revealing a nonmonotonic dependence of Fock-space delocalization on field strength without necessarily implying localization.

papers.title: Effects of Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld Gravity on Black Hole Accretion
papers.abstract: Black holes offer a unique setting to test gravity in the strong-field regime, where deviations from General Relativity are expected to be most pronounced. We study how modified gravity changes the structure of an advection-dominated accretion flow (ADAF) around a supermassive black hole. The gravitational field governing the disc is described by a Paczyński--Wiita-like potential derived in Eddington-inspired Born--Infeld (EiBI) gravity, formulated \textit{à la} Palatini. We solve the ADAF-like equations for this potential and compare the radial profiles of the flow with those obtained for the standard Paczyński--Wiita potential. The largest difference appears in the gas density, which is several orders of magnitude higher in the EiBI case near the inner region and converges to the standard result at large radii. The specific angular momentum and temperature are lower in EiBI gravity, while the radial velocity differs mainly at large radii for both solution branches, $ s=-1$ and $+1$. The angular velocity and the disk aspect ratio $H/r$ change only slightly. These results show that EiBI gravity can modify the density structure of hot accretion flows in the strong-field regime, potentially providing observational discriminators.

papers.title: Layered Wire-Grid Haloscope for Millielectronvolt Axions and Dark Photons
papers.abstract: We propose MADGRID (Millielectronvolt Axions and Dark photons with layered GRIDs), a few wire grids in front of a mirror, tuned by their spacing, forming an epsilon-near-zero slab that radiates through its face into external optics. Unlike wire-plasma haloscopes, the signal need not cross the lossy medium to reach an antenna, and metal grids replace the disks of dielectric haloscopes. A 1 m$^2$ array in 10 T could probe axion-photon couplings below the CAST bound up to 1.4 meV with kinetic-inductance detectors, and KSVZ couplings over 0.8-3.9 meV with future photon counters. Without a magnet, it could probe dark photon mixings down to $3.4\times10^{-16}$.

papers.title: Relating approaches to interacting quantum clocks and systems
papers.abstract: The problem of describing the dynamics of quantum systems relative to quantum clocks with which they interact is relevant to the physics of quantum reference frames and quantum gravity alike. There have been different approaches that derive a relational time-dependent Schrödinger equation for the system relative to the clock from a time-independent Hamiltonian constraint. We show that some of these approaches, due to Smith and Ahmadi, Gemsheim and Rost, as well as the so-called Born-Oppenheimer approach, can be unified in a single framework for describing conditional quantum states. In particular, the Born-Oppenheimer approach to quantum cosmology is seen to correspond to a type of interacting Page-Wootters formalism. We discuss the issue of unitarity and linearity, or lack thereof, in the relational dynamics, and we conclude with a brief outlook to further developments.

papers.title: Cosmic merger rates and population evolution of binary black hole mergers in AGN disks
papers.abstract: Active galactic nuclei (AGN) disks are promising sites for hierarchical binary black hole (BBH) mergers, which next-generation gravitational-wave detectors will probe out to high redshift. Predicting their contribution requires linking BBH evolution in AGN disks to the poorly constrained high-redshift evolution of active supermassive black holes (SMBHs). We introduce ARISE (AGN Rates and Intrinsic Stellar-BH Evolution), a framework that embeds semi-analytical models of BBH evolution in AGN disks into a cosmological description of the AGN number density, SMBH mass function, Eddington-ratio distribution, and nuclear metallicity. We consider a conservative AGN-abundance model anchored to observed luminosity functions, as well as Eddington-limited and super-Eddington scenarios based on the CAT cosmological model, compatible with JWST observations of high-redshift AGNs. The merger-rate density is set primarily by the disk viscosity parameter $α$: at $z = 0.2$, we find a rate of $12$--$37$ Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$ for $α= 0.01$ and $0.5$--$6$ Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$ for $α= 0.1$. The redshift evolution depends strongly on how SMBHs grow. The rate density peaks at $z \simeq 1.8$, $3.3$, and $3.9$ ($1.5$, $3.6$, and $3.9$) for $α=0.01$ ($0.1$) in the conservative, Eddington-limited, and super-Eddington models, respectively, and in the super-Eddington model it stays nearly flat out to $z \simeq 10$. For $α= 0.1$, AGN disks account for $\sim 2$--$40\%$ of the LVK-inferred merger rate, consistent with current upper limits from GW--AGN associations. For $α= 0.01$, they match or exceed it. The Einstein Telescope (ET) should detect $\sim 10^{5}$ ($\sim 10^{4}$) AGN-disk mergers per year for $α= 0.01$ ($0.1$). ET will test the AGN channel at redshifts where the AGN population models differ most strongly, providing independent constraints on the growth of early SMBHs.

papers.title: Singlet-Triplet Transition of Rotating Moiré Atoms in a Magnetic Field
papers.abstract: Moiré superlattices can bind several electrons to each potential minimum, forming few-electron "moiré atoms." Using neural quantum states that obey magnetic periodic boundary conditions, include full Landau-level mixing, and treat both spin sectors, we map the ground state of two-electron moiré atoms in a superlattice as a function of moiré depth and magnetic field strength. At strong field each atom is a spin-triplet maximum-density droplet with canonical angular momentum $\langle L_z\rangle=-1$ and a persistent circulating current: the rotating counterpart of the "Wigner molecular crystal" recently imaged in moiré superlattices. Deepening the wells drives a singlet-triplet transition to non-rotating spin-singlet atoms whose only current is a weak diamagnetic counter-circulation. The transition moves to deeper wells as the field grows, so depth and field together open a window for the formation of rotors. This is the collective analog of the singlet-triplet transition of two-electron quantum dots. At the transition, the orbital magnetic moments of the atoms reverse sign as their spin polarization switches, a joint signature accessible to magnetometry. If the atoms are instead polarized by other means, such as magnetic proximity coupling, the rotors lock at weak field into a spontaneously ordered crystal of dimers in a pinwheel pattern.

papers.title: Model-independent and reconstruction-free evidence for cosmic acceleration from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations
papers.abstract: While there is ample evidence that the universe's expansion is accelerating, most of this evidence relies on assuming a shape of the relative expansion rate, $H(z)/H_0$, informed by a cosmological model or a kinematical approach. Model-independent analyses are common for supernova datasets but rarely applied to other data. In this work, we use uncalibrated baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) from DESI DR2 for a model-independent test of acceleration, which makes no assumptions about the theory of gravity or the energy content of the universe. We test for cosmic acceleration with three model-independent statistics that rely purely on the measured Alcock-Paczyński parameter, the isotropic BAO, and the line-of-sight BAO, and do not require any reconstruction between redshift bins unlike previous analyses. Accounting for the look-elsewhere effect, among all statistics we find $2.4σ$ - $4.1σ$ evidence for cosmic acceleration within $0 \leq z \leq 0.934$ when assuming flatness; allowing for spatial curvature, $|Ω_k| \leq 1$, at least two of the three statistics retain $2.4σ$ - $3.5σ$.

papers.title: Bridging Scales: Multi-Zone GRMHD-Informed Anisotropic AGN Feedback in Galaxies
papers.abstract: We present a galaxy-scale black hole (BH) accretion and feedback model incorporating results from multi-zone general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations spanning the event horizon to the Bondi radius. The model replaces a fixed suppression of the Bondi rate with a nuclear-environment-dependent factor, $κ^{\rm hot}_{\rm cho}$, set by the local ratio of Bondi to gravitational radius, and distributes outflow mass, kinetic energy, and thermal energy according to the angular structure measured in the large-dynamic-range GRMHD calculations. We apply it to idealized isolated simulations of an M87*-like massive elliptical and a Milky Way/Sgr A*-like galaxy, spanning over three orders of magnitude in BH mass without tuning accretion or feedback efficiencies to match observables. In the M87*-like system, the GRMHD-informed angle-dependent feedback model suppresses late-time stellar mass growth more effectively than the isotropic reference model, despite similar long-term BH accretion rates. Varying the uncertain mass loading of the collimated polar component has a modest impact on BH growth and star formation, indicating that feedback anisotropy matters more than its detailed mass loading. We find that $κ^{\rm hot}_{\rm cho}$ varies with nuclear environment and time, yielding BH growth histories markedly different from fixed-suppression models. For Sgr A*, this variable factor yields an accretion rate more consistent with Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) constraints than a fixed, suppressed Bondi model. These results show that nuclear-environment-dependent accretion and feedback angular structure affect BH-galaxy evolution, requiring subgrid models to include more than a universal Bondi suppression factor and a scalar feedback efficiency.

papers.title: Umbilic Observatories
papers.abstract: We study gravitational dynamics for the simplest example of an umbilic boundary in four-dimensional general relativity --- a three-dimensional de Sitter hypersurface embedded in a four-dimensional Minkowski world. Generally speaking, an umbilic surface has the property that its induced metric is proportional to its extrinsic curvature. We consider the case of both conformal boundary conditions, as well as Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed at the timelike hypersurface. For both cases, we find that there are no linearised modes whose imaginary frequency grows with angular momentum. The conformal boundary conditions allow for a dynamical boundary degree of freedom, in addition to the bulk excitations. The umbilic property linearly decouples the boundary Weyl mode from the bulk dynamics, yielding linearly stable dynamics. In contrast, the Dirichlet problem has no boundary mode. The umbilic hypersurfaces may thus constitute an improved starting point for defining gravitational dynamics in the presence of a timelike boundary. Throughout our analysis, we draw parallels to the structure of spatial infinity for asymptotically Minkowski spacetimes and a more finite realisation thereof.

papers.title: Conformal boundaries and the photon sphere of AdS black holes
papers.abstract: We study linearized gravitational perturbations of four-dimensional Schwarzschild-AdS black holes with finite timelike boundaries subject to conformal boundary conditions. These fix the conformal class of the induced metric and the mean curvature, while allowing the boundary Weyl mode to fluctuate. The photon sphere plays a distinguished role in this problem: a static boundary at this radius is totally umbilic, and the scalar problem separates exactly into independent bulk and boundary sectors. We prove the absence of exponentially growing scalar and vector modes for spherical harmonics of degree two and higher. We determine how large angular momentum instabilities are suppressed as the boundary approaches umbilicity. Near the horizon, we recover the universal Rindler spectrum, including sound and shear excitations. We numerically follow these fluid modes as the boundary is moved outwards and find that they approach standard gravitational quasinormal modes at the asymptotic AdS$_4$ boundary. For large black holes, these asymptotic endpoints correspond to the sound and shear poles of the dual three-dimensional conformal field theory. We also study perturbations of the AdS$_4$ black brane, where we find an analogous continuation of the fluid modes in the absence of an intermediate umbilic boundary.

papers.title: Separation of variables for massive spin-2 fields on the Kerr black hole
papers.abstract: Massive spin-2 fields on the Kerr black hole generally obey coupled partial differential equations. We show that these equations separate through two commuting angular operators acting on five components of the field, its curl and its linearised Weyl tensor. A joint angular eigenfunction fixes the relative profiles of the five polarisations and leaves one second-order radial equation. The separation constants satisfy an algebraic relation that follows from the angular operators themselves. The construction removes the obstruction to a Teukolsky-type equation by a radial transport identity, then eliminates the additional radial solution through a first integral. It provides ordinary differential equations for massive spin-2 fields on Kerr, and, equivalently, for Kaluza-Klein perturbations of the Kerr black string.

papers.title: Monopole-Fermion Scattering from Twisted Conformal Boundary States
papers.abstract: We derive monopole-fermion scattering correlators from conformal boundary states in twisted sectors. The key ingredient is that symmetry-preserving boundary conditions contain sectors twisted by topological symmetry lines. Their overlaps determine correlators of operators attached to these lines, including the outgoing excitations required by charge conservation in the Callan-Rubakov effect. We construct the twisted boundary states of $N$ free Dirac fermions with $U(1)^N$-preserving boundary conditions, extending the familiar description in terms of charge lattices to shifted lattices describing twisted sectors. Using cluster decomposition and open-closed duality, we determine their coefficients and fix their normalization relative to the untwisted boundary state. We find that the Callan-Rubakov boundary condition yields a two-point function between an incoming fermion and an outgoing defect operator with a coefficient of unit modulus, even when the corresponding correlators of ordinary local fermions vanish. Finally, we relate these correlators to four-dimensional partial-wave scattering using gauge-covariant asymptotic states. We identify the missing $s$-wave contribution to the unitarity relation and argue that the twisted channel supplies it with precisely the required normalization.

papers.title: Leaking Sound Waves: Gravitational Waves From Dark Sectors Weakly Coupled to the Standard Model
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions in a dark sector can produce an observable stochastic gravitational-wave background, and many models predicting such signals in current and future experiments have been explored. For moderately strong transitions, hydrodynamical simulations suggest that sound waves generated by the expansion and collisions of true-vacuum bubbles are the dominant source of gravitational waves. It is often assumed that these sound waves propagate only within the dark-sector fluid, while the impact of the visible sector is neglected. In this paper, we investigate the effects of a weak coupling between the dark and visible fluids on the resulting gravitational-wave signal. We adopt a phenomenological hydrodynamical description of two ultra-relativistic fluids, parametrizing their interactions without specifying an underlying microscopic model. We focus on the regime in which the coupling can be neglected during the phase transition but becomes relevant during the subsequent, longer-lasting period of sound wave propagation. Within this framework, we analytically show that, even if the bubble expansion initially affects only the dark fluid, sound waves can subsequently be induced in the visible sector. Using the sound-shell model, we find that, despite the additional sound waves generated in the visible sector, the total gravitational-wave signal sourced by both fluids is generally suppressed compared to the case of a completely decoupled dark sector. This suppression becomes more pronounced for larger interaction rates and a larger ratio of relativistic degrees of freedom in the visible sector to those in the dark sector. The coupling also modifies the shape of the gravitational-wave spectrum.

papers.title: Missing Mergers: On the Unexpected Delay-Time Distribution of Binary Neutron Star Mergers
papers.abstract: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration has detected two binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, GW170817 and GW190425. While no clear electromagnetic counterpart was discovered for GW190425, a coincident counterpart to GW170817 (GRB170817A, AT 2017gfo) was discovered in an early-type galaxy, NGC 4993. Using broad-band photometry and an integrated optical spectrum, we measure a mass-weighted age of $12.4^{+0.5}_{-0.7}$ Gyr (90% credible) for NGC 4993, which is an estimate of the delay time between star formation and merger for the GW170817 progenitor. BNS systems are expected to have a power-law delay-time distribution (DTD) with a minimum delay time, $t_{\rm min}$, of ~10 Myr and index $α\approx -1$. This canonical DTD, convolved with the cosmic star-formation history, predicts ~16 BNS mergers at delay times of ~100 Myr for every BNS merger at 10 Gyr; under it, the chance of detecting even one merger as old as GW170817 is ~1.8%. The long delay time of GW170817 therefore implies many "missing" shorter-delay mergers if the canonical DTD holds. A DTD with $t_{\rm min} = 12.6$ Gyr and $α= -1$ is favored over the canonical DTD by a factor of 40-140, and over short gamma-ray burst and Galactic double-NS DTDs by factors of 80-280. These results are in tension with current population synthesis models, the Milky Way double NS population, and the SGRB population. Explaining the LVK population requires either a dramatically different separation distribution than commonly assumed, an additional channel with a long delay time and comparable rate to an isolated-binary formation scenario, or a large population of BNS mergers missed in the LVK analysis. This result has wide-ranging implications for binary-population synthesis, chemical enrichment models, connections between BNS mergers and SGRBs, and future gravitational wave observations.

papers.title: On Boundary State Screening via Solitons
papers.abstract: We present a coarse classification scheme for the boundary data of massive QFTs based on transitions of boundary states via soliton / kink profiles. Starting from the lattice of boundary states, we introduce the boundary screening group $\mathbb{B}$: the equivalence classes of boundary states which cannot be connected by such transitions. In string theory backgrounds which geometrically engineer an interacting QFT in the target space, $\mathbb{B}$ computes the worldsheet analog of the target space defect group $\mathbb{D}$. When $\mathbb{B}$ is non-zero, it provides a diagnostic for having a target space with non-normalizable modes. For interfaces between QFTs, similar considerations imply the existence of a non-trivial conserved charge associated with soliton absorption / transmission, which means that the interface cannot fully dissolve / disappear. Similar considerations hold for junctions of QFTs, which in the special case of string worldsheet CFTs translate to junctions of string theories. We illustrate these general considerations with a number of non-geometric 2D $\mathcal{N} = (2,2)$ Landau-Ginzburg models, as well as their natural lifts to 4D $\mathcal{N} = 1$ Wess-Zumino models.

papers.title: On the Role of Gravity in Supercooled Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Theories with radiative mass generation and radiative symmetry breaking (RSB) lead to first-order phase transitions (FOPTs) and the production of gravitational waves (GWs) as well as primordial black holes if supercooling lasts long enough. Here we investigate the role of gravity in supercooled FOPTs that occur in the RSB scenario. We use a model-independent approach that is valid when a quantity (which we explicitly determine and is computable once the model is specified) is small enough. Eventually, the curvature of spacetime becomes relevant if the FOPT does not complete in the case in which gravity is ignored. We also include the effect on the FOPT of the non-minimal couplings with coefficients of zero mass dimension. Depending on such non-minimal couplings, gravity can enhance or reduce the region of parameter space where the phase transition completes. Observable consequences of the role of gravity on the FOPT that can be probed by current and future GW detectors are then worked out and we explore the possibility that the background of GWs detected by pulsar timing arrays is produced by FOPTs in the RSB scenario. We also estimate the number of e-folds that elapse when the field playing the role of the order parameter is trapped in the false vacuum, which provides important information for cosmology.

papers.title: A Universal Approach to Hydrodynamics in Higher Dimensions via Tensor Networks
papers.abstract: Extracting late-time hydrodynamic transport properties directly from microscopic quantum models, especially in dimensions beyond one, is believed to be classically intractable. This owes, in part, to the extensive growth of entanglement in higher dimensions and often a mismatch between geometric and tensor network locality. Here, we extend the Density Matrix Truncation (DMT) algorithm to accurately and quantitatively predict high-temperature transport coefficients (e.g. diffusion constants) in up to three dimensions. Additionally, we demonstrate the ability to capture the slow crossover dynamics characteristic of weakly broken integrability. The intuition underlying our approach is to preserve the geometrically local information crucial for hydrodynamics throughout the time evolution, despite using a one-dimensional matrix product state ansatz for higher-dimensional calculations. Our work pushes the boundary of classical computability and opens the door to benchmarking the high-temperature, late-time dynamics of generic quantum simulators.

papers.title: Surprisingly normal? GW241011 and GW241110 in the context of hierarchical merger classification
papers.abstract: Uncovering the origins of merging binary black holes is a key goal in gravitational-wave astrophysics, but identifying the formation channel of a particular binary is complicated by imprecise measurements and uncertain theoretical predictions. While classification often involves computing metrics from an event's inferred properties, measurement precision varies across parameter space. Using the perhaps-surprising low masses of the hierarchical merger candidates GW241011 and GW241110 as a backdrop, we consider the classifiable distribution, which steps beyond detectability to assess what events may be correctly characterized as part of a population. Interpreting classification outcomes, and assessing the falsifiability of theoretical model predictions, are benefit by understanding the regions of parameter space that a priori enable---and do not enable---confident measurement. For hierarchical mergers, we demonstrate that mass ratio is the largest intrinsic driver of identification, while orbital inclination and signal-to-noise ratio are the key extrinsic factors. Further, we show GW241011 and GW241110 achieve classification metrics consistent with similar simulated hierarchical mergers. Model selection and classification require the context of measurement capacity, especially as catalogs offer growing numbers of events with seemingly unusual properties.

papers.title: Giant Gravitons in AdS$_5\times$SE$_5$ and the Superconformal Index of Toric Quiver Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We derive giant-graviton contributions to superconformal indices by quantizing probe D3-branes in type IIB backgrounds $\mathrm{AdS}_{5}\times SE_{5}$. For $SE_{5}=T^{1,1}$ and $Y^{p,q}$, we determine the scalar, vector, and fermionic fluctuations of maximal giant gravitons and extract their BPS spectra. The resulting single-letter indices agree with those predicted by the giant-graviton expansions of the dual toric quiver gauge theories. These results show that the single-giant terms in finite-$N$ supersymmetric counting functions can be recovered directly from quantized D3-brane degrees of freedom and point toward a universal worldvolume origin of giant-graviton expansions directly on the supergravity side. We view the results as a step in an intrinsically gravitational framework, much like the open-closed-open triality, for addressing supersymmetric microstate-counting problems that are conventionally outsourced to the dual field theory.

papers.title: DiscKosky: Efficient Genealogical Constraints from Sector-By-Sector Critical Point Counting
