Besides undetectability, we show that this scheme is provably secure against removal adversaries with batched detector access, in the sense that no probabilistic polynomial-time adversary can achieve a non-negligible advantage over an adversary restricted to adding isotropic white-noise with a $\sqrt{2}\times$ larger perturbation budget, and we show this $\sqrt{2}$ factor to be tight. Evaluations on Stable Diffusion 2.1 and XL demonstrate the attack against the existing defense, and show that our scheme preserves generation quality and withstands common perturbations and targeted removal attacks.

papers.title: Berry curvature dipole circuit quantum electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum three-wave mixing is an important resource in superconducting quantum circuits. The traditional implementation uses Josephson junction arrays and is activated by magnetic flux. Here we introduce the Berry curvature dipole (BCD) quantum circuit element, which achieves quantum three-wave mixing without breaking time-reversal symmetry. This quantum three-wave mixing results from the BCD nonlinear Hall effect in noncentrosymmetric quantum materials taken to a dissipationless, quantum coherent few-photon regime. We show how nonlinear Hall materials can be integrated to superconducting microwave circuits to accomplish multiphoton vacuum Rabi splittings and dynamical stabilization of bosonic Schrödinger cat states. Such BCD circuit quantum electrodynamics are a concrete exemplar of a physical resource for quantum information processing enabled by nonlinear response in quantum materials.

papers.title: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves by a Kerr black hole
papers.abstract: We simulate the gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) by a Kerr black hole using a $(1+1)$-dimensional time-domain mode-sum approach. To enable efficient explicit time evolution, we implement a localized hyperboloidal foliation combined with a static field redefinition, ensuring bounded characteristic speeds across an extended, uniform tortoise-coordinate grid. Incident GW initial data are constructed by projecting a plane-wave Weyl tensor onto the Kinnersley tetrad. Through local spin-dyad rotations and Wigner $D$-matrix transformations, our framework accommodates both idealized wave packets and realistic binary coalescence signals at arbitrary incidence and polarization angles. To accurately resolve the lensed waveforms, we evolve over $68,000$ coupled $(j,m)$ modes. Our results reveal that a Kerr black hole acts as a diffraction-limited thick lens, focusing GWs into a forward beam. For idealized wave packets, the primary prompt pulse exhibits a spin-independent transverse Gaussian profile, whereas the subsequent lensing coda is sensitive to the black hole's spin. For binary coalescence signals, strong-field lensing substantially modifies the post-merger ringdown. However, the lensed inspiral and merger phases in Kerr and Schwarzschild backgrounds are virtually identical, yielding waveform mismatches below $2.2\times10^{-5}$ across various inclinations and polarizations. These findings demonstrate that non-spinning Schwarzschild models provide an accurate and computationally economical surrogate to search for strong-field lensing signatures with current ground-based detectors.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal coupling enables tunable exceptional-point response in non-Hermitian circuits
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) exhibit characteristic square-root spectral responses to weak perturbations, with response magnitudes governed by configuration-dependent prefactors that are often relatively small. Modulating these prefactor while preserving the exceptional characteristics offers an additional degrees of freedom for engineering non-Hermitian sensing responses. Here, we report a nonreciprocal non-Hermitian circuit system with gyrator-meditated coupling that supports a continuous family of EP configurations. Unlike reciprocal coupling, which typically yields a unique EP configuration for balanced gain and loss, nonreciprocal coupling allows the directional forward and backward coupling strengths to be varied while maintaining their product and thus preserving the EP condition and yielding a library of EPs. This additional freedom enables continuous control of the frequency-splitting magnitude without modifying the square-root characteristic dependence on absolute perturbation strength. We show that the spectral splitting induced by a given absolute resistance perturbation can be enhanced by appropriately adjusting the coupling asymmetry. Theoretical predictions, circuit simulations, and experimental reflection-spectrum measurements consistently confirms this tunable response. Our results establish nonreciprocal coupling as an alternative approach for engineering and enhancing EP-induced perturbative responses without changing their characteristic branch-point scaling.

papers.title: Atomic Charge Chirality from Electric Multipoles
papers.abstract: We establish an electric-multipole ($Q_{lm}$) criterion for chirality of local atomic charge distributions. For the 11 crystallographic chiral point groups, we identify representative lowest-rank multipole contents required to distinguish the opposite handednesses. For the axial groups $C_n$ and $D_n$ with $n=2,3,4,6$, chirality arises from the relative orientation of two azimuthal anisotropies with $m=n$, belonging to consecutive ranks $l=n$ and $n+1$. Their coexistence produces a latitude-dependent twist of the $n$-fold charge distribution. The polar component, although allowed in $C_n$, is distinct from this chiral mechanism and is not required for handedness. The cubic groups $T$ and $O$ exhibit distinct realizations, with octahedral chirality first appearing at rank nine. We further show that, within a spinless $s$-$p$-$d$-$f$ atomic basis, the scalar charge density contains multipoles only up to rank six and therefore cannot encode the handedness of $C_6$, $D_6$, or $O$. These results connect electric-multipole content and atomic orbital degrees of freedom to the microscopic encoding of crystallographic handedness.

papers.title: Phase Retrieval of Bandlimited Signals Using a Morlet Wavelet and an Admissible Companion
papers.abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate that complex bandlimited signals can be uniquely recovered (up to a global phase factor) from two families of wavelet transform magnitudes, sampled at twice the Nyquist rate in two frequency bins. These families come from translations of the fixed dilated Morlet wavelet and a fixed companion wavelet. The companion wavelet admits an augmented Morlet--Gaussian representation. We rewrite the two families as two modulated Gaussian convolution measurements of an auxiliary bandlimited signal. Using a Gaussian convolution uniqueness result, we prove that samples on \((4B)^{-1}\mathbb{Z}\) determine every signal in \(PW_B^2\) (up to a global phase factor). Compared with earlier wavelet phase retrieval results, our approach requires significantly fewer sampling points.

papers.title: The Constructive Cavity Method for the Ising Perceptron
papers.abstract: We apply the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) to the Ising perceptron. The process starts from positive soft channels admitting an auxiliary representation $$ U(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{tx}ρ(\mathrm{d}t),\qquad ρ\ge0, $$ with an auxiliary measure having a finite exponential quadratic moment. This rewrites the perceptron as a dense, bipartite Gaussian model with an Ising layer and a continuous auxiliary layer. The CCM blanket geometry then gives two constructive variance profiles, $Q_\ell$ on the Ising side and $Γ_\ell$ on the auxiliary side. The bipartite shell scale is $$ Q_{\ell+1}Γ_{\ell+1}-Q_\ellΓ_\ell, $$ and Gaussian core comparison removes the core contribution $ΔQ_\ellΔΓ_\ell$ under blanket refinement. The scalar cavity functional has three terms, $$ \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{perc}}(ν)=\mathbb{E}\left[\log\langle2\cosh x\rangle_ν+α\log\langle U(s)\rangle_ν-\log\langle e^y\rangle_ν\right], $$ where $x$ is the new-spin field, $s$ is the new-constraint field, and $y$ is the cavity correction. CCM identifies the constructive cavity variables with the Aizenman--Sims--Starr random overlap structure (ROSt) variables. Parisi's recursive averaging then gives $$ \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{perc}}^{\mathrm{CCM}}(ζ,Q,Γ)=X_0(0)+αY_0(0)-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\ell=0}^{R}ζ_\ell\left(Q_{\ell+1}Γ_{\ell+1}-Q_\ellΓ_\ell\right). $$ The replica-symmetric specialization gives Gardner's formula for the generalized Ising perceptron. Specializing the constraint terminal to the hard channel gives the Krauth--Mézard functional for the binary perceptron.

papers.title: Signatures of Narrowband and Ultrashort-Pulse-Like Probing in Coherent Anti-Stokes Raman Scattering Using Twin Beams and Sum-Frequency Generation Readout
papers.abstract: We theoretically investigate coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) driven by bright twin beams with sum-frequency generation (SFG) readout. Expressing the SFG output in terms of quantum-field correlation functions yields multiple correlation structures with distinct properties associated with different interaction pathways on the bra and ket sides. Among them, frequency correlations between the CARS probe and SFG gating fields enable the two fields to act collectively as an effective narrowband probe, avoiding probe-induced spectral convolution. When this behavior appears on either the bra or ket side, the other retains Raman relaxation information as if probed by an ultrashort pulse.

papers.title: Harmonic brightness oscillations point to magnetar giant flares in rare short gamma-ray bursts
papers.abstract: Kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) have been observed in a few rare gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but their physical origin remains uncertain. We reanalyze the two short GRBs with reported kilohertz QPOs, GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A, and find evidence for possible harmonic-like organization around a characteristic frequency scale near 360 hertz. The similar harmonic-like pattern in GRB 910711 and in the confirmed magnetar giant flare (MGF) event GRB 200415A, including features extending above 4 kilohertz, points to timing phenomenology on frequency scales relevant to magnetar oscillation modes. The temporal and spectral similarities between the two events and the difficulty of explaining these features in merger-driven scenarios favor an MGF-like interpretation of GRB 910711. This timing phenomenology may therefore provide an additional observational handle, complementary to spectral, temporal, and localization information, for distinguishing rare MGF-like transients from merger-driven GRBs.

papers.title: The inverse local-relative correspondence and the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation
papers.abstract: We prove the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation for the local Gromov--Witten theory of smooth weak del Pezzo surfaces, by identifying its unique formal solution with the inverse of the local-relative correspondence. We construct this inverse through an associative set-partition convolution and establish the identification using Zagier's recursion for the Bloch--Okounkov $n$-point function. The proof applies in all genera and includes non-toric surfaces.

papers.title: Two faces of symmetry match in gear-like coupled rotary motors
papers.abstract: Rotary molecular motors commonly couple components with different rotational symmetries, but how this gearing controls energy transduction remains unclear. Here we show that symmetry can produce a fundamental tradeoff in coupled stochastic barrierless rotary motors: the gear ratio that maximizes output power under tight coupling is also the ratio that requires the strongest coupling to remain locked. Consequently, weakening the coupling can invert the effect of gearing, transforming a power maximum into a local minimum. At strong driving, both the power-optimal and most slip-susceptible ratios approach symmetry match. Numerical solutions of the Fokker-Planck dynamics for rotors with finite energy barriers reproduce these predictions and reveal how the behavior changes when driving strength is fixed per rotation or per subunit. Motivated by the bacterial flagellar motor, these results identify coupling strength as a key determinant of whether matched rotational symmetries enhance or suppress energy transduction, providing a general design principle for coupled molecular motors.

papers.title: Communication and Privacy Trade-Offs in Distributed Storage With Shared Secret Keys
papers.abstract: We study distributed storage over public communication channels where privacy is realized using shared secret keys. Specifically, a user wishes to store a file across $L$ servers such that any subset of at least $t$ servers can reconstruct the file, while any subset of at most $z$ colluding servers learns no more than a fraction $α$ of the file. Unlike classical secret-sharing models that assume secure communication channels between the user and each server, we consider a setting where all transmissions occur over a public channel and the user shares an individual secret key of length $n$ bits with each server. For a fixed key length $n$, we characterize the trade-off between the privacy leakage parameter $α$ and the maximum file size that can be securely stored. Additionally, we determine the minimum local randomness, public communication, and storage required to achieve this optimal trade-off.

papers.title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC outperforms all baselines, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product.

papers.title: virasoro_blocks: Software for the 2d bootstrap
papers.abstract: We introduce virasoro_blocks, software that computes Virasoro conformal blocks at any central charge in a form suitable for the numerical bootstrap. At each finite order in the elliptic nome, Zamolodchikov's recursion gives the block as a positive prefactor times a rational function of the exchanged weight. However, its many Kac poles make it difficult to use in semidefinite programming approaches to the bootstrap. In this software we use optimal interpolation to reduce the number of poles while keeping high accuracy. The software works in arbitrary precision and handles singular central charges, including the minimal models and $c=1$. It also computes global blocks, $N=1$ superconformal blocks, torus characters, and torus one-point blocks. We illustrate it with two applications. Assuming only scalar Virasoro primaries, we compute bounds on the scalar gap that approach the window of Liouville solutions between $(c-1)/16$ and $(c-1)/12$. We also bound the average exchanged dimension in four-point functions of identical scalars at several central charges. These bounds have a rich structure, and many known 2d CFTs lie on or near their boundary.

papers.title: Logarithmic transformations on the six-sphere
papers.abstract: We show that there are infinitely many choices of the multiplicities in the logarithmic transformation step of the Alpöge--Claude construction which produce a complex threefold diffeomorphic to the six-sphere. Moreover, distinct choices of the multiplicities yield biholomorphically inequivalent complex structures.

papers.title: Measuring Longer-Horizon Leveraged ETF Performance
papers.abstract: Many investors hold leveraged exchange-traded funds (LETFs) for more than one day. Because these products reset leverage daily, their longer-horizon returns need not equal the stated leverage multiple times the underlying return. We explain this gap using a return identity that separates what we call the convexity bonus, volatility drag, and product costs. We also discuss several common ways to measure LETF performance and highlight how these measures can produce misleading assessments of how real-world LETFs perform. We propose evaluating ex-post performance using realized terminal wealth, which measures how much invested wealth grew. For ex-ante analysis, we propose using expected log returns to quantify how fast capital compounds over time. We show that estimating expected cumulative return by compounding the historical arithmetic mean can rank investments backwards, report gains for funds that lose money, suggest that infinite leverage is optimal when expected returns exceed borrowing cost, and reward temporary price fluctuations that reduce LETF wealth. We argue that even if the distribution of daily returns is known by the econometrician, expected terminal wealth is sensitive to whether the model draws days independently or draws monthly or annual blocks of daily returns and can be driven by a small number of economically infeasible payouts.

papers.title: Complete quasinormal modes of Type-D black holes. II. Extremal Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: We develop a double-confluent Heun method that extends our previous study of complete quasinormal-mode (QNM) spectra of Type-D black holes to extremal Kerr black holes. Radial boundary conditions and angular regularity determine the gravitational frequencies at extremality. Compared with earlier spectra restricted to the conventional Riemann sheet, analytic continuation across frequency branch cuts reveals additional QNMs on unconventional Riemann sheets. Spin continuation follows our Schwarzschild mode families toward extremality, with the survey extending through the 41st overtone on specified angular branches and Riemann sheets. We show for the first time that unconventional Class I modes with $m<0$, continued from unconventional Schwarzschild modes, form zero-damping sequences approaching the superradiant bound $Mω=m/2$ in the extremal limit. Within a fixed angular sector, finite-damping and zero-damping sequences are interspersed in the Schwarzschild overtone ordering, so a single overtone cutoff cannot separate them. Matching near the superradiant bound distinguishes nonextremal sequences accumulating at the critical frequency from isolated QNMs at exact extremality. Scattering-amplitude calculations verify representative roots and their sheet assignments. The expanded spectrum clarifies how Schwarzschild mode families reorganize at extremality, with completeness established by contour counting within a bounded frequency domain on a specified angular branch and Riemann sheet.

papers.title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
papers.abstract: The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. Its single instrument provides diffraction-limited visible imaging (~0.15 arcsec in the optical) together with simultaneous near-infrared (R ~ 100) slitless spectrophotometry, so that every detected source is observed in the NIR by the survey itself, with spectral information delivered at a resolution set by its brightness (full R ~ 100 typing at the bright end, synthetic medium-band or broadband photometry below it) and with no separate follow-up, a capability decisive for time-domain science. With it, KST addresses the three outstanding questions of dark physics in concert: the dynamics of dark energy, the nature of dark matter, and gravitational-wave dark sirens as independent cosmological rulers. KST combines measurements of expansion and structure growth to test dark-energy models. A two-tiered "Wedding Cake" strategy (2,000 deg^2 Wide plus 10 deg^2 cluster-targeted Deep Survey) combines weak lensing, baryon acoustic oscillations, and a near-infrared-standardized Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram to constrain dark energy at its pivot redshift (sigma(w_p) ~ 0.03); maps dark matter from cluster cores to galactic substructure to test cold dark matter against warm and self-interacting alternatives; and builds a deep near-infrared host catalog for a distance-ladder-independent H_0 from dark sirens. The same data yield a Legacy Science portfolio (galaxy evolution, active galactic nuclei, exoplanets, and the Milky Way) at no additional observing cost. As Korea's first dedicated astrophysics space mission, KST occupies a niche complementary to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Euclid, and Roman.

papers.title: Time-Switching Energy-Harvesting Quantum Relay-Assisted FSO Communication with Displaced Squeezed Signaling
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a quantum relay-assisted free-space optical (FSO) communication system in which a decode-and-forward relay is powered by time-switching optical energy harvesting and forwards the decoded information using displaced squeezed signaling (DSS). To obtain a physically con sistent description of turbulence-induced loss for non-classical signaling, each hop is modeled as a pure-loss bosonic chan nel whose random transmissivity follows a truncated Gamma Gamma law, i.e., the Gamma-Gamma irradiance conditioned on the physically admissible range of a transmittance. Under this channel, coherent states remain pure, whereas squeezed states are mapped to mixed Gaussian states. Under Helstrom-optimal detection, the average error of the coherent hop is derived in exact Laplace-series form. For the DSS hop, we derive the output states, a closed-form Gaussian fidelity with rigorous two sided bounds on the Helstrom error, and prove the existence of a loss-aware optimal photon partition. Furthermore, we prove that optimized squeezing preserves both the turbulence-induced diversity order and the leading asymptotic constant of coherent relaying, so that its benefit is a finite-photon-budget effect, and that an interior throughput-optimal harvesting fraction exists. A covariance-preserving benchmark with an exact series representation yields an analytical upper bound on the achievable throughput whose absolute gap vanishes as the relay photon budget grows. Numerical results based on the exact mixed-state Helstrom error quantify the benefit of squeezing and the regime in which it is useful.

papers.title: Simultaneous Real-Color Time-Domain Survey of the Coma Field with the Multi-channel Photometric Survey Telescope (Mephisto)
papers.abstract: We present the results from a high-cadence, multi-channel time-domain survey targeting the Coma galaxy cluster, utilizing the newly commissioned 1.6-m Multi-channel Photometric Survey Telescope (Mephisto). Mephisto's pioneering mosaic focal-plane design enables strictly simultaneous imaging in three distinct optical bands ($u/v, g/r, i/z$). This unique capability allows for the extraction of true, instantaneous spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of fast-evolving transients. Our survey continuously monitors a 20-square-degree footprint centered on the Coma cluster. By strategically targeting this massive local structure, we exploit cosmic anisotropy to significantly amplify the volumetric discovery rate of stellar explosions. During the initial six-month pilot operation, we successfully detected and tracked nine new supernovae (SNe). Remarkably, our high-cadence, multi-band strategy allowed us to capture ultra-early rising light curves and pre-discovery signals (e.g., SN 2026dyr) hours to days prior to formal discovery alerts. These instantaneous early-phase colors allow us to reconstruct intrinsic SEDs without temporal interpolation, providing reliable constraints on the physical parameters of early supernova (SN) evolution. Furthermore, our observed supernova yield shows good agreement with theoretical forecasts based on local stellar mass and star-formation rate overdensities. These pilot results validate the efficiency of the Mephisto Coma survey, demonstrating its objective capability to systematically explore the local transient population and provide rapid optical localizations for future multi-messenger events.

papers.title: Volumetric Nanophotonics for Enhanced Scintillation and Remote Light Outcoupling
papers.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. Under high-energy excitation, the patterns appear up to ~3.5$\times$ brighter and demonstrate emission enhancement trends consistent with well-established nanophotonic scaling laws. We also report a novel functionality we call "remote outcoupling," in which the nanophotonic patterns emit light that is generated in another region of the scintillator, without being directly excited themselves. Our monolithic nanofabrication approach extends nanophotonic scintillators into the bulk, which is an important step towards total control over scintillation using photonic design.

papers.title: Tactus: Tactile & Pose Sensing Glove for Natural Dexterity Data Collection
papers.abstract: Collecting naturalistic human manipulation demonstrations with accurate contact force and hand pose is essential for robot dexterous manipulation policy and foundational world model learning - yet no existing wearable platform provides both calibrated fingertip force sensing and occlusion-resilient hand tracking in a form factor that preserves natural manipulation behavior. We present Tactus, a textile-integrated sensing glove that co-optimizes three design pillars: (1) a thin, conformal 3D-knit form factor (1.5 mm fingertip stackup) designed to minimize interference with natural manipulation, (2) strategically placed capacitive tactile sensors at manipulation-relevant regions informed by empirical contact studies, and (3) IMU-fused pose tracking that maintains accuracy through the hand-object occlusions where manipulation data is most valuable. Tactus includes a documented calibration pipeline for cross-glove consistency and per-session calibration for subject-dependent correction. To enable objective comparison, we introduce standardized benchmarking protocols for tactile force regression and hand pose estimation, and apply them to Tactus and two commercially available tactile gloves - to our knowledge the first quantitative cross-platform evaluation of this kind. Tactus resolves a minimum detectable force of 0.59 N at 95% confidence, 1.6 - 2.7x lower than the commercial baselines, and with 0.87 cross-participant consistency, while our pose tracking sustains 11.0 mm fingertip keypoint relative error during manipulation, when occlusion is heaviest. We show that these combined signals support object property estimation, slip detection, and representative recording of hand-object interaction - yielding demonstration data with the fidelity required for contact-aware manipulation policies and world models.

papers.title: HERA: Assessing an Autonomous Agent for Quantum Device Measurement
papers.abstract: Large language model agents have begun to carry out laboratory measurements, but their scientific conclusions are useful only if they hold up under scrutiny. Demonstrating this requires controlled studies because models are stochastic and the context a model is given steers its conclusions. Here we introduce HERA, an autonomous agent designed to carry out cryogenic transport measurements of quantum devices. HERA draws on a knowledge base curated by lab members that holds measurement protocols, software tools, and literature references. We assessed HERA with a blinded trial against an expert on the stacking order of two multilayer graphene devices, an ablation of its knowledge base, and hundreds of offline replays in which models designed the trial's central measurement without running it. HERA's conclusions matched the expert's sealed conclusions on both tested devices. The ablation and the replay studies measured the impact of the knowledge base across different models, showing that with it every model designed better measurements and reasoned more soundly. To test how readily HERA extends to a new problem, we tasked it with finding and characterizing superconductivity in a different material system. This required a few hours of expert time to develop a new experimental protocol, after which HERA did both autonomously. These results show that, with a knowledge base designed for the task, language model agents are capable of sound experimental science.

papers.title: Fate of Quantum Magic
papers.abstract: Magic, a quantum resource distinct from entanglement, measures departure from states stabilized by products of Pauli operators. Such stabilizer states can be maximally entangled yet admit efficient classical description: quantum advantage requires magic. We develop a powerful framework to evaluate the degree of magic in generic many-body states. We use it to study the fate of magic under thermal and dynamical evolution. In the transverse field Ising model, we find a thermal sudden death of magic that saturates with system size, and occurs after the death of entanglement. We reach similar conclusions in generic spin chains, and in the Kitaev quantum spin liquid on the honeycomb lattice, where the threshold shows an intricate dependence on subregion shape. We then study how magic equilibrates after a quantum quench. In quenches of generic spin chains, the magic of a subregion typically dies before entanglement, contrary to thermal trajectories. An explanation is given in terms of the geometry of non-magical states. As a third type of trajectory, we examine the fate of magic with separation with an appropriate notion of non-local magic and establish a sudden death. Finally, we show how to experimentally witness a volume law of frame-robust magic in quantum materials by using neutron scattering.

papers.title: Are Black Hole and Cosmological Horizon Thermodynamics Necessarily Inequivalent?
papers.abstract: It has recently been argued that cosmological horizon thermodynamics and black hole thermodynamics are generically inequivalent in any consistent, UV complete theory of quantum gravity, where it was suggested that this could be falsified by the identification of a counterexample. This conjecture was motivated in part by noting that cosmological horizons do not incorporate many of the convenient features found in the black holes described by string theory. In this work, we consider as a toy model a universe with a single non-rotating black hole and a positive cosmological constant. We work in the Nariai limit where the mass of the black hole is taken to its maximum possible value, and where we also assert that the quantum field theory living on this background is strictly parity invariant. In the semi-classical regime where we neglect instability of the exact Nariai equilibrium under quantum fluctuations, we find that the observer cannot readily distinguish the physics in the neighborhood of the black hole horizon from the physics in the neighborhood of the cosmological horizon. This does not prove that the two are generically equivalent in any universe, though it does suggest that they cannot be entirely unrelated in general. We propose that any consistent theory of quantum gravity that aims to describe black holes in a universe with a positive cosmological constant should provide a related microscopic origin for the leading semiclassical cosmological entropy and black hole entropy in the neighborhood of the particular limit considered here.

papers.title: Modular Bayesian Foundation Models: Bayesian time series encoders for OOD detection, routing and forecasting
papers.abstract: Industrial systems continuously generate time series that vary in sampling frequency, scale, dynamics, and operating regime. Consequently a single time-series foundation model may not be able to represent all regimes effectively and retraining a large model for every new dataset or regime shift is computationally expensive. Modular foundation models address this issue by reusing specialised encoders trained on diverse datasets and by allowing the expansion of capabilities through the addition of new experts. This approach requires compact experts to minimize storage cost and a proper selection mechanism of experts for unseen data. We propose a modular foundation model framework that combines end-to-end Bayesian encoder training with uncertainty based routing. Using Singular Bayesian Neural Networks (SBNNs), we build a collection of compact Bayesian encoders whose epistemic uncertainty guides label-free selection. At the selected ranks, our Bayesian collection uses 63.8\% less storage than its deterministic counterpart. We evaluate this framework on time-series data through distribution shift, encoder selection, and probabilistic forecasting. Across seven incoming datasets, uncertainty-based routing is competitive with distance-based routing in terms of forecast MSE, while reducing average ECE from 0.086 to 0.072 and average NLL from 0.907 to 0.836. It also increases PICP90 from 82.28\% to 89.03\%. In a separate model-family comparison, we evaluate the SBNN pipeline against full-rank Bayes by Backprop, deep ensembles, and MC Dropout. The SBNN pipeline achieves an average MSE of 0.390, comparable with 0.396 for deep ensembles, 0.389 for MC dropout, and 0.443 for the full-rank Bayesian model. It uses 63.9\% fewer parameters than MC dropout, 81.9\% fewer than the full-rank model, and 92.8\% fewer than the deep ensemble.

papers.title: Generative Rate-Distortion-Perception Theory on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: Generative communication uses transmitted information to control stochastic generation at the receiver. A fundamental question is how much source-specific information must be communicated so that outputs generated at the receiver satisfy prescribed fidelity and reliability requirements while preserving the conditional source distribution. We address this question for sources on compact Riemannian manifolds by developing a generative rate-distortion-perception (GRDP) framework without common randomness. We formulate an asymptotic operational GRDP function under a geodesic distortion radius and a failure-probability constraint, and establish its single-letter characterization through an equivalent informational formulation. Furthermore, for the informational formulation with the high-reliability limit, we derive a geometric lower bound determined by the largest source probability mass of a region with bounded geodesic diameter, together with an upper bound based on probabilistic coverings of the source manifold. Small-radius analysis of the lower bound reveals the roles of intrinsic dimension and scalar curvature in the required communication rate. For uniformly distributed sources on compact homogeneous Riemannian manifolds, we prove that the bounds coincide, yielding an exact characterization of the limiting GRDP function. We further specialize this result to unit spheres, obtaining an explicit expression that relates the minimum communication rate to the geodesic distortion radius and intrinsic dimension, revealing that for the $d$-dimensional unit sphere with $d\ge2$, increasing the communication rate by $d$ bits per source symbol can reduce the distortion radius by more than half.

papers.title: Spectral theory of large data with power-law latent features
papers.abstract: Power-law eigenvalue spectra of covariance matrices estimated from data appear in diverse domains ranging from neural populations to proteins. We introduce a generative latent feature model for such data, optionally corrupted by measurement noise, and develop its spectral theory. We derive closed leading-order self-consistent equations for the Stieltjes transform of the covariance matrix from which the bulk eigenvalue density is obtained and provide a variational principle for the self-consistent equations. We also compute the positions and fluctuations of isolated top eigenvalues. The theory is validated in known algebraic limits and tested against simulations.

papers.title: Capital growth since the 19th century
papers.abstract: We argued in an earlier paper (Getty and Tkachenko 2025b), from data reported for net saving and market-value capital by 94 nations over the period 1980-2021, that net saving has had little or no effect on capital growth at the global scale. Here we extend the study backward to the earliest year, in each country, for which those data have been reported or reconstructed. We find a still smaller margin of possibility (1.6% versus 6.4%) of contribution of net saving to capital growth at the collective scale. We also propose and defend an alternative explanation of capital growth, and suggest a larger role for the cash flow concept in economic analysis.

papers.title: Magnetism in a homometallic square-planar Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$$_4$Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$ metallacrown
papers.abstract: The well-established homometallic metallacrown Cu(II)[12-MC$_\text{Cu(II)N(Shi)}$-4]$^{2-}$, comprising four square-planarly arranged Cu(II) ions surrounding a slightly off-plane central Cu(II) ion, provides an excellent platform for investigating magnetism in exchange-coupled Cu(II) clusters both by experimental and ab initio numerical methods. In the present work, sterically bulky substituents are introduced into the salicylhydroxamate ligand to obtain a modified derivative, Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$[12-MC$_\text{Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$N(L)}$-4]$^{2-}$ (Cu$_4$Cu), thereby effectively suppressing intermolecular magnetic interactions and enabling a detailed investigation of its intrinsic ground-state spin structure and exchange interactions. Static magnetization reveals competing antiferromagnetic exchange interactions of $J_1=-8.1(2)$ THz ($-33.5(8)$ meV) between the central and the peripheral sites and $J_2=-4.40(12)$ THz ($-18.2(5)$ meV) between neighboring sites on the ring of the metallacrown, which are corroborated by ab initio broken symmetry-based density functional theory (DFT). These couplings yield an $S=1/2$ ground state for Cu$_4$Cu at low temperatures, for which X-band and high-frequency/high-field electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) precisely determine the $g$-factors $g_x = 2.028$, $g_y = 2.056$, and $g_z = 2.222$ close to axial anisotropy and in agreement with our DFT results. The ground-state spin-configuration is characterized by $d_{xy}$-character of the unoccupied states. Furthermore, our magnetization data evidence thermal transitions across a doublet-to-quartet gap of $Δ_{1/2\rightarrow3/2} = 4.8(4)$ THz which is also indicated by the emergence of an excited-state EPR signal.

papers.title: Running cosmological constant in light of recent CMB-BAO data
papers.abstract: We revisit single-field slow-roll inflation driven by a running cosmological constant, i.e. a cosmological constant receiving a logarithmic radiative correction, in light of the latest CMB-BAO data. The relative radiative correction $δ$ is treated as a free parameter of the model and allowed to be positive or negative. For positive $δ$, the predictions interpolate between a logarithmic regime and a linear inflation one. Compatibility with CMB-only data is confined to a narrow stripe near the $2σ$ border where $δ$ is relatively large. On the other hand, the predictions fit easily within the constraints including BAO data in a wide range of parameters. For negative $δ$, the slow-roll approximation breaks down at small field values and the predictions are excluded by data. However, once the effective mass contribution inside the logarithmic correction is taken into account, the negative $δ$ potential develops a local maximum and behaves like a hilltop model, achieving compatibility with CMB-only data, while agreement with CMB-BAO data is possible only at $2σ$.

papers.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and prove that every vector bundle of rank at least three admits smooth connected simply branched spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Clustered Federated Learning in Non-IID Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Current and emerging mobile networks face increasing privacy, scalability, and performance challenges as distributed learning becomes essential for advanced 6G services. These challenges are amplified by the presence of non-IID data, naturally arising in heterogeneous wireless environments, that degrade the performance of standard Federated Learning (FL) approaches. To address non-IID data across clients, we propose a Clustered Federated Learning (CFL) framework that assigns clients to specialized models during training. Data-domain clustering initializes model-based clustering, enabling identification and exploitation of client similarities without sharing raw data while reducing communication cost. Motivated by mmWave beam selection, we evaluate our methods on a wireless simulation dataset (DeepMIMO) and complement it with two non-IID benchmarks (FEMNIST, Rotated CIFAR-10) to isolate different non-IID characteristics. Our best configurations improve accuracy over IFCA by 4.8 pp on DeepMIMO and 10.6 pp on FEMNIST while reducing downlink data volume by 83.1 % on FEMNIST compared to IFCA. We demonstrate that different clustering strategies suit different non-IID characteristics. These results show that our CFL methods enable resource-efficient, and high-performance distributed learning in future 6G networks.

papers.title: Coexistence of superconductivity and magnetic order in BaFe$_2$S$_3$: evidence for orbital-selective delocalization
papers.abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges from correlated electronic states is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. The quasi-one-dimensional spin-ladder compound \bfs\ serves as a unique platform to study this interplay, as it lacks the two-dimensional square lattice characteristic of most iron-based superconductors. Here, we combine high-pressure x-ray and neutron diffraction, x-ray emission spectroscopy, and electrical transport to map its structural, magnetic, and electronic evolution into the superconducting regime. We \revised{observe} a striking pressure-induced decoupling: while the long-range stripe-type antiferromagnetic order remains remarkably robust under pressure up to the onset of superconductivity, the local iron magnetic moment is suppressed by nearly 80\%. This dichotomy \revised{points to an orbital-selective mechanism}, where specific Fe $3d$ electrons remain localized to sustain magnetism while others delocalize to form the itinerant and superconducting state. \revised{Superconductivity emerges while long-range magnetic order is still present, revealing that the two coexist in \bfs, which we attribute to} the selective response of multiorbital electronic degrees of freedom.

papers.title: A First-Order Phase Transition in Spin-Imbalanced BCS Theory of Superconductivity
papers.abstract: We study a translation-invariant BCS functional of superconductivity for a system of spin-$1/2$ fermions with spin-dependent chemical potentials, $μ_+\neqμ_-$. Numerical work of Caldas and Mota and analytical work of Freiji, Hainzl, and Seiringer has suggested an unusual first-order phase transition in spin-imbalanced BCS models, in which the normal state becomes globally unstable while remaining locally stable. Here, we prove that a first-order phase transition occurs in such spin-imbalanced BCS functionals. For each sufficiently small fixed spin imbalance and sufficiently low temperature, there is a coexistence coupling $λ_{\mathrm{fo}}$ strictly below the linear-stability threshold $λ_{\mathrm{lin}}$ of the normal state at which the Cooper pair density exhibits a nonzero jump and the minimized energy has a kink. The methodological insight is a coercivity estimate obtained by decomposing the BCS energy minimization into two parts, where the ``inner'' problem minimizes over the one-particle density matrices at fixed pairing and can be exactly solved by a Legendre--Fenchel transform.

papers.title: Separating the Density Wave Phase from Zero-Resistance Superconductivity in La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10}$
papers.abstract: Identifying the key ingredients for superconductivity under pressure in the Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates remains a formidable challenge, due to a complex interplay between structural variations, oxygen content and location, electronically ordered phases, and the need for high pressures to reach the superconducting phase. To disentangle these complex inter-dependencies, here we study a series of clean single crystals of trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10}$. We discover that enhanced biaxial, compressive pressures induce a zero-resistance state at a 60\% lower pressure compared to previous reports. At the same time, we completely separate the low-pressure density wave phase from superconductivity, effectively ruling out that soft, quantum critical fluctuations of the density wave order parameter act as the pairing glue in this system. Our results establish biaxial, in-plane pressures as a powerful tool for promoting superconductivity in nickelates, unifying the required pressure scales for superconductivity in different Ruddlesden-Popper structures, and providing a connection to the recently discovered thin film samples.

papers.title: Probing Scalar Polarization with Next-Generation Gravitational-Wave Detectors: The Roles of Detector Geometry and Source Inclination
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of compact binaries offer a direct way to test whether gravity admits polarizations beyond the two tensor modes of general relativity. We perform a forecast to assess how well future multi-messenger events will constrain the presence of scalar polarizations in gravitational waves. Performing binary neutron star injections, we forecast next-generation constraints on three modified gravity parameters in the PPE formalism: $α$ (tensor amplitude), $α_B$ (scalar amplitude) and $β$ (tensor and scalar phase). Cosmic Explorer (CE) and Einstein Telescope (ET) each tighten every parameter by 1--2 orders of magnitude over an O5 LIGO-Virgo network, with ET's triangular geometry giving a persistent $\approx2\times$ improvement over 2$\times$CE on the scalar-mode amplitude $α_B$ in both a GW170817-like and a second, representative BNS. We show that, if the sky position and luminosity distance are known from EM observations, adding an EM-based prior on the orbital inclination $ι$ narrows the $α_B$ constraint by $\approx56\times$ relative to an isotropic inclination prior, for a GW170817-like event. We also assess how EM inclination priors as well as assumptions on the neutron star equation of state may affect the inference on the scalar amplitude $α_B$. Overall, these results indicate that detector geometry and the availability of well-placed EM external information are both important levers --- alongside raw network sensitivity --- for next decade scalar-polarization tests.

papers.title: Open-Source Framework for the Visualization, Quantification, and Analysis of 4D Flow and High-Dimensional Magnetic Resonance Images
papers.abstract: Background: Four-dimensional (4D) flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) captures 3D anatomy and blood velocity across the cardiac cycle, but current post-processing software is closed, varies across platforms, and sits outside open-source image-computing frameworks. We developed an open-source framework for the import, visualization, and quantification of 4D flow and other high-dimensional CMR within SlicerHeart, an extension for 3D Slicer. Methods: Import 4D Flow reads vendor DICOM, applies preprocessing, and stores velocities as a time-resolved vector field; Analyze 4D Flow provides measurement planes, streamline and Doppler-like visualization, segmentation propagation, and quantification. Underlying both, we extended the Insight Toolkit to store five- and higher-dimensional arrays. Flow quantification was compared with a commercial package (cvi42) and 2D phase contrast in 13 patients with congenital heart disease across 108 paired regions of interest (Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients, ICCs). Consensus-recommended processing methods were also implemented as an open-source library with an automated test suite of analytic and CFD phantoms and clinical acquisitions. Results: The modules integrate with 3D Slicer's segmentation, registration, and rendering tools and export velocity fields and geometry for computational modeling. Agreement with cvi42 was close: forward volume bias -0.1 mL (95% limits of agreement 2.2 to -2.3; ICC 0.997), effective volume per minute bias -0.015 L/min (0.21 to -0.24; ICC 0.994). Against 2D phase contrast, forward volume bias (-2.2 mL) and mean absolute percentage error (21.8%) matched cvi42 (-2.1 mL; 21.3%). Conclusions: This open, extensible framework brings 4D flow CMR into an established image-computing ecosystem and agrees closely with a commercial reference; every step can be inspected, reproduced, and improved.

papers.title: MAS-Loop: Beyond One-Shot Orchestration towards Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Training-time multi-agent system (MAS) design seeks to learn reusable orchestration policies, yet prevailing approaches remain largely one-shot: an Orchestrator generates a system but only observes and learns from its terminal outcome. This paradigm discards execution trajectories that expose system-level failures and contain fine-grained information beyond the terminal outcome, leaving no direct basis for revising the source MAS, evaluating the updated MAS, or learning from the resulting contrast. To this end, we introduce MAS-Loop, an execution-grounded framework that closes this feedback loop by coupling an Orchestrator with a trajectory-conditioned Refiner. For each task, the Orchestrator constructs and executes a source MAS to obtain an outcome score and an intermediate trajectory. Conditioned on the trajectory, the Refiner localizes an actionable failure, formulates a trajectory-grounded diagnosis, and proposes a bounded patch to the agents, information flow, or execution configuration. The executable updated MAS is re-executed on the same task to measure its realized outcome under stochastic execution. This pair-MAS comparison provides complementary learning signals: the Orchestrator learns to generate strong systems with fewer recoverable failures, whereas the Refiner learns to expose and repair observed weaknesses, thereby driving policy-level co-evolution across training iterations. Experiments show that MAS-Loop achieves the strongest overall performance among the evaluated baselines, with consistent gains from refinement across all evaluated benchmarks. The co-evolution process also yields MAS-JudgeCorpus, a dataset of execution-grounded source-updated pairs with orchestration- and trajectory-level supervision, which can provide the community with support for MAS reward modeling and trajectory-aware investigation.

papers.title: Collective sliding relaxor ferroelectricity across thousand-layer van der Waals superstructures
papers.abstract: Relaxor ferroelectrics are among the most important electromechanical materials owing to their exceptionally large electrostrictive responses. However, conventional relaxor behavior is generally associated with chemical complexity and structural disorder, where local compositional fluctuations generate polar nanoregions, making the microscopic origin of this behavior difficult to control and engineer. Here we report sliding relaxor ferroelectricity (S-RFE), a previously unknown relaxor state in which engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity enables cooperative interlayer sliding to generate collective relaxor behavior. Through stacking-phase engineering in rhombohedral boron nitride, we create sliding domains that act as structural analogues of polar nanoregions and cooperatively align under an electric field through interlayer sliding. This collective state produces reversible electromechanical deformation of up to approximately $-1.6\%$ with negligible hysteresis in approximately 300-nm-thick crystals, corresponding to approximately 1000 atomic layers. The resulting electrostriction coefficient ($Q_{33}$ of approximately $1200\,\mathrm{m}^{4}\mathrm{C}^{-2}$) exceeds those of most crystalline electrostrictors by orders of magnitude. Unlike conventional relaxors, whose electromechanical response is often suppressed by dipolar freezing at low temperatures, S-RFE remains active down to 1.6 K and maintains giant electromechanical functionality. Our results establish sliding relaxor ferroelectricity as a new route to relaxor behavior and reveal how atomic-scale interlayer motion can be amplified into collective mesoscale functionality across approximately one thousand layers, providing a materials-by-design platform for electromechanical, photonic, and quantum technologies based on van der Waals materials.

papers.title: Thermodynamic cost of locally maintaining a steady state
papers.abstract: The Gibbs states of local Hamiltonians have short-range conditional correlations. To maintain a steady state with long-range conditional correlations, one might expect that a stochastic process must ``pay'' either in nonlocal moves or entropy production. Surprisingly, we find strictly local Gaussian processes that obey detailed balance and have unique steady states with arbitrarily long-range conditional correlations. We show that such processes must still produce entropy, if implemented using a local quadratic Hamiltonian coupled locally to equilibrium, rapidly relaxing baths. We lower-bound this entropy production in terms of the steady state's conditional mutual information (CMI); if the CMI decays exponentially with distance, the associated length-scale is called the Markov length $ξ$. The entropy production per site per relaxation time obeys $\hatσ\ge c ξ^2$ for large $ξ$, and with $c$ an implementation-dependent constant. We also bound the tradeoff between coupling range and entropy production. We contrast these Gaussian processes with jump processes on discrete state spaces, for which, under certain irreducibility assumptions, steady states with long-range CMI are only possible if detailed balance is violated. We conjecture (and present evidence) that rapidly mixing local jump processes cannot stabilize steady states with long-range CMI.

papers.title: Adaptive Local Measurements For Quantum Learning Can Exponentially Outperform Nonadaptive Global Measurements
papers.abstract: Can measurements chosen adaptively, in response to earlier outcomes, be exponentially more informative than measurements fixed in advance? In many quantum settings, adaptivity helps at most polynomially; known exponential advantages require coherent measurements across copies or restricted measurements. We show an exponential advantage measuring one copy at a time, with no quantum memory kept between state copies, even when the nonadaptive learner may perform arbitrary global measurements on each copy. We construct explicit families of multi-qubit states in which a scalar parameter is encoded in one of exponentially many candidate observables, with an auxiliary marker indicating which one. An adaptive protocol identifies the relevant observable and then measures it using only single-qubit measurements and one round of adaptation. At fixed accuracy, it needs logarithmically many copies as the qubit count grows, whereas every nonadaptive protocol needs exponentially many. The same mechanism yields an exponential gap in local asymptotic minimax mean squared error constants, tight up to the exponential base. The states are separable and classical in label-dependent product bases; no entanglement or other nonclassical correlations are required. The gap comes from measurement incompatibility: the candidate observables cannot be measured jointly, so a fixed measurement must divide its information budget among them, while adaptivity selects the informative one. Accordingly, the separation disappears when the candidate observables commute, and cannot occur with fully observed classical samples. Measurement incompatibility thus emerges as a resource for quantum learning, distinct from entanglement and quantum memory, that classical feedback alone can exploit.

papers.title: Maxwell's equations are universal for sparse linear algebra
papers.abstract: Optical and wave-based analog computing has re-emerged as a route to accelerating linear algebra, with metamaterials and photonic circuits shown to invert matrices and solve integral equations. However, it has remained unclear which problems such passive structures can represent, and at what cost, once encoding, precision, conditioning and readout are accounted for. Here, we show that every polynomially conditioned sparse linear system can be compiled into a three-dimensional dielectric -- a cavity filled with lossless, isotropic material of bounded permittivity -- whose time-harmonic response encodes its solution. For $m$ nonzero coefficients, the volume of the structure and the cost of writing it down and reading out the answer scale as $\tilde O(m^{3/2})$, coefficients require only $O(\log m)$ bits, and every field that approximately satisfies Maxwell's equations decodes to an approximate solution. We prove the construction for the continuum equations and give a computer-assisted version for the Yee discretization underlying finite-difference solvers. Read in reverse, it implies that electromagnetic simulation is, up to this overhead, as hard as general sparse linear algebra: a sufficiently fast general-purpose Maxwell solver would yield a faster sparse linear solver.

papers.title: Generalized Symmetries of QED$_4$ on Non-Spin Manifolds
papers.abstract: Generalized symmetries are sensitive to the tangential structure of spacetime. We study this interplay for massless QED on oriented non-spin four-manifolds, where the photon becomes a spin$^c$ connection and the path integral sums over spin$^c$ structures. The shifted flux quantization extends the magnetic 1-form symmetry into a $w_2$-twisted 1-form symmetry: its $2π$ rotation acts as a gravitational sign, fixed by the normal bundle of the surface the operator wraps. The obstruction to treating it as an ordinary magnetic 1-form symmetry is an order-two mixed magnetic-gravitational anomaly, which is classified by reduced oriented bordism and detected on the Wu manifold. In a fixed spin$^c$ sector, this anomaly is removable by a counterterm, so it is a property of the sum over spin$^c$ structures. We discuss its consequences for gapped, Coulomb, and Higgs phases. The chiral anomaly is governed by the index of the spin$^c$ Dirac operator, so rational chiral defects carry gravitational as well as electromagnetic responses. A spin$^c$ Hall topological field theory cancels the electromagnetic part but leaves a framing anomaly. At the level of anomaly inflow, this is canceled for every rational angle by stacking a neutral, generally noninvertible Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev layer. The same framing subtlety affects the chiral defects of QED on curved spin manifolds. The complex projective plane illustrates each of these features explicitly.

papers.title: The Hidden Value of Soft Infrastructure for Urban Flood Adaptation
papers.abstract: As sea level rises and flooding events become more frequent, cities are tapping into a range of engineering and planning solutions to reduce flood losses. Beyond traditional ``hard'' infrastructure (e.g., sewage, seawalls), ``soft'' infrastructure that supports and empowers the role of citizens in preparedness has been hailed as a promising avenue for improving adaptation. Despite its promise, there have been very limited attempts to quantify its effectiveness in reducing losses relative to hard infrastructure, particularly in urban environments. This study fills this knowledge gap using generative AI to quantify the effectiveness of a range of hard and soft infrastructure in urban areas. We demonstrate, for the first time, that soft infrastructure can significantly reduce flood losses, with an impact on par with hard infrastructure. Our results open the door to novel ways of confronting adaptation challenges in cities. Soft infrastructure is a viable alternative, especially when budgetary or time constraints make hard infrastructure unattainable. Policymakers should also couple soft and hard infrastructure to maximize resilience.

papers.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Forecast Treatment Effects in Economics?
papers.abstract: I use LLMs to forecast treatment effects of research studies pre-registered on the AEA RCT Registry and the Open Science Framework. I focus on studies whose results were first publicly released in 2026 and elicit forecasts from models whose training or knowledge cut-off dates were before the relevant set of papers was released. First, LLM models extract forecasting questions from the pre-registrations or pre-analysis plans. These questions elicit forecasted treatment effects; not all resolve in the subsequent papers, but those that do can be used to consider forecast accuracy. Forecasts were elicited for 889 treatment effects from 39 papers with results disclosed in January 2026 or later, or 673 from 33 papers after screening. Forecasts were elicited in raw units but I focus on those that could be standardized and therefore compared across papers. Currently, the median absolute forecast error is 0.054 SD for the best model, the average absolute error is 0.093 SD, and the MSE is 0.0218. The AI forecasts perform substantially better than benchmarks forecasting 0 effect or forecasting the mean effect of other papers' results in that time period. Overall, these results suggest considerable scope for forecasts to be of value in informing policy and research.

papers.title: Mpemba effect as an entropy-production race:Finite-amplitude bounds on crossing times in Markovian relaxation
papers.abstract: Two canonical preparations evolving under a common final Markov generator can exhibit the Mpemba effect because they excite different relaxation modes. We bound the first crossing of their relative entropies by treating relaxation as an entropy-production race. The exact balance $-\dot D=\dot e_p$ implies that a meeting occurs when the accumulated \emph{difference} of normalized entropy-production rates, $\int_0^t(r_H-r_C)\,\mathrm ds$ with $r_α=\dot e_p^α/D_α$, equals the initial logarithmic deficit $\ln[D_H(0)/D_C(0)]$. Global entropy-decay inequalities yield a lower crossing-time bound when the entropy-decay constant is bounded from below and the hot rate from above; we supply both certificates. A nonzero cubic moment of a slowest eigenfunction is sufficient for the modified logarithmic Sobolev constant to lie strictly below the spectral gap. Combining established relative-entropy comparison inequalities with Markov contraction and the actual mode amplitudes gives finite-amplitude crossing bounds without a small-deviation expansion. For an exactly strong, reversible three-state preparation these give $0.1659\le t_M\le0.1674$ in model time units, independently certified by outward-rounded interval arithmetic. This interval is narrower than $1\%$ and contains $t_M=0.1662209$. The conservative global-rate comparison used here gives only $t_M\ge0.042$. The hotter preparation starts $6.12$ times farther from equilibrium, yet it reaches $D=10^{-5}$ at $t=0.233$, compared with $t=0.844$ for the colder one. Mean energy crosses later than relative entropy. For a fixed driven generator, nonadiabatic entropy production governs the same balance. These results concern finite-state relaxation in a specified distance and do not predict water-freezing times.

papers.title: Effect of the surface on the energy levels in PbS and PbSe nanocrystals
papers.abstract: The structure of the electron and hole quantum confinement levels in spherical PbS and PbSe nanocrystals (NCs) is studied within the framework of a four-band effective-mass model. This level structure was initially calculated within the Kang--Wise model, which employs the standard boundary condition of vanishing carrier wave functions at the NC surface. This model, however, does not allow one to account for the effect of the NC surface on the level structure. Here, the effect of the NC surface is modeled using general boundary conditions (GBCs) imposed on the envelope wave functions at the surface. We show that the surface properties modify the size dependence of the electron and hole confinement levels and lead to an additional spin--orbit splitting of the $1P_{h,e}$ levels. Using the GBCs, we are able to quantitatively describe the size dependence of the lowest optical transitions in bare PbS and PbSe NCs and explain the differences between the absorption spectra of bare and Cl-passivated PbS NCs

papers.title: Improved LCL Equivalences and Curve Decoding Alphabet Sizes
papers.abstract: Local Coordinate-wise Linear (LCL) properties, introduced by Levi, Mosheiff, and Shagrithaya (2025), capture coding-theoretic properties such as list decoding and list recovery. They showed that every LCL property has the same rate threshold for random linear codes (RLC) and random Reed--Solomon codes (RRS). Brakensiek, Chen, Dhar, and Zhang (2025) extended this to random additive codes. Thus any property of all subspace design codes holds for RLCs and RRS at the same rate. In this work, we improve the probabilistic guarantees in the RRS local equivalence theorem and extend the equivalence to all known subspace design constructions individually. Each such construction, including folded Reed--Solomon codes, has the same LCL threshold as RLC and RRS codes. We apply these results to alphabet-size bounds for curve decoding. Curve decoding, introduced by Goyal and Guruswami (2025) and Carmon et al. (2026), is a row-span-constrained LCL property implying proximity gaps (PG), correlated agreement (CA), and mutual correlated agreement (MCA), relevant to IOPs and SNARKs. Informally, a rate-$R$ code $C \subset \mathbb{F}^n$ is $(\ell,δ,a,b)$-curve decodable if any degree-$\ell$ curve $u:\mathbb{F}\to\mathbb{F}^n$ that is $δ$-close to $C$ on at least $a$ points has at least $b\leq a$ nearby codewords lying on a degree-$\ell$ curve in $C$. Goyal and Guruswami (2025) and Goyal, Guruswami, Sun, and Wootters (2026) established curve decodability for RLC and RRS codes at radius $δ$ approaching $1-R$, but with large alphabets in $\ell$ and $η:=1-R-δ$. Using our improved LCL equivalence and rank-sensitive counting inspired by Goyal and Guruswami (2026), we exponentially improve alphabet requirements while matching the best known values of $(a,b)$. For $\ell=O(1)$, our alphabet-size bounds match the best known for list decoding, and improves results for PG, CA, and MCA.

papers.title: SuperCrude EoS: A Simple, Analytical, and Reasonably Accurate Equation of State for Astrophysical Fluid Dynamics
papers.abstract: We present SuperCrude, a vastly simplified astrophysical equation of state that captures the most important physics needed for explosive astrophysics, but using compact, physically-motivated analytical approximations rather than precise interpolated data tables. We present a number of code tests demonstrating the performance of SuperCrude in a wide range of parameter space. In large regions of parameter space, SuperCrude is precisely accurate to within the accuracy level of helmeos. For some regions (especially where degeneracy, gas, and radiation are comparable) SuperCrude has errors in its effective adiabatic index on the order of a few percent. The solver's estimate of the temperature is less accurate, on the order of tens of percent. Because the solver is analytic, SuperCrude is designed in such a way to guarantee exact thermodynamic consistency. We incorporate SuperCrude into some hydrodynamic and astrophysical test problems, including the thermonuclear explosion of a white dwarf star. When coupled with a stiff nuclear network, SuperCrude does not achieve the same nucleosynthetic yields as helmeos, motivating future work to improve the temperature accuracy further.

papers.title: Local Quantum Fault Tolerance Without Expansion
papers.abstract: We study fault-tolerant quantum computation using a fixed, local error-correction rule and a geometrically simple code: the cubical $(d,d')$-Toric code with $d',d-d'\geq 2$, including the 4D Toric code. Under sufficiently weak local-stochastic Pauli noise, our construction uses noiseless, bounded-depth classical processing per physical time step. Its correction cycle acts only on the current syndrome, has constant depth, and is repeated unchanged during idle logical computation; it requires neither multiscale decoder states nor scale-dependent communication delays. Our proof treats errors and syndromes as chains in a cubical complex, combining geometric shrinking under the sweep rule with a space--time explanation-tree argument inspired by Toom's theorem. It does not rely on expansion. We establish three results: 1.Explicit higher-dimensional sweep rule. We give a local algorithm for choosing sweep corrections on cubical $(d,d')$-Toric complexes, resolving the local-existence question of Kubica and Preskill. 2. Fault-tolerant computation. We prove a circuit-level threshold theorem for noisy sweep cycles interleaved with logical gates. In particular, the 4D Toric code admits a fixed, constant-depth syndrome-based correction cycle without a multiscale decoder or expansion-based encoding. We do not claim constant total-depth overhead. 3. Ideal decoding under local-stochastic noise. For an initial local-stochastic Pauli error of rate $p$ below threshold, $n^{d+1}$ noiseless sweep cycles recover the encoded state on a side-length-$n$ $(d,d')$-Toric code with probability at least $1-O(\operatorname{poly}(n))p^{Ω(n)}$, extending earlier guarantees for independent errors.

papers.title: What to randomize matters: a controlled study of volume, axis and representation in low-data molecular generation
papers.abstract: Chemical language models can struggle to generate new molecules when trained on small datasets, where a model may reproduce training examples rather than learn a useful generative distribution. Randomized SMILES augmentation varies atom traversal, whereas Sequential Attachment-based Fragment Embedding (SAFE) also allows the order of fragment blocks to vary. How these distinct sources of representational variation affect low-data molecular generation has not been clearly studied. Here, using 1,000 seed molecules to train an autoregressive sequence model, we compare canonical SAFE with randomized SAFE at increasing corpus sizes, isolate atom-order and fragment-order axes of SAFE randomization, and compare fully randomized SAFE with randomized SMILES at molecule-by-molecule matched training corpora. Three findings emerge. First, randomization of SAFE alone raises the genuine yield of novel molecules more than 450-fold, turning a model that merely reproduces its training set into a practical molecular generator. Second, the two axes of randomization act jointly rather than additively: atom order alone reaches a tenth, and fragment order alone a seventh, of the genuine yield obtained when both vary, which is four times their combined contribution. Third, at matched corpus size and compute, randomized SAFE delivers 2.8 times the genuine yield of randomized SMILES. Welch tests with Games-Howell post-hoc comparisons resolve every difference on the primary outcomes. In the low-data regime, thus, what one randomizes rather than only how much determines whether augmentation produces new molecules or merely new spellings of the training set.

papers.title: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory
papers.abstract: We establish a direct connection between the entanglement bootstrap and the Doplicher--Haag--Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, we prove Haag duality and establish a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, we further construct an affine bijection from density matrices on the entanglement-bootstrap fusion space to normalized positive intertwiners in the corresponding operator-algebraic fusion channel. These results connect the entropic and operator-algebraic descriptions of anyons directly, without passing through exactly solvable lattice models.

papers.title: Generating Multipartite Entanglement via Structured-Bath Engineering
papers.abstract: We present how to dissipatively prepare genuinely multipartite-entangled steady states with mutually independent local reservoirs by harnessing an Abelian strong symmetry and temporal bath correlations. In interacting Ising chains, we demonstrate that, for a broad class of system-environment couplings, flat baths exponentially erase Ising-axis correlations. Structured baths overcome this obstruction by converting temporal bath correlations into classical spatial correlations. Strong symmetry then promotes these correlations to the quantum domain, enabling global multipartite entanglement. Within weak-coupling theory, we obtain exact steady states despite the generator's nonquadratic nature: strong symmetry reduces their construction to a classical problem for arbitrary Ising couplings. This reduction reveals an exact connection between classical distinguishability and entanglement. We then show how to engineer the bath spectrum to increase the correlation length and enable the preparation of GHZ-like states from separable initial conditions. We test the mechanism beyond the analytical regime using exact Markovian embeddings and tensor-network simulations. Our approach is particularly suited to superconducting and trapped-ion platforms, and we propose a concrete implementation for the latter using sympathetically cooled motional modes.

papers.title: Spectrum of the steady-state distribution function of disordered Lindbladian fermions at large channel number
papers.abstract: Free fermions coupled to particle gain and loss relax to a Gaussian steady state, in which every natural orbital has its own occupation. We find the distribution of these occupations $\varrho_{\rm st}$ for a random Hamiltonian coupled to many random gain and loss channels. Each orbital is filled and emptied at its own rates, and the Hamiltonian, moving particles across the levels during their lifetime, averages the differences between the orbitals. We show that this averaging is incomplete: the spread of the occupations decreases only as the inverse square root of the number of channels per level. At large system size the distribution depends on the grain Hamiltonian only through its density of states $ν(E)$. The spread is bounded by the baths alone: even Hamiltonians with unbounded, heavy-tailed spectra cannot widen it beyond this bound. The spread suppresses the particle-number fluctuations below their binomial value.

papers.title: Random Non-Commutative Error-Correcting Codes
papers.abstract: Chapman, Dinur, and Lubotzky recently introduced the theory of non-commutative error-correcting codes, generalizing classical coding theory to arbitrary groups via $δ$-robust subsets used to detect proper subgroups. Building on this foundation, this paper systematically studies an analogue of random codes for arbitrary groups, exploring the extent to which the classical Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound holds in this non-commutative setting. While random universal codes of linear size in free groups are shown to be asymptotically bad, we establish a complete characterization for general families of finite groups. Specifically, a family of finite groups admits good random codes (forming a GV family) if and only if it exhibits uniform polynomial maximal-subgroup growth. Furthermore, we provide explicit quantitative bounds on the rate and optimal distance range based on intrinsic parameters, proving that families of finite solvable groups always form GV families and determining the exact probabilistic rate for direct powers of a fixed finite simple group.
