papers.title: Market Efficiency in a Changing Asset Population: Mobility, Entry, and Survival over Cryptocurrency's Full History
papers.abstract: Weak-form efficiency implies symmetry restrictions on the Markov chain governing movement across the cryptocurrency capitalisation distribution. We test them on the full listed population: 8,970 assets, 690 weekly cross-sections, 2013 to 2026, with entry, exit and survival observed rather than inferred. Symmetry is rejected in every era, but the asymmetry falls by seventy percent, and what converged is entry-driven compositional churn rather than coins' own valuations. The bottom decile earns 27.5% per week on paper and nothing among assets that trade, on capacity of $293,000. Compensation for neglect exists precisely where trading does not.

papers.title: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable-Antenna Compensation of Channel Aging in Over-the-Air Split Learning
papers.abstract: Split learning (SL) trains a neural network across devices by exchanging intermediate activations and gradients. In over-the-air SL, the wireless channel serves as an inter-layer linear map, and when the forward and backward channels match, reciprocity and conjugation supply the backward product without channel estimation at the base station (BS). Passive user motion, which the learning link does not control, breaks this match. Movable antennas let the antenna move relative to the user device, and we use this freedom to compensate the displacement. For a stationary BS and a propagation environment quasi-static within each exchange, returning the antenna to its forward-transmission position restores the channel and yields a conditionally unbiased gradient estimate. We also derive when discrete positioning or mechanical movement can achieve this in time. A residual displacement below a quarter wavelength keeps the real part of the channel correlation positive for any angular spectrum. At zero effective offset, independent Gaussian jitter attenuates this correlation without reversing its sign, whereas a persistent offset can reverse it, and in arrays the tolerance depends on the receive-combining direction. These effects enter a nonconvex convergence bound, and a local analysis shows that partial mechanical compensation saves cycle time to first order at only a second-order loss in correlation. In CIFAR-10 experiments, a user terminal without channel state information stays at chance level under uncompensated walking motion, while discrete positioning stays within about 0.3 percentage points of exact restoration, including at a speed beyond the modeled actuator's limit.

papers.title: Hidden Staggered Superconducting Order in V2Se2O-Family Altermagnets
papers.abstract: $η$ pairing describes a staggered superconducting condensate whose order parameter changes sign between neighboring unit cells while maintaining a uniform magnitude. Nearly four decades after its theoretical proposal by C. N. Yang, a material platform for stabilizing $η$ pairing has remained elusive. Here, we reveal that altermagnetism, despite being pair breaking for conventional BCS pairing, naturally favors $η$-like pairing in V$_2$Se$_2$O-family altermagnets. Their valley-contrasting spin structure gives rise to oppositely spin-polarized, symmetry-related valleys centered at $X=(π,0)$ and $Y=(0,π)$, which form spin-singlet pairing partners separated by the commensurate momentum $\mathbf Q=(π,π)$, thereby favoring an $η$-like condensate. Self-consistent calculations demonstrate that the resulting $η$-like state remains robust over broad variations of chemical potential, hopping parameters, and Fermi-surface topology. To detect this hidden staggered order, we propose a phase-sensitive Josephson measurement with a uniform superconductor, where destructive interference suppresses single-Cooper-pair tunneling while preserving two-Cooper-pair processes. This constitutes a charge-$4e$-like Josephson response despite a bulk condensate composed of charge-$2e$ Cooper pairs, providing a direct phase-sensitive signature of the otherwise elusive $η$-like condensate in V$_2$Se$_2$O-family altermagnets.

papers.title: Fully Gapped Superconductivity in the Nonsymmorphic Centrosymmetric Superconductor In2Bi
papers.abstract: The nature of superconductivity in nonsymmorphic In2Bi remains an open question, with ongoing debate over whether it exhibits conventional (BCS-like) or unconventional superconductivity. Here we report the physical characteristics and superconducting properties of polycrystalline In2Bi. Measurements of electrical resistivity, magnetization, penetration depth, and specific heat demonstrate the superconducting transition temperature about 6 K, with a sharp transition in resistivity (Delta_Tc = 0.1 K) and RRR = 57.32, reflecting the high quality of the sample. The upper critical field Hc2(0) obtained from resistivity and magnetization measurements are in good agreement with each other and are smaller than the Pauli limit, suggesting orbital limited mechanism. The coherence length = 35.43 nm, penetration depth = 101.9 nm and electron-phonon coupling constant = 1.05 suggest strongly coupled type-II superconductivity. For T<Tc, Delta_lambda(T) is best described by an s-wave BCS model and does not have any power law dependency with T, which is expected for a nodeless superconducting order parameter. The superfluid density reveals a fully gapped superconductivity with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.02. In the superconducting state, the electronic specific heat is best described by an s-wave BCS model with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.05. All these results from the present study indicate that In2Bi is a typical type-II,BCS-like, strongly coupled, and fully gapped superconductor in the dirty limit.

papers.title: AcupunctureBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Generative Models in the Acupuncture Domain
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in the field of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), standardized benchmark evaluations for TCM have gradually emerged. Acupuncture is a crucial component of TCM. However, existing evaluation benchmarks are lacking in this domain. To address this gap, this paper proposes AcupunctureBench, the first independently constructed large-scale multimodal benchmark for the acupuncture domain, covering text, image, and video modalities. The AcupunctureBench spans multidimen sional knowledge in acupuncture, including acupuncture theory, meridians and acupoints, clinical reasoning, TCM syndromes, and practical acupoint operation. To achieve large-scale construction while ensuring medical professionalism, this work designs a human-machine collaborative data construction pipeline and proposes efficient deduplication strategies to reduce redundant samples, while extensively adopting data synthesis to mitigate data leak age risks. AcupunctureBench contains a total of 58,526 question samples and 1,216 video samples, covering multiple task types including objective questions, subjective question answering, case analysis, image understanding, image reasoning, and video understanding. Based on this benchmark, this paper evaluates 14 large language models, 14 large multimodal models, and 4 video foundation models, and further releases the first dedicated evaluation website for the acupuncture domain.

papers.title: AgentCount: An Agentic Workflow for Traceable Colony Counting and Insight Generation from Agar Plate Images
papers.abstract: Colony counting is commonly used to evaluate microbial populations in food safety testing and microbiological studies. Despite its wide application, manual counting is time-consuming and operator-dependent, and the final count often lacks a record of the objects included in the measurement. To address these limitations, this study presents AgentCount, an open-source agentic workflow for colony counting and result interpretation from agar plate images. Plate photographs and plating metadata are processed through seven agents for image quality control, plate localisation, colony detection, counting, CFU calculation, validation, and reporting. Colony detection is performed using Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) with multiple text prompts and morphology-based filtering. After that, replicate statistics are calculated and a large language model (LLM)-based agent is used to generate a results narrative. Intermediate outputs, including quality scores, segmentation masks, detections, and warnings, are retained to support review of the reported values. The workflow also extends to skill-guided analysis of archived microbial population data. In a retrospective comparison with two previously published studies, we benchmarked 241 published endpoints, including all 216 mean +- SD values of the meat-analogue pathogen tables; on the 168 endpoints with a complete n=6 replicate source, 164 (97.6%) agreed within 0.01 log10 units. Overall, AgentCount demonstrates the promising potential of agentic workflows for applications in applied microbiology.

papers.title: ProtoGTX: Prototype-Aligned Graph Transformer for Explainable Whole-Slide Image Analysis
papers.abstract: Deep learning has achieved strong performance in computational pathology, but explaining whole-slide image (WSI) predictions remains challenging. Existing explanation methods often highlight important regions without identifying their morphological patterns, leaving a gap between patch-level computational evidence and slide-level pathological interpretation. We propose ProtoGTX, a graph-based framework that combines spatial contextualization with a flexible morphological prototype vocabulary. ProtoGTX separates the reference prototypes used to define morphological concepts from the predictive model: the reference vocabulary can be generated from training data by unsupervised clustering or supplied externally, and remains fixed during classifier training. Patch features are first contextualized over a spatial graph, after which learnable prototypes representing morphological concepts are optimized through cross-attention. Their slide-level activation profile is aligned with the morphological composition induced by the fixed reference prototype bank. On the CPTAC and BRACS datasets, ProtoGTX outperforms the evaluated MIL, prototype-based, and graph-based baselines, with particularly pronounced improvements on BRACS. Qualitative analyses further show that spatial contextualization transforms fragmented patch-level prototype assignments into more coherent tissue regions. In BRACS, prototype maps also co-localize with pathologist annotations and regions relevant to slide-level prediction. These results demonstrate that ProtoGTX provides complementary semantic and spatial explanations while retaining a prototype vocabulary that can be defined independently of the predictive model. Code is available at https://github.com/mizuno-group/ProtoGTX.

papers.title: The Source of Data Value: Consumer Disclosure, Access Design, and Platform Monetization
papers.abstract: Digital marketplaces increasingly earn revenue from transaction commissions and seller-facing data services. Sellers may purchase data to increase revenue or avoid competing with an informed rival. We examine how consumer disclosure rights shape these motives and the platform's incentive to provide data. We develop a game-theoretic model of a commissioned platform, two differentiated sellers, and privacy-sensitive consumers. Data generates value through bilateral sales-revenue gains and competition threats arising from asymmetric access. Under mandatory collection, the platform can monetize defensive adoption, even when bilateral personalization reduces seller revenue. Under voluntary disclosure, anonymous purchasing and strictly positive privacy costs make unilateral disclosure unattractive in the baseline. Exclusive access thus yields no usable information, restores sellers' no-data rejection payoffs, and eliminates defensive fees. Profitable provision therefore requires nonnegative bilateral revenue gains. Under full fee extraction, sellers retain their no-data net profits. This revenue alignment does not guarantee welfare gains: additional transactions may benefit consumers, whereas segmentation in an already covered market can raise anonymous prices and reduce welfare. Capping anonymous offers at their no-data benchmark protects individual consumers and limits positive-mass provision to the transaction-creation region. Extensions consider access choice, heterogeneous privacy costs, imperfect identification, and limited contractual credibility. Platforms should evaluate data services based on both bilateral-use and seller-rejection outcomes, and sellers should distinguish revenue-enhancing from defensive investments. Regulators should distinguish equal-access rules from effective consumer control and monitor pricing in anonymous channels.

papers.title: Image Moment Estimation for Crowded Datasets
papers.abstract: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is an imaging technique capable of reconstructing high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) structure of biological macromolecules from a set of noisy projection images taken at random viewing directions. The mathematical model for cryo-EM images typically assumes that each image contains exactly one particle, which is centered at the origin. However, many experimental datasets contain particle images which include multiple particles: one central particle and a few crowding particles. This deviation from the model leads to inaccurate estimation of image statistics, such as the low-order image moments. To account for this, we propose a method to estimate image moments while correcting for the effect of crowding particles. This method can be run directly from a set of cryo-EM micrographs with picked particles, and we demonstrate its efficacy on a wide array of synthetic data.

papers.title: Bystander on the Fence: Sanctions in a Multipolar World
papers.abstract: We provide a theory of optimal trade sanctions with three strategic players: Home (sanctioner), Foreign (target), and Bystander. Bystander may act unilaterally or ally with either party subject to a participation constraint. We derive three novel results. First, members of a coalition generically set different tariffs either under Stackelberg timing or when transfers are imperfect. Second, as sanctions tighten, Home's welfare can improve even beyond the unilateral terms-of-trade optimum due to strategic interactions. Third, we characterize feasible sanctions targets when Home and Foreign compete for Bystander's support. An alternative implementation arises with competition: Home lets Foreign win, but Foreign's transfer to Bystander implements the sanctions target. We apply our model to sanctions against Russian crude. In a calibration exercise, cooperation among India, China, and Russia best matches observed data. Sanctions could have been roughly 70% more effective had China and India acted unilaterally or had the sanctioning coalition made them a better offer.

papers.title: MultiPASE: Shape-Aware Comparative 3D Genome Analysis
papers.abstract: 3D genome structures reconstructed from Hi-C data provide valuable insights into chromatin organization, but comparing them across conditions and time points remains challenging because of noise, variability, and arbitrary orientation. State-of-the-art comparison approaches often rely on contact-matrix-based summaries, which do not preserve the spatial geometry of the reconstructed structures and make integration with gene expression and chromatin accessibility difficult. There is therefore a need for robust structural alignment and spatial abstraction methods that support integrated analysis across conditions and time points. We present MultiPASE, a computational pipeline for comparative analysis of reconstructed 3D genome structures represented as gene-level spatial point clouds. MultiPASE aligns point clouds into a shared coordinate frame using coarse-to-fine rigid registration with PCA-based axis disambiguation and robust ICP refinement, then summarizes spatial organization using two complementary shape abstraction methods that produce stable, nested, multi-scale representations from dense core regions to broader structural extent. Using Hi-C-derived reconstructions from viral infection experiments, we show how the approach reveals condition-dependent structural changes that are difficult to interpret from raw 3D structures alone. By integrating spatial structure with gene expression and chromatin accessibility, MultiPASE supports interactive analysis of spatial organization and gene relocation patterns. A quantitative validation, reported in the Supplementary Materials, shows that the proposed shape abstractions preserve non-convex features, remain stable across samples, and that the alignment pipeline is necessary for meaningful comparison. A usage case and a usability evaluation with eight participants demonstrate the pipeline's effectiveness for comparative structural analysis.

papers.title: Asymptotic evaluation of multidimensional oscillatory integrals
papers.abstract: Oscillatory integrals appear throughout physics, from diffraction and gravitational lensing to real-time path integrals. Their asymptotic evaluation is complicated by the need to determine which real and complex saddle points contribute, and how they are connected by Stokes phenomena. In multiple dimensions, this traditionally requires computing the steepest descent manifolds in a high-dimensional complex space. Here, we develop an algebraic alternative for integrals with polynomial and rational exponents. Using integration by parts and Brieskorn reduction, we construct a finite-dimensional Gauss-Manin system that generates the asymptotic expansions of all saddle points. Its Borel transform yields a Fuchsian system, whose monodromy determines the Stokes constants and hence the adjacency of the saddles. Combined with the recent South-East rule, this identifies the contributing saddles and enables superasymptotic and hyperasymptotic approximations without computing gradient flows. We demonstrate the method for the parabolic umbilic diffraction integral and a Lorentzian lens as examples, obtaining agreement to machine precision. The methods are implemented in an accompanying open-source Julia package \href{https://github.com/jfeldbrugge/IntegralResurgence.jl}{\texttt{IntegralResurgence.jl}}.

papers.title: The typical red cell makes too little vacuole material for coalescence to build the large vacuoles of pocked cells
papers.abstract: Red blood cells carrying intracellular vacuoles, called pocked cells, are a sensitive marker of splenic function: about 0.5% of cells in healthy people, 20 to 70% after splenectomy. Vacuoles too small to see are common, and visible ones are thought to grow when small ones merge. We tested that idea with a particle model that resolves the cell's membrane, its contents and every vacuole, and with an inventory of the vacuole volume a cell can make. In tube, shear and vascular flows, a cell's vacuoles met within a second, and, allowed to fuse, ten merged into one to five. Meeting is not what limits growth; material is. At the rate measured after splenectomy, all the vacuoles an average cell makes in its 120-day life fuse into one body 0.6 $μ$m across, the size healthy cells carry, but 16 times smaller in volume than the 1.5-$μ$m bodies of patients without a spleen. Taking vacuole size as set at formation, a population model in which vacuoles are made mainly in young cells, and far faster in a small minority that alone makes material for a large one, accounts for the published counts, sizes and age profiles and, on first-hand measurements, favours a splenic clearance that rises several-fold as cells age; letting that minority's vacuoles fuse fits nearly as well. At a model splenic slit, the cell's spare surface decided passage, and a vacuole mattered only when it led. A slit experiment would test whether brief encounters fuse vacuoles.

papers.title: Alert-List Concordance for Evaluating Imputation Strategies in ICU Sepsis Prediction
papers.abstract: Preprocessing is an under-measured reliability risk in clinical prediction: a model can keep a similar AUROC and still change who receives an alert. Imputation quality is commonly evaluated using reconstruction error or aggregate discrimination, neither of which directly measures agreement on which patients are flagged. At a matched alert rate, pipelines with similar aggregate performance can produce different patient lists. This question is especially relevant under the frequent, structured missingness of real ICU records. We therefore introduce alert-list concordance, which asks whether two pipelines identify the same high-risk patients, measured by the Jaccard similarity of their top-k% alert sets with patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals. On PhysioNet/CinC 2019 (40,336 patients, 71.9% missingness), we compare nine imputation strategies and a native-missingness baseline using a fixed XGBoost configuration, fitted and Platt-calibrated separately for each strategy. After Bonferroni correction, 22 of the 28 reconstruction-method pairs showed no statistically significant difference in patient-level AUROC, yet their alert lists overlap at Jaccard 0.518 to 0.750. Similar aggregate discrimination can therefore accompany different patient selections. ForwardFill is a separate outlier, pairing higher discrimination with the lowest overlap in the matrix, 0.40 to 0.45. The broad pattern holds within each hospital system and under six patient-level aggregation rules. At the row level, eight of ten methods fall within an AUROC range of 0.011. In this row-level pipeline, deep imputers did not outperform mean imputation on discrimination, and the sequential implementations cost 5 to 12 times mean imputation in total pipeline wall-clock time on our hardware.

papers.title: Harness-Driven Agentic Operation of Optical Pooled Screen Analysis
papers.abstract: Optical pooled screens connect genetic perturbations to changes in cell morphology and behavior, but turning the microscopy data into interpretable results takes complex, multi-day analyses. Established pipelines process this data, yet researchers still select parameters, inspect outputs, and resolve failures for each experiment. Here, we present Brieflow-auto, a pipeline-specific harness implemented as a Claude Code plugin that lets a coding large language model (LLM) operate Brieflow, an open-source end-to-end pipeline for optical pooled screening data. A researcher supplies experimental facts and approves the launch. An agent tunes parameters in an interactive notebook, and the harness validates the configuration, monitors execution, recovers from common failures, and checks output quality. For pipeline defects, the agent opens upstream issues proposing backward-compatible fixes for the broader community. In five previously analyzed screens, harness runs yielded more cells with a confident single-gene assignment than the original hand analyses. On a screen the pipeline was not designed for, the harness turned each failure into a reviewed upstream fix. More broadly, we propose that wrapping an established pipeline in a harness can substantially accelerate its use and the long-term reliability of its codebase.

papers.title: Learning the Shared Latent Structure of Cryo-EM Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Understanding biomolecular function requires characterizing three-dimensional structure and conformational variability, for which cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is a powerful tool. Cryo-EM produces noisy two-dimensional particle images in which molecular structure, particle pose, and imaging conditions are jointly encoded. Recovering biological information from these observations spans inverse problems including pose estimation, heterogeneity analysis, and reconstruction. These tasks are usually addressed independently despite shared protein structure and image formation, motivating a common representation across inverse problems. Since biologically meaningful differences may be spatially localized, we study self-distillation with complementary global and masked patch objectives. Because experimental dataset discrimination can reflect acquisition-specific cues, we develop controlled synthetic and experimental evaluations and find that structural discrimination benefits from dense spatial features. We introduce the EMber family of vision transformers, pre-trained on >50 million experimental particle images from 214 EMPIAR datasets together with simulated projections from 268,000 molecular assemblies. EMber improves upon existing methods at conformational and compositional discrimination by 14.85 and 14.26 percentage points, estimates conformational populations to within 1.59pp error with a linear probe, and produces particle assignments yielding reference-quality reconstructions in fewer epochs. We demonstrate how to learn representations that capture biological information for use across multiple cryo-EM inverse problems.

papers.title: SALE: Source-Aware Dynamic Pricing with Strategic Buyers
papers.abstract: In modern commerce, firms and platforms typically use customer features from different sources to personalize prices: some features are verified using seller records or third-party data, while others are self-reported and may be strategically manipulated by buyers seeking lower prices. In this paper, we study the problem of source-aware dynamic pricing with strategic buyers, where the buyer's valuation is a sparse linear function of her high-dimensional features plus market noise with an unknown distribution. We develop the Source-Aware Localized exploration and calibrated Exploitation (SALE) policy, which personalizes exploration using past learning and verified features, and corrects for strategic manipulation using verified and reported features during exploitation. Our novel personalized design aims to narrow the range of prices explored, reducing unnecessary exploration at excessively high or low prices. To support learning under this design, we derive a new population equation that enables sparse valuation parameter estimation and, in turn, nonparametric estimation of the unknown noise distribution, even when buyer features are dependent over time. By uncovering the intrinsic sparse structure, our analysis establishes estimation guarantees for both learning tasks using the same exploration data. With these guarantees, we show that SALE achieves a sublinear expected regret bound, explicitly quantifying the benefit of using verified features to narrow exploration intervals. Several numerical studies further demonstrate the appealing performance of SALE.

papers.title: Attraction from repulsion in an interacting Chern band: chiral superconductivity, generalized Hall crystals, and competing fractional Chern insulators
papers.abstract: Experiments realizing strong interactions in partially filled Chern bands have observed fractional Chern insulators (FCIs), superconductors, and topological crystals in close proximity. Yet the microscopic relation between them remains poorly understood. Here, we use tensor network simulations to study repulsively interacting spinless fermions in a tunable topological band of the checkerboard lattice. We characterize the competing phases and identify key features of the experimental phenomenology. FCIs from the Jain sequence transition into chiral p-wave superconductivity both below and above half filling as the band dispersion is enhanced. By contrast, at half filling, a generalized Hall crystal with quantized Hall conductance and a doubled unit cell forms for sufficiently strong coupling. Surprisingly, a weak-coupling approach starting from a metallic parent state captures the nature of both ordered phases at intermediate coupling. We find that fluctuations in the metal generate longer-range attraction, which we analyze within the random-phase approximation. This approach captures the pairing symmetry as well as the radial form factors of the Cooper pairs, and incorporating this attraction into Hartree-Fock selects the observed Hall crystal. Together, these results identify fluctuation-induced attraction from repulsion as a common microscopic ingredient of ordering, while our tensor network computations establish the direct competition of both phases with FCIs.

papers.title: Band-Resolved Superconducting Gaps via the Thermal Hall Effect in CeRu2
papers.abstract: Standard bulk probes of multiband superconductors cannot assign pairing gaps to specific electron or hole Fermi surfaces. Here we show that thermal Hall transport ($κ_{xy}$), constrained by specific heat and normal-state magnetotransport, resolves this ambiguity in the compensated heavy-fermion superconductor CeRu$_2$. Fixing the gap magnitudes ($Δ_e/k_B\approx 13$K, $Δ_h/k_B\approx 8$K) and band mobilities completely determines the electronic degrees of freedom in $κ_{xx}$ and $κ_{xy}$. A low-field sign reversal in $κ_{xy}$ places the larger gap on the heavy Ce $4f$ electron sheets and the smaller on the hole sheets.

papers.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
papers.abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to about 50mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.

papers.title: The Information Bottleneck and the Privacy Funnel are NP-hard
papers.abstract: Given a joint distribution $P_{XY}$ of random variables $X,Y$ on finite alphabets, the information bottleneck method seeks a representation $T$ of $X$ that is as informative as possible about $Y$ while compressing $X$; the privacy funnel asks for a representation that discloses much about $X$ while leaking little about $Y$. In both scenarios $T$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given $X$. We show that computing the optimal value $\operatorname{IB}(P_{XY},R) = \sup_T \{ I(Y;T) : I(X;T) \le R \}$ of the information bottleneck problem, as well as its Lagrangian relaxation $L_β(P_{XY}) = \sup_T [ I(Y;T) - βI(X;T) ]$, is NP-hard. Moreover, unless $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$, neither $\operatorname{IB}(P_{XY},R)$ nor $L_β(P_{XY})$ can be approximated in polynomial time within an additive error of order $|\mathcal{X}|^{-(1+α)}$, for every fixed $α> 0$. We also prove that computing the privacy funnel $\operatorname{PF}(P_{XY},r) = \inf_T \{ I(Y;T) : I(X;T) \ge r \}$ and its Lagrangian relaxation $Λ_β(P_{XY}) = \inf_T [ I(Y;T) - βI(X;T) ]$ is NP-hard, and that, unless $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$, neither can be approximated in polynomial time within an additive error of order $|\mathcal{X}|^{-2}$.

papers.title: Constrained dissipation and the lifetime of quantum many-body scars
papers.abstract: We investigate the fate of quantum many-body scars in the PXP model subject to Markovian dissipation. We show that when local jump operators respect the same symmetries of the Hamiltonian the full Liouvillian spectrum displays a tower of states with properties analogous to standard quantum scars: large overlaps with Néel states and equally spaced gaps in the imaginary part of the eigenvalues, set by a single frequency. Whether the long-time dynamics is dominated by scars is determined by the real parts of the eigenvalues, which are set by the ratio between the two relaxation rates $γ_{\pm}$ describing spin flips down-to-up or up-to-down respectively. For asymmetric dissipation ($γ_+ > γ_-$) the scarred eigenvalues have the smallest real parts: the resulting enhanced fidelity oscillations are further stabilized by staggered jump operators. In contrast, replacing the full projection operator in the dissipators with a partial one breaks the symmetries of the problem and is seen to destroy dissipative scars altogether.

papers.title: $d$-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$
papers.abstract: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave state is energetically favored, while extended-$s$-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below $T_c$, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows $1/T_1T\propto T^2$, together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust $d$-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO$_{2}$, while trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{8}$ at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between $d$-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.

papers.title: Mutual Information in High-Dimensional Neural Coding
papers.abstract: Estimating mutual information in large neural populations is limited by the exponential growth of possible neural response patterns. Here we apply a Monte Carlo framework to make this problem tractable by sampling from a conditionally independent population model fit from single-neuron responses. The estimator accurately recovers analytical ground truth, corrects finite-data bias, and scales to empirical recordings containing 100 to 10,000 neurons from visual cortex, hippocampus, and retina. Across systems, stimulus uncertainty decays exponentially with population size, revealing a simple scaling law for high-dimensional neural codes.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
papers.abstract: This is the third paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. Here we study simplicity through two countable structures with simple unstable theories: the Rado graph, and the symplectic space of labels of Pauli strings of finite support, in which addition records the products of the strings and the symplectic form records their commutation. In the second structure, forking characterizes the logical errors of stabilizer codes: an error undetectable by the checks of a code is logical exactly when its type over the stabilizer labels and a complete set of logical-operator labels forks over the stabilizer labels, and the independence theorem becomes a rule for gluing syndromes. A two-valued relation between countable sets of labels defines a diagonal bipartite observable, whose real-valued theory describes Alice's probability mixtures of labels and their expected responses at Bob's probes. Mixing changes the classification: if the relation has the independence property, this theory has the tree property of the second kind. For the observable of the symplectic form, actual mixtures of checks witness this property for the response itself; for the observable of the Rado graph, every array that witnesses it for a quantifier-free formula in Bob's probe contains idealized preparations, which lie outside the original structure.

papers.title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
papers.abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill makes mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, but what it damages has not been measured. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions in four MoE families on short-answer question answering. At half the experts the F1 loss is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but no longer answers briefly. The loss is made at a few tokens: the two chat-template tokens before the answer in Qwen3-30B-A3B, and the first 8-32 tokens, where the instruction sits, in DeepSeek-V2-Lite. Keeping them at full experts removes most of the F1 loss and about half and a fifth of the increase in answer NLL. Reduction changes the first-token sink statistics by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most a quarter of the loss. We then test placement on real prompts with about 4% of tokens at full experts. Putting them on the task interface keeps F1 within one point of the unmodified model, while the same budget scattered in the documents is about 3 points worse in both prespecified primary tests of this comparison. Time to first token falls about 14% on 11K-token prompts.

papers.title: Causal Integrated Gradients: Scalable Feature Attribution Along Causal Paths
papers.abstract: Existing feature attribution methods that account for feature dependencies do not scale to high dimensions. We propose causal integrated gradients (CIG) and causal expected gradients (CEG), which extend integrated gradients to incorporate prior causal structure among input features while retaining its computational efficiency and, under conditions on the causal graph, its axiomatic guarantees. In many settings, some causal structure between features is already known, for example, that a transcription factor causally regulates a target gene's expression. Yet existing gradient-based methods cannot exploit this structure, instead crediting a feature's downstream effects over its true upstream cause, such as ranking the target gene above the transcription factor that regulates it. Our key idea is to embed this causal structure by routing the integration path along the causal graph. The method thereby decomposes each feature's attribution into a direct effect and effects mediated through its causal descendants. We evaluate CIG in three settings of increasing realism. First, on a synthetic benchmark with a known causal model, CIG's attributions best match the ground-truth causal effect from Pearl's do-calculus, matching the accuracy of causal Shapley values at a fraction of the computational cost. Second, on simulated single-cell gene expression data with a known gene regulatory network (Dyngen), CIG most accurately recovers the transcription factors driving the simulation. Third, on real interferon-$β$ stimulation data, where only an approximate causal graph is available, CIG better prioritizes the transcription factors driving the measured response than DeepSHAP and integrated gradients. Together, these results show that incorporating causal structure into gradient-based attributions recovers upstream drivers that existing methods miss, without sacrificing scalability.

papers.title: Documenting Trofinetide Treatment Phenotypes in Rett Syndrome with a Dual-LLM Consensus Pipeline
papers.abstract: Objective: Trofinetide, approved in 2023 as the first Rett syndrome treatment, lacks scalable real-world monitoring because chart review is labor-intensive. We developed a dual large language model (LLM) consensus pipeline to extract 18 treatment-response phenotypes, comprising 4 adverse effects, 13 Rett clinical features, and medication refusal, from clinical notes. Materials and Methods: We analyzed 26,763 notes from 108 patients with confirmed sustained trofinetide exposure at Texas Children's Hospital. The pipeline filters notes by keyword, classifies each through two LLMs requiring consensus, and aggregates a patient-by-timepoint matrix. Architecture and prompt were selected on a diarrhea development set, then frozen and applied to the other 17 phenotypes with the phenotype definition substituted, as an out-of-sample test. The reported prompt comparison scores 183 expert-labeled cells. Results: A prompt requiring diarrhea to be active and severe performed best (84.2 $\pm$ 0.0% accuracy; F1 = 0.674), 47 percentage points above regular-expression matching ($p < 0.0001$). Expert reviewers judged six of the pipeline's calls per phenotype, three positive and three negative, and agreed with 90.2% (92/102). The 13 Rett clinical features are manifestations of the disorder itself rather than adverse effects of trofinetide. Gross and fine motor impairment, language/communication, and stereotypy were documented present in 92-100% of patients at every visit. Discussion: In-context LLM extraction captured multi-domain treatment responses. The outcome is documented presence at each visit, not a direction-of-change judgment. Conclusion: Coupling in-context LLM reasoning with a consensus architecture offers a scalable alternative to keyword and regular-expression extraction for real-world evidence, adapting to new phenotypes and medications through configuration alone.

papers.title: Exciton superfluidity in two-dimensional bilayers at zero and high magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We study interlayer exciton superfluidity versus layer separation in two-dimensional electron-hole bilayers at zero magnetic field and quantum Hall bilayers at total filling $ν_T=1$. Unscreened Hartree-Fock theory predicts coherence at every finite separation, with an energy scale decaying inversely with separation at large distances. We examine how screening, correlations, and spatial instabilities modify this prediction. At zero field, we solve the linearized gap equation with the full momentum and frequency dependence of the interaction screened within the random-phase approximation, without an imposed cutoff. The apparent plasmon enhancement of pairing in the ladder approximation is largely cancelled by the second-order crossed-rung correction. Static screening determines the leading pairing exponent in the controlled high-density limit at fixed separation. At large separation, the pairing scale falls exponentially with squared separation while the instability persists. Extending this result to fixed density assumes Fermi-liquid layers and higher-order dynamical corrections subleading to the static pairing interaction. At high field, we obtain an analytic uniform Hartree-Fock saddle point in the lowest Landau level, coherent at every finite separation. Within Hartree-Fock theory, its finite-wave-vector collective-mode instability favors an excitonic supersolid, distinguishing loss of spatial uniformity from loss of coherence. We conjecture that the quantum Hall bilayer evolves continuously toward weak pairing of composite fermions, with a scale far below the mean-field prediction at large separation. This suppression could produce an apparent critical separation at finite temperature without a ground-state quantum phase transition. The comparison separates the existence, energy scale, and spatial stability of interlayer coherence.

papers.title: A general feedback mechanism unifying stochasticity, long transients, and resilience
papers.abstract: Stochasticity in complex systems is commonly treated either as external noise added to deterministic dynamics or as an effective stochastic description of deterministic chaos. A framework in which stochastic dynamics arise endogenously from deterministic chaos and subsequently feed back on the deterministic dynamics, thereby fundamentally reshaping system dynamics, remains rare. Here, we develop such a framework. Through the interaction between deterministic and stochastic dynamics, alternative stable states, critical transitions, adaptive capacity, stochasticity, and resilience become dynamically interconnected within a single model. Furthermore, the framework establishes a new mechanism of long transients, driven by two key factors: (i) time-scale separation and (ii) time-delay-induced cancellation. Stochasticity plays a dual stabilizing-destabilizing role in long transients: it promotes their persistence while also facilitating their eventual escape and collapse. This dual role allows resilience to be quantified dynamically through escape and stochastic recapture dynamics. Finally, we establish the generality of the mechanism mathematically and numerically across a broad class of one-dimensional nonlinear systems, suggesting that it reflects a general dynamical principle.

papers.title: How language model agents reshape price competition
papers.abstract: Repeated Bertrand competition is a stringent benchmark for algorithmic pricing: in homogeneous-goods markets, standard learning procedures typically select the stage-game Nash outcome with prices near marginal cost. We show that LLM pricing agents can escape this benchmark, depending on deployment decisions. LLMs outperform standard online learners through faster adaptation, but this advantage largely disappears against full-information learners. An extracted surrogate algorithm illustrates how LLMs in specific deployments profit from regularly undercutting slower learners. Agents that post one price every period from raw market histories that include rival prices can sustain supracompetitive regimes in self-play. Agents that periodically emit probability distributions from summarized histories of their own profits instead move toward the competitive region in self-play. Markets mixing these interfaces can generate dynamic regimes in which LLMs establish a high-price anchor and regularly undercut it to capture demand. These regimes can keep both competitors' prices above marginal cost. Deployment choices shape these outcomes, shifting the focus from stationary equilibria to dynamic pricing regimes.

papers.title: X-Fly: Learning to Reach and Stop in Full-Chunk Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Aerial vision-language navigation (VLN) agents built on large vision-language models are expensive to query. Executing a complete predicted action chunk before replanning amortizes this cost, reducing model inference from 195 to 42 ms per executed waypoint for our policy. It also moves the states at which the policy is queried away from expert demonstrations, which supervise neither recovery from these states nor termination at the learner's own arrival. On OpenFly test-seen, no-stop failures account for 47.78% of full-chunk behavior cloning (BC) outcomes. We present X-Fly, a staged training framework for full-chunk aerial VLN. Recovery DAgger labels learner-visited decision states with smooth chunks that reconnect to future expert segments and with STOP at the first in-region state. Flow-GRPO then jointly refines the chunked flow controller and a Bernoulli STOP policy from same-task closed-loop outcomes, supplemented by outcome-verified stopping supervision. With eight controls per decision, X-Fly reaches 74.18% SR on test-seen and 51.73% on test-unseen, compared with 16.45% and 18.43% for full-chunk BC and 32.04% and 29.46% for DreamFly.

papers.title: Pairing-channel reconstruction by Ising spin-orbit coupling in a multiorbital triangular-lattice model
papers.abstract: Ising spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is widely known for locking electronic spins and protecting superconductivity against in-plane paramagnetic pair breaking. Here we show that, in a correlated multiorbital system, Ising SOC can play a qualitatively different role: it reconstructs the hierarchy of spin-fluctuation-mediated pairing channels by reshaping the low-energy Fermi surfaces, orbital-spin coherence factors, and momentum-resolved scattering phase space. We study a noncentrosymmetric two-orbital triangular-lattice model with Rashba SOC, Ising SOC, and onsite SOC. We solve the pairing problem within a multiorbital random-phase-approximation framework. In the single-orbital limit, an $E$-representation state with a dominant $S_z=0$ component emerges only at relatively strong Ising SOC. Orbital degrees of freedom facilitate the stabilization of this pairing state at a smaller nominal Ising SOC strength and generate a broad competition between $E$ and $A_1$ pairing channels. The $E$ state can maintain the same $S_z=0$ triplet character, whereas the $A_1$ state becomes a fully gapped sign-changing $\splusminus$ superconductor. The latter also realizes a topologically nontrivial phase in the time-reversal-invariant weak-pairing regime, with a nonzero $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index, Wilson-loop spectral flow, and boundary modes. Its topology is not carried by a single orbital pairing component, but emerges cooperatively from the dominant intra- and inter-orbital pairing components. These results establish a microscopic route by which Ising SOC and orbital hybridization can reconstruct interaction-driven superconductivity, producing both Ising-triplet and topological singlet-dominated phases in correlated non-centrosymmetric systems.

papers.title: Unique Charge-density-wave Order and Fluctuation-induced Phonon Softening in the Optimally-doped Trilayer Cuprate Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{10+δ}$
papers.abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) order is a ubiquitous feature of cuprate superconductors that competes with superconductivity. However, its behavior remains poorly understood in trilayer compounds, which contain the optimal number of CuO$_2$ layers for superconductivity. Here, we report Cu $L_3$- and O $K$-edge resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements of optimally-doped Bi$_{2}$Sr$_{2}$Ca$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{10+δ}$ (Bi2223), the trilayer cuprate with the highest superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) among Bi-based cuprates. We observe CDW order with a single in-plane wavevector of ${\bm q}_{\text{CDW}} = (0.25, 0)$, demonstrating that a coherent CDW order is formed across the trilayers. We also resolve CDW fluctuations emanating from the static order, whose profiles differ between the Cu $L_3$ and O $K$ edges. The phonon softening occurs where these CDW fluctuations interact with the phonon branch, indicating that the RIXS phonon anomaly is driven by the coupling between CDW fluctuations and the phonon branch.

papers.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: For a one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operator with bounded nonconstant iid potential, we prove a unit-intensity Poisson limit for local eigenvalues unfolded by the integrated density of states. The limit holds at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. In particular, it holds for Bernoulli potentials at every fixed nonzero coupling. The proof uses auxiliary phase functions built from inverse stationary measures to obtain an exact IDS drift. Projective contraction then yields exponential crossing times, and a spatial subdivision argument gives independent Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows. At energies where the IDS has a finite positive derivative, the usual linear rescaling gives the same limit.

papers.title: Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demand efficient inference, where the multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations in linear projections dominate compute and energy cost. Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces this cost by mapping weights and activations to low-bit integers. Power-of-Two (PoT) weight quantization promises efficient multiplier-free LLM inference via shift-add logic, but suffers significant accuracy degradation at low bit-widths due to its coarse base-2 quantization grid. We introduce Fractional PoT (FPoT), a base-$\sqrt{2}$ (half-octave) fractional PoT grid that achieves practical 4-bit weight quantization while preserving a fully integer shift-add datapath. The method combines (i) the base-$\sqrt{2}$ weight grid with uniform integer activations, (ii) a calibration-time grid-alignment refinement absorbed into the static per-channel scale, and (iii) a lightweight 1-adder $\sqrt{2}$ approximation whose error is absorbed during weight calibration via approximate-grid quantization, yielding a processing element (PE) with significantly fewer gates than a 4-bit integer multiplier. On Llama-3-8B with 4-bit weight and activation quantization, FPoT improves zero-shot commonsense reasoning performance by 8.72% relative to the PoT baseline, while maintaining performance close to the uniform integer baseline, with only a negligible 0.4%p degradation. These results hold across various configurations spanning seven models and three bit-widths. Furthermore, FPoT can be integrated with state-of-the-art LLM PTQ methods, demonstrating framework-agnostic applicability.

papers.title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
papers.abstract: Protein foundation models increasingly support the generation of novel biological sequences, yet their reliance on large public datasets creates opportunities for adversarial manipulation of the material they learn from and retrieve. We investigate two data-only poisoning attacks against protein design systems, targeting the pre-training corpus of autoregressive protein language models and the retrieval corpus of a text-guided protein generator. For the first, we pre-trained ProtGPT2 and ProGen2 variants of 300 million parameters, introducing poisoned protein sequences containing one of two triggers followed by one of three payloads. Across all poisoned runs, both architectures acquired highly reliable trigger-dependent generation under uniform and ramped poisoning schedules. Under ramped exposure, the earliest majority activation occurred after only 200 contaminated examples, while for the uniform schedule earliest activation occurred around 5000 poisoned samples. For the second attack, we inserted records into a retrieval corpus system without modifying its weights or decoding procedure. A single query-aware record captured a top-16 retrieval position for 58\% of templated requests and 97\% of free-text requests. Conditional on successful poisoned retrieval, 62\% of requests produced altered sequences, while 19-21% acquired the inserted domain by profile-HMM homology. A universal query-unaware attack using 1,500 records also achieved substantial retrieval capture and domain transfer. Together, these findings demonstrate that adversarial protein sequence contributions can establish persistent, sequence-specific behaviour during pre-training or redirect protein generation at inference, while leaving ordinary model behaviour largely preserved. Our work establishes the integrity and biological provenance of protein sequence data as critical safeguards for generative protein design systems.

papers.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of Kähler geometry: the classical Kähler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Ampère energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics.

papers.title: Causal-horizon scaling of prompt X(3872) formation lengths
papers.abstract: A causal-horizon ensemble relates changes in prompt production to spatial correlations involved in forming $\X$. Each horizon represents the spatial coherence range of an early-field pulse. For weak phase fluctuations and overlap widths small compared with the mean horizon, ensemble averaging makes the fractional loss of formation probability proportional to the Gaussian source-state overlap width. Extending this dependence as an effective law at finite attenuation, we compare three states to eliminate the common field coefficient. A common-slope fit to matched LHCb prompt $\X/\Ps$ and $\Ps/\Jp$ ratios at 13 TeV gives conditional formation scales. With a common Gaussian source, common field coupling, fixed relative production baselines and a direct-$\Jp$ reference, the central fit requires a source root-mean-square width above about 0.60 fm and an $\X$ effective Gaussian RMS separation of at least about 1.25 fm. The same assumptions require at least a factor of about 4.5 increase in the $\X$ formation probability relative to its no-field value between 4--6 and 12--14 GeV/$c$ in $2<y<3$. Calculations with finite feed-down and a nodal reference assess the length calibration. A matched three-state activity measurement tests the same spatial slope without an additional activity-dependent parameter.

papers.title: Strain-enhanced superconductivity in RuO$_2$ thin films: Joint experimental and theoretical studies
papers.abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of RuO$_2$ films grown on TiO$_2$ substrates by combining film fabrication and transport measurement with \textit{ab initio} calculation. Experimentally, we grow several RuO$_2$ (110) thin films on TiO$_2$ (110) substrates and observe superconductivity with critical temperature ($T_c$) of $\sim$2.0 K in 20-nm and 30-nm RuO$_2$ (110) thin films. Theoretically, we study the superconductivity in both RuO$_2$ (110) and RuO$_2$ (100) epitaxial films within McMillan formalism of isotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Among the salient results, the calculated phonon dispersion relations of all the considered RuO$_2$ films show that the epitaxial films are dynamically stable. Importantly, our \textit{ab initio} calculations reveal that independent of the film orientation, the [001] compressive strain $ε_{[001]}$ pushes the flat Ru $d_{z^2}$-dominant bands towards the Fermi level ($E_F$), and significantly soften the out-of-plane acoustic phonon mode near the R point in the Brillouin zone, which substantially enhances the electron-phonon coupling (EPC) strength $λ$ and hence the calculated $T_c$ in the RuO$_2$ films. Remarkably, the amount of the phonon softening and the enhanced $T_c$ increase almost linearly with the increasing $ε_{[001]}$. The calculated $T_c$ for the films with thickness of $\geq$ 20 nm agree well with the experimental $T_c$. These findings demonstrate that among other things, lattice mismatch strain provides an effective route for tuning phonon-mediated superconductivity in RuO$_2$ and other thin films.

papers.title: OmicsBench: a long-horizon multi-turn benchmark of AI agents on research-study-scale bioinformatics
papers.abstract: Computational biologists increasingly delegate substantial analyses to AI agents in long-horizon, multi-turn sessions, yet most benchmarks of agents' bioinformatics capabilities pose a single short task with a single-shot prompt. We present OmicsBench, a long-horizon, multi-turn bioinformatics benchmark for AI agents. Each of its 97 tasks links dependent subtasks into a directed acyclic graph, for 662 underlying subtasks in all. Each subtask is posed as one user turn and graded deterministically against an answer key, with optional in-context feedback on incorrect answers. Across 12 models on three harnesses, the slowest agent averages 3.6 hours per task, and no combination comes near saturating the benchmark, with mean scores of 0.43 to 0.57 out of a possible 1 without in-context feedback and 0.54 to 0.67 with it. Multi-turn evaluation also uncovers behavior that single-shot prompts cannot, as agents score lower on subtasks that depend on earlier subtasks, and in-context feedback helps agents recover some of that loss. Because deterministic scoring gives no qualitative account of how an agent failed, we also introduce an unsupervised failure mode discovery pipeline that describes, embeds, and clusters agents' failed attempts to surface emergent failure modes. Applied to OmicsBench, this pipeline exposes qualitative shortcomings in how agents carry out bioinformatics analyses, ranging from agents applying their own statistical filters in place of the specified ones to agents writing whole answers from memory.

papers.title: Can Autonomous Vehicles Keep Their Cool? A Survey of Thermal Side-Channel and Perception Attacks
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) couple safety-critical perception to thermally constrained compute. Physical adversaries can spoof thermal infrared (IR) sensors used for night driving, while unprivileged software co-tenants can fingerprint perception workloads from thermal, dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS), and thermal event interrupt (TEI) telemetry required for package safety. These paths differ in mechanism and privilege, but both exploit interfaces that AV stacks cannot disable without compromising Safety of the Intended Functionality (SOTIF). Existing microarchitectural and CPS surveys cover cache timing, adversarial ML, and camera or LiDAR spoofing; none frames physical thermal IR attacks and unprivileged silicon thermal telemetry as one residual-risk class. This survey systematizes thirteen works into thermal perception integrity, telemetry leakage, and model-information extraction, comparing them by privilege, timescale, co-tenancy, deployability, and AV relevance while mapping defenses to residual risk. A commodity proxy supports the software co-tenant branch only; physical IR evidence comes from cited literature. We identify open problems in on-target automotive evaluation, fusion trust under IR spoofing, chiplet thermal coupling, capability-based telemetry, and standards-ready threat analysis, motivating co-design across sensors, operating systems, silicon, and automotive standards.

papers.title: Separating mixtures of single-fiber orientation distributions for increased sensitivity to crossing white matter fibers
papers.abstract: Intro: Diffusion MRI allows for in vivo probing of brain tissue architecture via micron-level diffusion aggregated at the millimeter scale, but crossing white matter fibers decrease the sensitivity of downstream tasks such as microstructural modeling and tractography. Current fixel-based methods for identifying the number, orientation, and spread of fibers rely on finding the peaks of fiber orientation distributions from constrained spherical deconvolution. However, this method is biased by the spreads of nearby fibers and fails at angular separations lower than approximately 40-50 degrees. Methods: In this work, we perform a constrained nonlinear optimization called fiber segmentation by signal splitting and iterative least squares estimation (FISSILE), modeling each voxel as a mixture of single-fiber distributions. We use FISSILE to fit axially symmetric fibers in simulations and on three in vivo human subjects from the Human Connectome Project, an ex vivo raccoon brain, as well as the same human subject scanned twice at two different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). Results: On simulated data, FISSILE successfully identifies fibers at an angular separation of 40° and a volume fraction of 0.1 at an SNR as low as 30, while MRtrix3's fod2fixel is limited to 60° separation and 0.1 volume fraction at the same SNR. On acquired data, FISSILE identified 85.8% of white matter voxels on average in human brains and 79.4% in the raccoon with at least one fiber crossing, whereas fod2fixel identified 30.1% and 44.5%. The number of white matter fiber crossings was mildly sensitive to different noise levels in the human subject with two acquisitions. Conclusion: A method that models the crossing fiber phenomenon as an unmixing problem increases sensitivity to individual fibers for more precise characterization of anatomy.

papers.title: How large an effect would we have seen? Positive controls, detection floors and dataset pitfalls in scalp-EEG speech decoding
papers.abstract: Objective. Studies that decode imagined speech from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) commonly validate their pipelines with a positive control, usually overt speech, and report null results without stating what effect size the pipeline could have detected. Approach. Using ds003626 ("Thinking out loud"), KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, we audited decoding of overt speech, articulator preparation and imagined speech with artifact-channel subsets, band-limited decoding and trial selection, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion. We injected class-dependent effects of known amplitude into the real recordings to measure the detection floor of five decoder families, and we checked the ds003626 labels against the dataset's acquisition protocol. Main results. On ds003626, two lip electrodes decoded overt speech at 0.7430 and the eight external channels at 0.7068, against 0.4231 for the 128-channel scalp montage, and no decodable signal survived in the 8-30 Hz band. On the other two corpora, within-subject accuracy rose monotonically with frequency into the range dominated by muscle activity. Band-power logistic regression detected an injected 8-30 Hz desynchronization of 0.54 uV under a criterion fixed in advance, whereas a compact convolutional network (EEGNet) detected nothing within subject up to 4.31 uV. In ds003626, the condition codes are the reverse of the intuitive reading, the class encoding changed between public releases, and condition is a deterministic function of time within each session. Significance. In these corpora the overt-speech positive control is dominated by myogenic signal and cannot validate a decoding pipeline. We recommend that speech-decoding studies report band-limited and artifact-channel accuracy, the direction of accuracy across frequency, and a measured detection floor.

papers.title: napari-TurboBox: Interactive Multi-Viewer Bounding Box Annotation for AI-Guided Volumetric Bioimaging
papers.abstract: Promptable segmentation models turn one 3D bounding box into an instance mask. Box placement therefore limits how fast microscopy volumes with thousands of objects are annotated. Each box must be checked in several synchronized viewers, but napari-bbox shares no state between viewers. An edit must update every viewer and slows down with more boxes. napari-TurboBox instead holds one shared copy of the boxes for all viewers. In a four-viewer layout, napari-TurboBox needs a few milliseconds per mouse move to update the three slice viewers up to $10^4$ boxes. The same update in napari-bbox leaves the 33 ms budget beyond about $10^3$ boxes and takes 159 ms at $10^4$. Boxes stay axis-aligned and export to COCO and YOLO as per-slice 2D boxes. napari-TurboBox is a pure-Python plugin for napari 0.6.6 to 0.9. The code is available at https://github.com/N-Friederich/napari-turbobox under the Apache 2.0 licence, and version 0.1.0 is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23090828 on Zenodo.

papers.title: Automating Observable Closure Analysis for Graph Transformation Models with MolFoundry
papers.abstract: Graph transformations model changing systems, with applications in software, biology and chemistry, among others. We introduce MolFoundry, a graph transformation framework, and present a workflow for observable analysis that tracks the dynamics of local patterns through rule composition. Analysing rule compositions avoids the need to enumerate a potentially infinite state space. Building on rule-algebraic stochastic rewriting, MolFoundry's kernel composes rules with nested application conditions, including missing-edge constraints. Given rules, rates and query patterns, the algorithms iteratively identify auxiliary pattern counts and search for closure. Using exact counting identities supplied by graph-family backends, successful searches yield closed ordinary differential equations for average counts or, with justified individual jumps, finite event models describing joint changes and rates. We evaluate conditional composition and automated discovery of auxiliary observables against published calculations and independent rule application. Applications to aldol addition, copolymerization and chlorination show how the framework yields quantitative predictions directly from molecular graph rules.

papers.title: Platelet-driven contraction enlarges accessible space in layered fibrin networks without uniformly accelerating particle escape
papers.abstract: Platelet traction contracts fibrin networks, yet whether contraction promotes or hinders the escape of suspended particles is unclear. We coupled an overdamped Langevin model of platelet--fibrin mechanics to Brownian transport of finite-size tracers through frozen network states. Nine mechanical replicas were evolved at four filopodial traction baselines (0--8.8\,nN), stacked into 5-$μ$m-thick domains of 50 layers and probed at 0--15\,s with 0.5-$μ$m tracers (29,952 trajectories, 100\,s observation). Benchmarked against experimental clot-contraction kinetics, the simulated contraction is post-lag, within one order of magnitude of experimental rates and corresponds to the onset of the contraction phase. Relative to the matched zero-baseline control, every active-baseline state showed greater projected contraction and a larger tracer-accessible volume ($+9.3\%$ to $+27.6\%$; exact sign test $p=0.0039$ per condition). At 15\,s, mean survival at 100\,s fell from 27.3\% to 14.3\% and the restricted mean exit time from 56.5 to 44.0\,s between the lowest and highest baseline, and all nine replicas shortened residence at 8.8\,nN. At lower baselines, responses differed among replicas, and nearly all retained tracers with a classified start were connected to an exit. Contraction therefore enlarges accessible space without uniformly accelerating escape, separating geometric accommodation from transport kinetics.

papers.title: Nodal nematic superconductivity in moiré graphene
papers.abstract: Unconventional superconductivity can emerge in various forms in strongly correlated systems. Historically, the most extensively studied examples include nodal and triplet pairing, which were experimentally detected in cuprates and superfluid helium-3, respectively. Beyond these canonical cases, there are also nematic superconductors, in which the rotational symmetry of the lattice is broken in the superconducting state. While there are several examples of nematic superconductors whose pairing emerges inside a preexisting nematic normal state, experimental evidence for superconducting states that intrinsically break rotational symmetry on their own has been exceedingly scarce. Here, we report the experimental realization and identification of an intrinsic multi-component nodal nematic superconducting state in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene (MATTG). By integrating tunneling spectroscopy with quantum transport measurements, we directly probe the symmetry of low-energy superconducting quasiparticles. Deep inside the superconducting state, we observe a pronounced two-fold anisotropy in the zero-bias tunneling conductance under an in-plane magnetic field, which is strongly suppressed together with superconductivity as the temperature or perpendicular magnetic field is increased. Remarkably, the major axis of anisotropy rotates by up to $90^{\circ}$ across the superconducting dome, indicating an intrinsic, field- and density-tunable symmetry of the low-energy excitations. These behaviors imply a nodal superconducting state in MATTG that spontaneously breaks the six-fold rotational symmetry of the moiré superlattice. Our results establish moiré graphene as a versatile platform for realizing and interrogating nodal nematic superconductivity, opening a new avenue for exploring unconventional symmetry-breaking superconducting states in two-dimensional materials.

papers.title: Magnetic Susceptibility of Superconducting Films in the Meissner-London Regime
papers.abstract: Extracting the London penetration depth, $λ(T)$, from the measured magnetic susceptibility, $χ(T)$, of a superconducting platelet in a perpendicular magnetic field requires knowing the function $χ(λ)$ computed for the actual sample geometry. Thin films are increasingly important in quantum computing and superconducting electronics, most of which operate at ultra-low excitation fields in the vortex-free regime. Understanding their electromagnetic response in the Meissner--London (finite-$λ$, no vortices) state is therefore essential for extracting intrinsic properties such as the London penetration depth and superfluid phase stiffness. While numerous prior works have addressed different aspects of this problem, here we focus on providing an analytical semi-empirical representation of $χ(λ)$ based on the 2D sheet-current model and establishing the limits of its applicability using two independent full 3D numerical solutions: finite-element modeling and a volume-current integral equation. As a result, we provide $χ(λ)$ for a disc of radius $a$ and thickness $d$ in closed form, valid for all $λ$ and for aspect ratios $δ\equiv d/(2a)\le0.05$, and accurate to $0.1\%$. The two-dimensional sheet description with Pearl length $Λ=2λ^2/d$ is adequate for $δ\lesssim10^{-4}$ and $λ\gtrsim 4d$. Thicker films require the full closed form, which includes the three-dimensional corrections. Using the same numerical analysis, we provide an empirical formula that maps rectangular samples---the geometry most commonly used in experiments---onto a disc with an ``effective radius'' for subsequent calculation of $χ(λ)$, and formulate a complete calibration protocol for whole-sample susceptibility measurements.

papers.title: Universal enhancement of the pairing gap in a dilute Fermi superfluid
papers.abstract: At zero temperature, a dilute Fermi gas with an attractive contact interaction forms a superfluid with gapped fermionic excitations. We show that the gap at weak coupling can be organized as a trans-series expansion in the interaction strength and the asymptotic Gor'kov-Melik-Barkhudarov gap. Low-energy virtual quasiparticles generate corrections that are linear in the gap with a leading coefficient nearly 25$\times$ larger than the other known coefficients. This substantially increases the gap at intermediate densities, highlighting that systematic corrections are crucial for quantitative predictions.

papers.title: Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling
papers.abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers possess unique dipolar properties, providing a path for exploring correlated many-body phases, electrically tunable dipole-dipole interactions, and long-range exciton transport. However, the large electron-hole separation underlying their dipolar character also results in a significantly reduced oscillator strength, limiting their direct optical interaction with light, and thus the direct probing of their dynamics and many-body interactions. Here, we show that by using Purcell engineering of critical coupling, a weak interlayer transition can absorb as strongly as the dominant intralayer transition, despite its much smaller intrinsic oscillator strength. Using this approach, in an open cavity architecture we demonstrate an order of magnitude IX absorption modulation in bilayer and trilayer MoS2, with doubling of the IX to A-exciton interaction strength weight from ~23% to ~53%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in a tailored closed cavity architecture, the IX enhancement can reach beyond an order of magnitude, from ~5% to ~83% excitonic absorption, enabling IX absorption similar to intralayer excitons. An analytical description of the interaction is obtained via a closed-form transmission-line model which separates the excitonic and photonic contributions to the optical response, revealing how cavity architecture can be designed towards critical coupling. Our findings establish Purcell engineering of critical coupling as a general route to controlling and enhancing weak excitonic transitions.

papers.title: Geometrical and Optical Design of the GUEST Laser-Ranged Test Masses for the Detection of Gravitational Waves in the $μ$Hz range
papers.abstract: The GUEST (Gravitational Universe Exploration with Satellite Tracking) mission aims at detecting gravitational waves in the yet almost unexplored $μ$Hz frequency range through high-precision orbital tracking. The unprecedented scientific objectives of this experiment demand equally advanced optical solutions: the highly eccentric orbit imposes dual measurement regimes; a low-velocity, long-range scenario at apogee and a high-velocity, short-range scenario at perigee. The substantial disparity between these conditions is addressed through a novel optical architecture incorporating two distinct types of Corner-Cube Retroreflectors (CCRs) with 1" and 2" apertures (CCR1 and CCR2, respectively). The proposed layout has been designed to ensure isotropy and homogeneity of the optical response while maintaining efficient packing over the spherical surface of the spacecraft. The resulting Optical Cross-Section (OCS) has been evaluated using a custom reduced-order model, which captures the behavior of individual CCRs under varying illumination conditions. This model has been calibrated by reconstructing the optical response of the LARES-2 satellite and has enabled a detailed assessment of the contributions of each CCR type along the GUEST orbit. Finally, sensitivity analyses have been conducted to investigate the impact of key design parameters, including the ratio between CCR types, laser wavelength, spacecraft diameter, Dihedral Angle Offsets (DAOs), and mechanical configurations.

papers.title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
papers.abstract: Conditional generative models are increasingly used for scientific prediction beyond the direct training support. Yet scientific questions often concern whether one intervention changes the effect of another. Such interactions can be of primary interest while explaining little of the total variation, allowing models to appear accurate overall without recovering the relevant scientific effect. It remains unclear how these models learn interactions and when these successfully extrapolate to unseen conditions. We therefore study interaction recovery in flow-matching models using a physiological time-series simulator, drug dose-response data, combinatorial cell perturbations, and molecular conformer generations, where we separate recovery from hallucinated interaction structure. In the controlled setting, individual effects are learned much earlier than interactions and models hallucinate interactions where none exist.
